```python
                            continue
                        self.assertIn(rule["labels"]["severity"], ("warning", "critical"))
                        # The Grafana delivery rule selects ALERTS by network.
                        self.assertEqual(rule["labels"]["network"], network)
                        self.assertNotEqual(rule["annotations"]["summary"].strip(), "")
                        url, _, anchor = rule["annotations"]["runbook_url"].partition("#")
                        self.assertEqual(url, runbook)
                        self.assertIn(anchor, anchors)

    def test_alert_names_are_the_reviewed_set(self):
        rules = vm_rules(self.monitored)
        self.assertEqual(set(rules), {f"storage-integrity.{group}" for group in MONITORING_ALERTS})
        for group, names in MONITORING_ALERTS.items():
            with self.subTest(group=group):
                alerts = [rule["alert"] for rule in rules[f"storage-integrity.{group}"] if "alert" in rule]
                self.assertEqual(len(alerts), len(set(alerts)))
                self.assertEqual(set(alerts), names)
                for alert in alerts:
                    self.assertRegex(alert, r"^(Arbiter|SentioNode|StorageIntegrity)[A-Za-z]+$")
        records = [rule["record"] for group in rules.values() for rule in group if "record" in rule]
        self.assertEqual(records, ["arbiter:safe_watermark:max", "arbiter:pending_blocks:max", "arbiter:track_safe_block_seq:max"])
        # The delivery probe of runbook §8 is applied with kubectl, never by the chart.
        self.assertNotIn("StorageIntegrityDeliveryProbe", set().union(*MONITORING_ALERTS.values()))

    def test_state_limit_is_the_smallest_voter_budget(self):
        limit = voter_state_limit(self.monitored)
        self.assertEqual(limit, min(SNAPSHOT_DOC_READ_CAP_BYTES, quantity_bytes("2Gi") // 4, quantity_bytes("2Gi") // 4))
        self.assertEqual(limit, 536870912)
        self.assertEqual(yaml.safe_load((CHART / "values.yaml").read_text())["monitoring"]["stateLimitBytes"], limit)
        # Spec §13.1: the memory alerts read the in-memory gauge, the volume alerts
        # the snapshot document plus the Raft log.
        for alert, divisor, series in (
            ("ArbiterStateSizeHigh", 4, ("arbiter_state_bytes",)),
            ("ArbiterStateSizeCritical", 2, ("arbiter_state_bytes",)),
            ("ArbiterRaftStorageHigh", 4, ("arbiter_snapshot_doc_bytes", "arbiter_raft_log_store_bytes")),
            ("ArbiterRaftStorageCritical", 2, ("arbiter_snapshot_doc_bytes", "arbiter_raft_log_store_bytes")),
        ):
            with self.subTest(alert=alert):
                expr = alert_rule(self.monitored, alert)["expr"]
                self.assertTrue(expr.endswith(f"> {limit} / {divisor}"), expr)
                self.assertEqual(tuple(metric for metric, _ in promql_selectors(expr)), series)
        # Voters with more than 4 GiB of memory and of volume are bound by the read cap.
        large = {"storageSize": "8Gi", "resources": {"limits": {"memory": "8Gi"}}}
        docs = documents(render({"arbiter": large, "monitoring": {"enabled": True, "stateLimitBytes": SNAPSHOT_DOC_READ_CAP_BYTES}}))
        self.assertEqual(voter_state_limit(docs), SNAPSHOT_DOC_READ_CAP_BYTES)
        self.assertTrue(alert_rule(docs, "ArbiterStateSizeHigh")["expr"].endswith(f"> {SNAPSHOT_DOC_READ_CAP_BYTES} / 4"))

    def test_state_limit_must_follow_the_voter_sizing(self):
        refusal = (
            "monitoring.stateLimitBytes ({}) must equal L = min(1 GiB snapshot read cap, "
            "arbiter.resources.limits.memory / 4, arbiter.storageSize / 4) = {}: resize the voters and this value together"
        )
        for arbiter, limit in (
            ({"resources": {"limits": {"memory": "1Gi"}}}, 268435456),
            ({"storageSize": "1Gi"}, 268435456),
            ({"resources": {"limits": {"memory": "1536Mi"}}}, 402653184),
        ):
            with self.subTest(arbiter=arbiter):
                self.assert_rejected({"arbiter": arbiter, "monitoring": {"enabled": True}}, refusal.format(536870912, limit))
                docs = documents(render({"arbiter": arbiter, "monitoring": {"enabled": True, "stateLimitBytes": limit}}))
                self.assertEqual(voter_state_limit(docs), limit)
                self.assertTrue(alert_rule(docs, "ArbiterStateSizeCritical")["expr"].endswith(f"> {limit} / 2"))
                # The check belongs to monitoring: without it the voters render at any valid size.
                self.assertEqual(voter_state_limit(documents(render({"arbiter": arbiter}))), limit)
        self.assert_rejected({"monitoring": {"enabled": True, "stateLimitBytes": 536870911}}, refusal.format(536870911, 536870912))
        same = {"storageSize": "2048Mi", "resources": {"limits": {"memory": "2048Mi"}}}
        self.assertEqual(voter_state_limit(documents(render({"arbiter": same, "monitoring": {"enabled": True}}))), 536870912)
```

```python
    def test_monitoring_changes_no_workload(self):
```

```yaml

# Monitoring of this network (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §13.1, §15;
# templates/monitoring.yaml): a headless metrics Service and a VMServiceScrape
# for the voters, a VMServiceScrape for the listed sentio-node SI hosts, and one
# VMRule. Off by default. Enable it only once every voter and every listed host
# runs a release that exports the series the rules read: an absent series never
# fires. Requires arbiter.protocol=pinned-genesis-v1 and arbiter.metrics.enabled.
# vmalert on sea only writes ALERTS series (notifier.blackhole), so delivery to a
# human is a Grafana rule on ALERTS{network="<network>"}
# (docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md §8). No value here enters a
# config checksum: turning monitoring on or off restarts nothing.
monitoring:
  enabled: false
  # The network label every scraped series gets; empty means schemaSnapshotID.
  network: ""
  interval: 30s
  scrapeTimeout: 10s
  # Extra labels on the VMServiceScrapes and the VMRule.
  labels: {}
  # L = min(1 GiB snapshot read cap, arbiter.resources.limits.memory / 4,
  # arbiter.storageSize / 4): 536870912 (512 MiB) for 2Gi voters. The state
  # alerts warn at L/4 and page at L/2; resize the voters before 3L/4. While
  # monitoring is on, validate.yaml refuses a value that differs from L, so a
  # voter resize changes this value in the same commit.
  stateLimitBytes: 536870912
  hosts:
    # charts/sentio-node releases in this namespace whose SI host series
    # (Service port hg-metrics) are scraped. StorageIntegrityHostUnscraped fires
    # for a listed release that has no target or does not answer, so list a
    # host only once it runs.
    releases: []
  clickhouse:
    # ClickHouseInstallation names (label clickhouse_altinity_com_chi of the
    # cluster's pod-annotation scrape) whose restarts and default-disk space
    # are alerted on.
    installations: []
    diskFreeWarnRatio: 0.2
    diskFreeCriticalRatio: 0.1
  runbookURL: https://github.com/sentioxyz/production/blob/main/docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md
```

```gotemplate

{{- /* The value of the network label the monitoring scrapes add to every
series: monitoring.network, or the network's schemaSnapshotID. */ -}}
{{- define "storage-integrity.monitoringNetwork" -}}
{{- default .Values.schemaSnapshotID .Values.monitoring.network -}}
{{- end }}

{{- /* Bytes of a voter quantity. Called with (dict "name" <value path> "value"
<quantity>); accepts only a whole number of Mi or Gi, the forms
values.schema.json allows, and fails on anything else. */ -}}
{{- define "storage-integrity.quantityBytes" -}}
{{- $quantity := toString .value -}}
{{- if not (regexMatch "^[1-9][0-9]*(Mi|Gi)$" $quantity) -}}
{{- fail (printf "%s must be a whole number of Mi or Gi ([1-9][0-9]*(Mi|Gi)), got %q" .name $quantity) -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- $number := int64 (trimSuffix "Mi" (trimSuffix "Gi" $quantity)) -}}
{{- if hasSuffix "Gi" $quantity -}}
{{- mul $number 1073741824 -}}
{{- else -}}
{{- mul $number 1048576 -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- end }}

{{- /* L of housegate spec 2026-10-14 §13.1: the smallest of the 1 GiB snapshot
document read cap (arbiter fsm/snapshot.go maxSnapshotDocBytes), a quarter of
each voter's memory limit and a quarter of each voter's Raft volume. */ -}}
{{- define "storage-integrity.stateLimitBytes" -}}
{{- $memory := int64 (include "storage-integrity.quantityBytes" (dict "name" "arbiter.resources.limits.memory" "value" .Values.arbiter.resources.limits.memory)) -}}
{{- $volume := int64 (include "storage-integrity.quantityBytes" (dict "name" "arbiter.storageSize" "value" .Values.arbiter.storageSize)) -}}
{{- min 1073741824 (div $memory 4) (div $volume 4) -}}
{{- end }}
```

Create `charts/storage-integrity/templates/monitoring.yaml`:

```yaml
{{- /*
Monitoring of one storage-integrity network (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §13.1,
§15): a headless metrics Service and a VMServiceScrape for the Arbiter voters,
a VMServiceScrape for the listed sentio-node SI hosts, and one VMRule.

The voters and every ClickHouse pod are also scraped by the cluster's
kubernetes-pods job through their prometheus.io annotations, without a network
label. The scrapes below add network and si_component, so every Arbiter and
host expression selects network="<network>" and never reads the duplicate;
ClickHouse and kube-state-metrics series are selected by namespace and pod or
installation instead. No expression selects on job, and every by() keeps
cluster, the label vmagent adds to every series, so an aggregated alert still
carries it. Every alert also carries the network as a rule label: the Grafana
rule that delivers these alerts selects ALERTS{network="<network>"}.

The host and ClickHouse groups render only with something to read: an absent
series never fires, so a rule without its scrape or installation would only
look armed. None of these values enters a config checksum.
*/ -}}
{{- if .Values.monitoring.enabled }}
{{- $fullname := include "storage-integrity.fullname" . }}
{{- $network := include "storage-integrity.monitoringNetwork" . }}
{{- $namespace := .Release.Namespace }}
{{- $limit := int64 .Values.monitoring.stateLimitBytes }}
{{- $runbook := .Values.monitoring.runbookURL }}
{{- $hosts := .Values.monitoring.hosts.releases }}
{{- $installations := .Values.monitoring.clickhouse.installations }}
{{- $chis := join "|" $installations }}
{{- $voterPods := printf "%s-arbiter-[0-9]+" $fullname }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ $fullname }}-arbiter-metrics
  labels:
    {{- include "storage-integrity.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: arbiter
    storage-integrity.sentio.xyz/metrics: arbiter
spec:
  # Headless and publishing not-ready addresses, so a voter that is up but not
  # ready is still scraped and a voter without an address counts as missing.
  clusterIP: None
  publishNotReadyAddresses: true
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ include "storage-integrity.name" . }}
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: arbiter
  ports:
    - {name: metrics, port: {{ .Values.arbiter.metrics.port }}, targetPort: metrics}
---
apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1beta1
kind: VMServiceScrape
metadata:
  name: {{ $fullname }}-arbiter
  labels:
    {{- include "storage-integrity.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    {{- with .Values.monitoring.labels }}
    {{- toYaml . | nindent 4 }}
    {{- end }}
spec:
  namespaceSelector:
    matchNames: [{{ $namespace | quote }}]
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
      storage-integrity.sentio.xyz/metrics: arbiter
  endpoints:
    - port: metrics
      path: /metrics
      interval: {{ .Values.monitoring.interval }}
      scrapeTimeout: {{ .Values.monitoring.scrapeTimeout }}
      relabelConfigs:
        - {action: replace, targetLabel: network, replacement: {{ $network | quote }}}
        - {action: replace, targetLabel: si_component, replacement: arbiter}
{{- if $hosts }}
---
apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1beta1
kind: VMServiceScrape
metadata:
  name: {{ $fullname }}-hosts
  labels:
    {{- include "storage-integrity.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    {{- with .Values.monitoring.labels }}
    {{- toYaml . | nindent 4 }}
    {{- end }}
spec:
  namespaceSelector:
    matchNames: [{{ $namespace | quote }}]
  # The charts/sentio-node Service of each listed release; its hg-metrics port
  # serves the embedded HouseGate registry with the SI host series.
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/component: node
    matchExpressions:
      - key: app.kubernetes.io/instance
        operator: In
        values:
          {{- range $hosts }}
          - {{ . | quote }}
          {{- end }}
  endpoints:
    - port: hg-metrics
      path: /metrics
      interval: {{ .Values.monitoring.interval }}
      scrapeTimeout: {{ .Values.monitoring.scrapeTimeout }}
      relabelConfigs:
        - {action: replace, targetLabel: network, replacement: {{ $network | quote }}}
        - {action: replace, targetLabel: si_component, replacement: host}
        - {action: replace, sourceLabels: [__meta_kubernetes_service_label_app_kubernetes_io_instance], targetLabel: release}
{{- end }}
---
apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1beta1
kind: VMRule
metadata:
  name: {{ $fullname }}
  labels:
    {{- include "storage-integrity.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    {{- with .Values.monitoring.labels }}
    {{- toYaml . | nindent 4 }}
    {{- end }}
spec:
  groups:
    # L = monitoring.stateLimitBytes = min(read cap, voter memory / 4, voter
    # volume / 4), checked by validate.yaml: warn at L/4, page at L/2, resize the
    # voters before 3L/4. The memory alerts read the in-memory gauge, the volume
    # alerts the snapshot document plus the Raft log (arbiter README).
    - name: {{ $fullname }}.arbiter-state-size
      rules:
        - alert: ArbiterStateSizeHigh
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_state_bytes{network="{{ $network }}"}) > {{ $limit }} / 4
          for: 30m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "Arbiter state passed L/4; plan the voter resize before 3L/4"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - alert: ArbiterStateSizeCritical
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_state_bytes{network="{{ $network }}"}) > {{ $limit }} / 2
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "Arbiter state passed L/2; resize the voters before it reaches 3L/4"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - alert: ArbiterRaftStorageHigh
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_snapshot_doc_bytes{network="{{ $network }}"} + arbiter_raft_log_store_bytes{network="{{ $network }}"}) > {{ $limit }} / 4
          for: 30m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "The snapshot document plus the Raft log passed L/4 of the voter volume budget"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - alert: ArbiterRaftStorageCritical
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_snapshot_doc_bytes{network="{{ $network }}"} + arbiter_raft_log_store_bytes{network="{{ $network }}"}) > {{ $limit }} / 2
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "The snapshot document plus the Raft log passed L/2 of the voter volume budget"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - alert: ArbiterSnapshotDocNearReadCap
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_snapshot_doc_bytes{network="{{ $network }}"} / arbiter_snapshot_doc_read_cap_bytes{network="{{ $network }}"}) > 0.5
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "The snapshot document passed half the read cap; a voter cannot restart once it crosses the cap"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - alert: ArbiterSnapshotRestoreFailed
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network) (increase(arbiter_snapshot_failures_total{network="{{ $network }}", operation=~"restore|install"}[15m])) > 0
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "A running voter refused a snapshot install or restore (a refused startup restore is a crash loop instead)"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
    # The arbiter README's arbiter-promotion group with this network's selector,
    # plus the separate quarantine alert the README asks for.
    - name: {{ $fullname }}.arbiter-promotion
      rules:
        - record: arbiter:safe_watermark:max
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_safe_watermark_block_seq{network="{{ $network }}"})
        - record: arbiter:pending_blocks:max
          expr: |-
            clamp_min(max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_sealed_block_seq{network="{{ $network }}"}) - arbiter:safe_watermark:max{network="{{ $network }}"}, 0)
        - alert: ArbiterPromotionStalled
          expr: |-
            (changes(arbiter:safe_watermark:max{network="{{ $network }}"}[15m]) == 0)
            and on (cluster, network)
            ((arbiter:pending_blocks:max{network="{{ $network }}"} > 0)
              or (max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_open_block_statements{network="{{ $network }}"}) > 0))
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "Arbiter has pending work but its safe watermark is not advancing (after the tracks activation, some track is stuck)"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - record: arbiter:track_safe_block_seq:max
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network, indexer_id) (arbiter_track_safe_block_seq{network="{{ $network }}"})
        - alert: ArbiterTrackStalled
          expr: |-
            (changes(arbiter:track_safe_block_seq:max{network="{{ $network }}"}[15m]) == 0)
            and on (cluster, network)
            ((arbiter:pending_blocks:max{network="{{ $network }}"} > 0)
              or (max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_open_block_statements{network="{{ $network }}"}) > 0))
            unless on (cluster, network, indexer_id)
            (max by (cluster, network, indexer_id) (arbiter_track_quarantined{network="{{ $network }}"}) == 1)
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "An SI indexer's safe track prefix is not advancing while the network has pending work"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - alert: ArbiterRejectedCleanupStuck
          expr: |-
            (max by (cluster, network, indexer_id) (arbiter_track_rejected_partitions{network="{{ $network }}"}) > 0)
            unless on (cluster, network, indexer_id)
            (max by (cluster, network, indexer_id) (arbiter_track_quarantined{network="{{ $network }}"}) == 1)
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "A released SI indexer's rejected-part cleanup is unacknowledged, so every consensus update is refused; quarantine the indexer again to pass the drain gate"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - alert: ArbiterTrackQuarantined
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network, indexer_id) (arbiter_track_quarantined{network="{{ $network }}"}) == 1
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "An SI indexer is quarantined: its track issues no new work and its host refuses its tables until an authority releases it"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
    # The voters themselves. A voter whose startup restore is refused exits
    # before /metrics listens, so the restart alerts read kube-state-metrics; the
    # verifiers export no metrics, so their count is the registry's.
    - name: {{ $fullname }}.arbiter-voters
      rules:
        - alert: ArbiterVoterUnscraped
          expr: |-
            (count by (cluster, network) (up{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="arbiter"} == 1) < {{ int .Values.arbiter.replicas }})
            or absent(up{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="arbiter"} == 1)
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "Fewer than {{ int .Values.arbiter.replicas }} Arbiter voters answer their metrics scrape; the Arbiter rules cannot fire for a voter that is not scraped"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#6-voters"
        - alert: ArbiterVoterRestarting
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, namespace, pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", pod=~"{{ $voterPods }}", container="arbiter"}[30m])) > 0
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "An Arbiter voter container restarted in the last 30 minutes"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#6-voters"
        - alert: ArbiterVoterCrashLooping
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", pod=~"{{ $voterPods }}", container="arbiter", reason="CrashLoopBackOff"}) > 0
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "An Arbiter voter is crash looping (a refused startup snapshot restore stops it before /metrics listens)"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#6-voters"
        - alert: ArbiterConsensusHoldStuck
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network, mode) (arbiter_consensus_hold_active{network="{{ $network }}"}) == 1
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "A consensus hold has been active for 15 minutes, past the leader's longest hold (consensus_admin.max_drain_mode, 10m by default)"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#7-reads-and-holds"
        - alert: ArbiterVerifiersBelowThree
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network) (arbiter_nodes{network="{{ $network }}", role="verifier", status="active"}) < {{ int .Values.verifier.replicas }}
          for: 10m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "Fewer than {{ int .Values.verifier.replicas }} verifiers are active in the Arbiter registry"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#4-verifiers"
    {{- if $hosts }}
    # The SI hosts' embedded HouseGate registry: the owner hg_safe audit, the
    # peer reserved-name guard and the table state.
    - name: {{ $fullname }}.hosts
      rules:
        - alert: SentioNodeOwnerAuditUnclean
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network, release) (sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_unclean_tables{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="host"}) > 0
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "The owner hg_safe audit of an SI host reports unclean tables (report mode only logs them; repair mode holds them Pending)"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#9-report-mode-soak"
        - alert: SentioNodeOwnerAuditHoldingTables
          expr: |-
            (max by (cluster, network, release) (sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_unclean_tables{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="host"}) > 0)
            and on (cluster, network, release)
            (max by (cluster, network, release) (sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_mode{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="host", mode="repair"}) == 1)
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "An SI host in owner-audit repair mode holds unclean tables Pending (733) until their audit is clean"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#10-repair-mode"
        - alert: SentioNodeOwnerAuditDroppedTwins
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network, release) (increase(sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_dropped_twins_total{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="host"}[1h])) > 0
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "The owner audit dropped resurrected hg_safe twins in the last hour (irreversible per part); the SNode log names them"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#10-repair-mode"
        - alert: SentioNodeOwnerAuditFSMUnavailable
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network, release) (increase(sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_fsm_unavailable_total{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="host"}[15m])) > 0
          for: 30m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "The owner audit cannot read the Arbiter's partition states and falls back to the SNode's own inventory"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#9-report-mode-soak"
        - alert: StorageIntegrityHostUnscraped
          expr: |-
            (max by (cluster, network, release) (up{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="host"}) == 0)
            {{- range $hosts }}
            or absent(up{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="host", release="{{ . }}"})
            {{- end }}
          for: 10m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "A listed SI host exports no metrics (no scrape target, or the scrape fails); its host rules cannot fire"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#5-snodes-in-report-mode"
        - alert: StorageIntegrityPeerReservedNameRefused
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network, release, reason) (increase(storage_integrity_peer_reserved_name_refusals_total{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="host"}[15m])) > 0
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "HouseGate refused a peer-trusted statement that mentions a reserved storage-integrity name"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#2-reserved-name-preflight"
        - alert: StorageIntegrityTablePendingTooLong
          expr: |-
            max by (cluster, network, release, table) (sentio_node_storage_integrity_table_pending_seconds{network="{{ $network }}", si_component="host"}) > 1800
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "An SI table has been Pending on its host for more than 30 minutes (733 to every client)"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
    {{- end }}
    {{- if $installations }}
    # The SI ClickHouse installations, from the pod-annotation scrape (label
    # clickhouse_altinity_com_chi). An owner restart inside the outdated-part
    # window resurrects the parts a REPLACE PARTITION retired.
    - name: {{ $fullname }}.clickhouse
      rules:
        - alert: StorageIntegrityClickHouseRestarted
          expr: |-
            min by (cluster, namespace, clickhouse_altinity_com_chi, pod) (ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_Uptime{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", clickhouse_altinity_com_chi=~"{{ $chis }}"}) < 900
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "An SI ClickHouse restarted less than 15 minutes ago"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - alert: StorageIntegrityClickHouseDiskLow
          expr: |-
            min by (cluster, namespace, clickhouse_altinity_com_chi, pod) (ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_DiskAvailable_default{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", clickhouse_altinity_com_chi=~"{{ $chis }}"} / ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_DiskTotal_default{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", clickhouse_altinity_com_chi=~"{{ $chis }}"}) < {{ .Values.monitoring.clickhouse.diskFreeWarnRatio }}
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "An SI ClickHouse's default disk is below monitoring.clickhouse.diskFreeWarnRatio free"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
        - alert: StorageIntegrityClickHouseDiskCritical
          expr: |-
            min by (cluster, namespace, clickhouse_altinity_com_chi, pod) (ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_DiskAvailable_default{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", clickhouse_altinity_com_chi=~"{{ $chis }}"} / ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_DiskTotal_default{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", clickhouse_altinity_com_chi=~"{{ $chis }}"}) < {{ .Values.monitoring.clickhouse.diskFreeCriticalRatio }}
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            network: {{ $network | quote }}
          annotations:
            summary: "An SI ClickHouse's default disk is below monitoring.clickhouse.diskFreeCriticalRatio free"
            runbook_url: "{{ $runbook }}#13-operating-rules"
    {{- end }}
{{- end }}
```

In `charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py`, insert after `STAGE3_P0_RUNBOOK_SECTIONS` (Step 7, before the two blank lines and `SENTIO_NODE_CHART`):

```python
# devnet2-si-v2's voter sizing, restated in storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml
# (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §13.1; Plan S3-B K14), and its L. A resize is the
# operating rule of docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md §13: it changes
# the overlay, these mirrors and monitoring.stateLimitBytes together.
DEVNET2_VOTER_MEMORY_LIMIT = "2Gi"
DEVNET2_VOTER_STORAGE_SIZE = "2Gi"
DEVNET2_STATE_LIMIT_BYTES = 536870912
# monitoring.enabled on devnet2-si-v2: docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md
# §8 turns it on in a single-service commit once every voter and both hosts
# export the series the rules read.
DEVNET2_MONITORING_ENABLED = False
DEVNET2_MONITORING_NETWORK = "devnet2-si-v2"
# The SI hosts and SI ClickHouse installations devnet2's rules cover. indexer-c's
# are appended only after its first start (Plan S3-B Task 21): a listed host that
# exports nothing fires StorageIntegrityHostUnscraped.
DEVNET2_MONITORED_HOSTS = ("sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a", "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b")
DEVNET2_MONITORED_CLICKHOUSES = ("storage-integrity-si-v2", "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b")
```

Append to `ActualFreshNetworkTest`, after `test_unset_owner_audit_renders_unchanged` (Step 3, before the two blank lines and `if __name__ == "__main__":`):

```python

    def with_monitoring(self):
        """The network release with monitoring.enabled merged last."""
        release = dict(self.control_release)
        release["values"] = list(self.control_release["values"]) + [{"monitoring": {"enabled": True}}]
        return documents(self.render_release(release))

    def test_devnet2_voter_sizing_is_pinned(self):
        # Spec 2026-10-14 §13.1 and Plan S3-B K14: the overlay restates the voters'
        # memory and volume, so a change of the chart defaults cannot resize them
        # unreviewed, and L of these voters is DEVNET2_STATE_LIMIT_BYTES.
        arbiter = yaml.safe_load((DEVNET2 / "storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml").read_text())["arbiter"]
        self.assertEqual((arbiter["storageClassName"], arbiter["storageSize"]), ("local-path", DEVNET2_VOTER_STORAGE_SIZE))
        self.assertEqual(arbiter["resources"], {
            "requests": {"cpu": "250m", "memory": "256Mi"},
            "limits": {"cpu": "2", "memory": DEVNET2_VOTER_MEMORY_LIMIT},
        })
        spec = self.control[("StatefulSet", f"{FRESH_RELEASE}-arbiter")]["spec"]
        self.assertEqual(spec["template"]["spec"]["containers"][0]["resources"], arbiter["resources"])
        self.assertEqual(spec["volumeClaimTemplates"], [{
            "metadata": {"name": "data"},
            "spec": {
                "accessModes": ["ReadWriteOnce"],
                "storageClassName": "local-path",
                "resources": {"requests": {"storage": DEVNET2_VOTER_STORAGE_SIZE}},
            },
        }])
        self.assertEqual(DEVNET2_STATE_LIMIT_BYTES, min(
            SNAPSHOT_DOC_READ_CAP_BYTES,
            quantity_bytes(DEVNET2_VOTER_MEMORY_LIMIT) // 4,
            quantity_bytes(DEVNET2_VOTER_STORAGE_SIZE) // 4,
        ))
        self.assertEqual(voter_state_limit(self.control, FRESH_RELEASE), DEVNET2_STATE_LIMIT_BYTES)
        # Turning monitoring on (runbook §8) passes the L check with these voters
        # and puts the state alerts at L/4 and L/2.
        monitored = self.with_monitoring()
        for alert, divisor in (("ArbiterStateSizeHigh", 4), ("ArbiterStateSizeCritical", 2)):
            with self.subTest(alert=alert):
                expr = alert_rule(monitored, alert, FRESH_RELEASE)["expr"]
                self.assertTrue(expr.endswith(f"> {DEVNET2_STATE_LIMIT_BYTES} / {divisor}"), expr)

    def test_devnet2_monitoring_follows_the_rollout(self):
        # docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md §8 turns monitoring on together
        # with DEVNET2_MONITORING_ENABLED; Plan S3-B Task 21 appends indexer-c's
        # host and installation together with the two tuples.
        monitoring = yaml.safe_load((DEVNET2 / "storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml").read_text())["monitoring"]
        self.assertIs(monitoring["enabled"], DEVNET2_MONITORING_ENABLED)
        self.assertEqual(monitoring["network"], DEVNET2_MONITORING_NETWORK)
        self.assertEqual(tuple(monitoring["hosts"]["releases"]), DEVNET2_MONITORED_HOSTS)
        self.assertEqual(tuple(monitoring["clickhouse"]["installations"]), DEVNET2_MONITORED_CLICKHOUSES)
        # The network label is this network's schema snapshot id.
        self.assertEqual(DEVNET2_MONITORING_NETWORK, arbiter_config(self.control, FRESH_RELEASE)["genesis"]["schema_snapshot_id"])
        # Every monitored host is a sentio-node release of this helmfile whose
        # Service carries what the hosts scrape selects.
        hosts = {
            name for (_, name), release in self.releases.items()
            if (FRESH_HELMFILE.parent / release["chart"]).resolve() == SENTIO_NODE_CHART
        }
        self.assertLessEqual(set(DEVNET2_MONITORED_HOSTS), hosts)
        # A host appended later (indexer-c, Plan S3-B Task 21) is rendered here.
        releases = {name: release for (_, name), release in self.releases.items()}
        rendered = {"sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a": self.source, "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b": self.indexer_b}
        for name in DEVNET2_MONITORED_HOSTS:
            with self.subTest(host=name):
                docs = rendered[name] if name in rendered else documents(self.render_release(releases[name]))
                service = docs[("Service", name)]
                labels = service["metadata"]["labels"]
                self.assertEqual((labels["app.kubernetes.io/component"], labels["app.kubernetes.io/instance"]), ("node", name))
                self.assertIn({"name": "hg-metrics", "port": 9091, "targetPort": 9091, "protocol": "TCP"}, service["spec"]["ports"])
        # Every monitored installation is a ClickHouseInstallation of this network.
        installations = {name for kind, name in self.control if kind == "ClickHouseInstallation"}
        for path in FRESH_FILES:
            if path.suffix == ".yaml":
                installations |= {
                    document["metadata"]["name"] for document in yaml.safe_load_all(path.read_text())
                    if document and document.get("kind") == "ClickHouseInstallation"
                }
        self.assertLessEqual(set(DEVNET2_MONITORED_CLICKHOUSES), installations)
        # The release renders the monitoring objects exactly while the rollout has
        # them on, and turning them on scrapes and alerts on what is listed here.
        self.assertIs(("VMRule", FRESH_RELEASE) in self.control, DEVNET2_MONITORING_ENABLED)
        monitored = self.with_monitoring()
        scrape = monitored[("VMServiceScrape", f"{FRESH_RELEASE}-hosts")]["spec"]
        self.assertEqual(scrape["selector"]["matchExpressions"][0]["values"], list(DEVNET2_MONITORED_HOSTS))
        chis = "|".join(DEVNET2_MONITORED_CLICKHOUSES)
        self.assertIn(f'clickhouse_altinity_com_chi=~"{chis}"', alert_rule(monitored, "StorageIntegrityClickHouseDiskLow", FRESH_RELEASE)["expr"])
        self.assertIn(f'network="{DEVNET2_MONITORING_NETWORK}"', alert_rule(monitored, "ArbiterStateSizeHigh", FRESH_RELEASE)["expr"])
```

Notes:
- **Why the runbook is shaped this way.** It follows the stage-2 runbook (header paragraphs, stage table with ways back, §0 layered on the earlier runbooks' §0, one bash session with `set -eo pipefail`, `Confirm before running.` before every mutating block, read-only blocks `tee`d into `$si_backup`, the voter order written once, revert blocks per commit). The order is binding: the reserved-name preflight before any `HG_TAG` image reaches a host (§2), the replay on fresh copies of all three voters before any voter moves (§3, Plan S3-A Task 11 Step 13), verifiers, then both hosts in report mode, then the voters followers first and the leader last (the reads and holds answer only on a leader on `ARBITER_TAG`; until then the owner audit counts `fsm_unavailable`, K3), then monitoring once every series exists (an absent series never fires), a soak, and repair per owner, indexer-b first (K12).
- **How the data-plane listener answers the reads (arbiter `origin/main`).** `SafeState` is registered by `RegisterDataPlane` (`server/server.go:142-150`) on `grpc_listen`, which `startGRPC` serves with `grpc.NewServer()` and no credentials or interceptor (`cmd/arbiter/grpc.go:43-58`); the chart binds `grpc_listen: 0.0.0.0:7080` and sets no `consensus_admin.listen` (`charts/storage-integrity/templates/arbiter.yaml:10`), so administration shares port 7080 (`cmd/arbiter/grpc.go:21-27`). Every read crosses `consensusReadBarrier` (`server/safestate.go:26-30`), and a follower answers with the leader's Raft id, which arbiter-core's `dataplane.Client.WithLeaderRetry` follows (`dataplane/client.go:168-214`; the client dials insecure, `:117-121`). The runbook tools reach port 7080 from inside a voter pod (`si_arbiter`, `si_voter`), as `arbiter-admin` does. So `partstates` is that client, built from `CORE_TAG`, copied into every voter's arbiter container like `si_put_voters` copies a file (stage-1 §0) and run in the leader's. The copy is an `exec` that writes into the pods (contract §15), so it is its own confirmed block (`si_partstates_put`, runbook §1.3 and again in §7 after the voters were replaced), and `si_partstates_run` never copies; the operators' `editor` role grants `pods/exec` but not `pods/portforward` (`k8s-common/_roles/editor-clusterrole.yaml`), so the tool cannot run locally against forwarded ports instead; the Raft ids equal the SNodes' `arbiterPeers` ids (`k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/sentio-node-indexer-a-storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml:86-92`).
- **The tool needs the table list from the registry.** `GetPartitionStates` requires `table_id`, so `partstates` first reads `TableRegistry.GetTableRegistry` (served by every arbiter since stage 1) and takes each table whose newest incarnation with `hg_*` tables (`HasPhysicalTables`) is owned by the indexer (`Owner`); `-registry` prints every incarnation for §2. It prints one JSON line per partition (contract §9, D5), the shape Task 15's `p0-partstates.py` reads (an object with a table id and a partition id); a table with no partition state (never promoted) prints no line, so every "each Active table promoted since the restart" check takes the Active tables from `-registry` (`si_active_tables`) and compares them with the partition lines (`si_unpromoted`). It builds with `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64` and `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.3+auto` (arbiter-core's `go` line at the base; `+auto` moves to a newer toolchain only when `CORE_TAG`'s `go.mod` requires one, where a bare `go1.26.3` would refuse, and a local Go 1.27 build makes the bundled `sonic` print a fallback warning on stderr); housegate's purego dependency still links the glibc loader (as the arbiter image's Dockerfile notes), which the debian-based arbiter image has.
- **K12 made checkable.** "Throughout" is read from VictoriaMetrics (`max_over_time`), and from at least two local `si_audit` samples appended hourly to `audit-<x>-soak.txt` (contract §9; Task 15's `p0_k12` counts them), so each soak ends no earlier than 24 h after the later of the owner's restart and §8's sync; "at least one promotion of each of its SI tables" is `last_acked_promotion_seq` above the promotion sequence recorded right after the restart (`$si_backup/restart-<x>`); "flat since the leader replacement" compares with a sample taken in the same block as the leader's replacement. indexer-b's SNode lists no genesis table (`tableIDs: []`) and its stage-2 test table was dropped, so the soak creates `devuser1.s3_p0` (the `devuser1` owner's own action, as stage 2's `s2_e2e`) and drops it in §11.
- **K13's delivery.** The Grafana rule is a user action with "no data" set to Normal (the healthy answer is no series, which would otherwise raise a NoData alert); the probe is a VMRule applied and deleted with `kubectl`; the permalinks are recorded by the user. VictoriaMetrics (`vmsingle-vm.monitoring.svc:8429`, the address other services use, e.g. `charts/sentio/values.yaml:187`) and vmalert (`vmalert-vm.monitoring.svc:8080`) are read from arbiter-0; §8's first block proves both answer before anything depends on them.
- **Anchors (binding for Task 15 and every `runbook_url`).** Step 6 checks every `runbook_url` of the rendered VMRule against the 14 top-level anchors of the table below (the `##` sections, the anchors Task 13's `STAGE3_P0_RUNBOOK_SECTIONS` and `test_every_rule_reads_only_this_networks_series` accept, D2) and prints the mapping. - [ ] **Step 2: Write the runbook checker and see it fail**

The checker encodes contract §9's sections, the confirmation convention, the shell syntax of every block and the `runbook_url` anchors, so the runbook is written against it. Write `$W.runbook-check.py` (local only, never committed):

````python
"""Checks docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md (Plan S3-B Task 14; local only, never committed).

usage: python3 -I runbook-check.py <runbook> [<rendered chart YAML with monitoring enabled>]

Checks: the section headings of Plan S3-B contract §9, in order, with unique
GitHub anchors; exactly one bash block in §0 and exactly one go block, in §0;
every mutating block after §0 preceded by "Confirm before running." and every
block so preceded mutating; every bash block parses under bash and /bin/bash
(3.2); no ledger placeholder left; and, given a rendered chart, every
runbook_url of its VMRule pointing at a top-level section anchor of this
runbook, the anchors Task 13's test_every_rule_reads_only_this_networks_series
accepts (STAGE3_P0_RUNBOOK_SECTIONS); it prints the alert-to-anchor mapping.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

import yaml

HEADINGS = [
    (2, "0. Session helpers"),
    (2, "1. Preparation"),
    (3, "1.1 Pins"),
    (3, "1.2 Identities"),
    (3, "1.3 Preconditions and baseline"),
    (2, "2. Reserved-name preflight"),
    (2, "3. Offline replay check"),
    (3, "3.1 Rehearsal binaries"),
    (3, "3.2 Baseline"),
    (3, "3.3 Replay"),
    (2, "4. Verifiers"),
    (2, "5. SNodes in report mode"),
    (3, "5.1 indexer-a"),
    (3, "5.2 indexer-b"),
    (2, "6. Voters"),
    (2, "7. Reads and holds"),
    (2, "8. Monitoring"),
    (2, "9. Report-mode soak"),
    (2, "10. Repair mode"),
    (3, "10.1 indexer-b"),
    (3, "10.2 indexer-a"),
    (2, "11. End"),
    (2, "12. Rollback"),
    (2, "13. Operating rules"),
    (3, "13.1 State size and voter resize"),
    (3, "13.2 The unresolved-intent step"),
    (3, "13.3 ClickHouse restarts"),
    (3, "13.4 Promotion budget for drills"),
    (3, "13.5 Holds"),
]
RUNBOOK_URL = "https://github.com/sentioxyz/production/blob/main/docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md"
MUTATING = re.compile(
    r"git push|helmfile .* sync|si_kubectl apply -f|si_kubectl delete |si_replace_voter|si_accept_a_track"
    r"|si_agent_start|si_revert_stage3|si_partstates_put|DROP PART|DROP TABLE|CREATE TABLE|INSERT INTO"
)
PLACEHOLDERS = re.compile(r"<(ARBITER_TAG|ARBITER_DIGEST|SN_COMMIT|SN_DIGEST|CORE_TAG|HG_TAG|PROTO_TAG)>")


def slug(text):
    # GitHub's anchor rule for ASCII headings: lower case, drop punctuation
    # other than hyphens and spaces, spaces to hyphens.
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 _-]", "", text.lower()).replace(" ", "-")


def main():
    path = sys.argv[1]
    text = open(path).read()
    problems = []

    found = [(len(m.group(1)), m.group(2)) for m in re.finditer(r"^(#{2,3}) (.+)$", text, re.M)]
    if found != HEADINGS:
        problems.append("headings differ from contract §9: unexpected %s, missing %s" % ([h for h in found if h not in HEADINGS], [h for h in HEADINGS if h not in found]))
    anchors = [slug(t) for _, t in found]
    if len(set(anchors)) != len(anchors):
        problems.append("duplicate anchors")
    sections = {slug(t) for level, t in found if level == 2}

    start = text.index("## 0. Session helpers")
    end = text.index("\n## 1. Preparation")
    blocks = list(re.finditer(r"^```(\w*)\n(.*?)^```$", text, re.S | re.M))
    bash = [b for b in blocks if b.group(1) == "bash"]
    go = [b for b in blocks if b.group(1) == "go"]
    if len([b for b in bash if start < b.start() < end]) != 1:
        problems.append("§0 must hold exactly one bash block")
    if len(go) != 1 or not start < go[0].start() < end:
        problems.append("the runbook must hold exactly one go block, in §0")
    if {b.group(1) for b in blocks} - {"bash", "go"}:
        problems.append("only bash and go blocks are allowed: %s" % ({b.group(1) for b in blocks} - {"bash", "go"}))

    confirmed = mutating = 0
    for b in bash:
        if start < b.start() < end:
            continue
        previous = [line for line in text[: b.start()].splitlines() if line.strip()][-1]
        is_confirmed = previous == "Confirm before running."
        is_mutating = bool(MUTATING.search(b.group(2)))
        confirmed += is_confirmed
        mutating += is_mutating
        if is_mutating != is_confirmed:
            problems.append("%s block without the matching confirmation: %s" % ("mutating" if is_mutating else "read-only", b.group(2).splitlines()[0]))

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        for i, b in enumerate(bash):
            f = "%s/block-%02d.sh" % (tmp, i)
            open(f, "w").write(b.group(2))
            for shell in ("bash", "/bin/bash"):
                r = subprocess.run([shell, "-n", f], capture_output=True, text=True)
                if r.returncode != 0:
                    problems.append("%s -n fails on block %d (%s): %s" % (shell, i, b.group(2).splitlines()[0], r.stderr.strip()))

    if PLACEHOLDERS.search(text):
        problems.append("ledger placeholders left: %s" % sorted(set(PLACEHOLDERS.findall(text))))

    urls = 0
    mapping = []
    if len(sys.argv) > 2:
        for doc in yaml.safe_load_all(open(sys.argv[2])):
            if not doc or doc.get("kind") != "VMRule":
                continue
            for group in doc["spec"]["groups"]:
                for rule in group["rules"]:
                    if "alert" not in rule:
                        continue
                    url = rule.get("annotations", {}).get("runbook_url", "")
                    base, _, fragment = url.partition("#")
                    urls += 1
                    mapping.append("%s -> #%s" % (rule["alert"], fragment))
                    if base != RUNBOOK_URL or fragment not in sections:
                        problems.append("%s: runbook_url %r is not a top-level section anchor of this runbook" % (rule["alert"], url))
        if urls == 0:
            problems.append("the rendered chart carries no VMRule alert")

    if problems:
        sys.exit("\n".join(problems))
    print("%d headings with unique anchors; %d bash blocks parse under bash and /bin/bash; %d mutating blocks, each confirmed; one go block in §0; no ledger placeholder" % (len(found), len(bash), mutating))
    if len(sys.argv) > 2:
        print("\n".join(mapping))
        print("%d runbook_url annotations, each a top-level section anchor of this runbook" % urls)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
````
