````markdown
# Storage integrity devnet2: multi-source stage 3 P0 (guards, owner audit, monitoring)

This runbook moves devnet2-si-v2 (releases `storage-integrity-si-v2`, `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a` and `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b` in `sentio-network-devnet2`) onto the stage-3 P0 builds of the multi-source storage-integrity design and turns their guards on: HouseGate's peer-trusted reserved-name guard on both hosts, the owner `hg_safe` audit in report mode and then in repair mode on both owners, the arbiter's stage-3 reads, consensus holds and state-size gauges, and the chart's alert rules with a delivery that reaches a human. Design: housegate `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-stage3-database-groups-design.md` §13.1, §14 and the P0 row of §16, as clarified by the stage-3 plans (housegate `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-s3a-p0-guards.md`, clarifications K1 to K10, and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-s3b-p0-hosts-rollout.md`, clarifications K11 to K22). It continues [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md) (multi-source stage 2, done on 2026-10-14: tracks active since epoch 5). The stage numbers below are this runbook's own.

| Stage | Change | Way back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | PR: the owner-audit value of `charts/sentio-node`, the monitoring objects (off) and the voter budget check of `charts/storage-integrity`, the devnet2 voter sizing restated, the stage-3 sentio-node image listed for review, the inertness script, this runbook; inert on merge | Revert the PR |
| 1 | Preparation and the reserved-name preflight (§1, §2) | None needed |
| 2 | Offline replay check of all three voters under `v0.12.0` and `<ARBITER_TAG>` (§3) | None needed |
| 3 | Verifiers to arbiter `<ARBITER_TAG>` (§4) | Revert (§12) |
| 4 | indexer-a, then indexer-b: sentio-node `<SN_COMMIT>` (HouseGate `<HG_TAG>`, arbiter-core `<CORE_TAG>`) with `owner_audit: report` (§5) | Revert (§12) |
| 5 | Voters one at a time to `<ARBITER_TAG>`, followers first, leader last (§6) | Replace them back (§12) |
| 6 | Reads and holds, read-only (§7) | None needed |
| 7 | Monitoring on, with a proven delivery to `#alerts` (§8) | Revert the values commit (§12) |
| 8 | Report-mode soak, at least 24 hours per owner (§9) | None needed |
| 9 | Repair mode: indexer-b, then indexer-a (§10) | Back to report (§12) |
| 10 | End: the P0 exit criteria (§11) | None needed |

Nothing in this runbook changes consensus state: no Raft command, field, snapshot version or feature string changes (Plan S3-A contract §0), the leader proposes nothing new, and every component can return to its previous image (§12): the voters and verifiers to arbiter `v0.12.0`, both hosts to sentio-node `5d2f1695e33d911cb642bf60b49b71cdb74f62a0`. The reads (`GetPartitionStates`, `GetPromotionOutcomes`, `GetBlockVerification`) and the consensus holds answer only on a leader that runs `<ARBITER_TAG>`; until §6 has replaced the leader, both hosts' owner audits fall back to their own acknowledged inventory and count `fsm_unavailable` (clarification K3), and a consensus update would be refused by the new `arbiter-admin` unless it passed `--hold none` (§13.5). This runbook submits no consensus update.

Every command block is bash. Run them from the root of a production checkout at `origin/main`, in order, in one dedicated `bash` session started with `set -eo pipefail` (from fish, run `bash` first). Every value a later block needs is written under `$si_backup`, so a block also runs in a new session once §0 is defined. Never run two stages in one window. From §4 until §6 has passed, freeze every other change to `storage-integrity-si-v2` and to both hosts: no other sync and no pod deletion outside this runbook.

Every block that pushes to production `main`, syncs a release, applies or deletes a resource, deletes, scales or restarts a pod, copies a file into a pod, runs DDL or writes data needs explicit user confirmation in chat before it runs; each such block is preceded by the line `Confirm before running.`. Never re-run a confirmed block only to see its output: a re-run repeats its writes. Read-only checks sit in separate blocks that are safe to re-run, and both kinds `tee` their output into `$si_backup`; read that file instead.

Writes in this runbook: indexer-a's acceptance INSERTs into `devnet101.swap_new2` through indexer-a's sidecar, values `3001` to `3004`, one per step (`si_accept_a_track`, §0 of the stage-2 runbook; the later stage-3 runbooks take disjoint values, `4101` and up for the lockdown and `3101` and up for indexer-c); the `devuser1` owner's soak table `devuser1.s3_p0` through its own local agent, rows 1 to 3, dropped again in §11; the throwaway VMRule `storage-integrity-delivery-probe` of §8; the throwaway read-only tool `partstates`, copied to `/tmp` of the voters' arbiter containers (§1.3, §7); and, in repair mode only, the owner audit's own `DROP PART` of a resurrected `hg_safe` twin, which is irreversible per part and expected never to run on devnet2 (`sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_dropped_twins_total` stays 0). Retryable `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` windows are expected for indexer-a's tables in §5.1 and §10.2, and for indexer-b's in §5.2 and §10.1, while that host restarts; in repair mode a host also answers its tables Pending (733, retryable) after its restart until its startup audit has completed.

## 0. Session helpers

Define the helpers of §0 of [storage-integrity-devnet2-dynamic-table-set.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-dynamic-table-set.md), then those of §0 of [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md), then those of §0 of [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md), unchanged, then these. They replace `si_backup` and `R`, so the earlier evidence stays untouched, and `si_stage2_image`, which would otherwise read this runbook's pins:

```bash
si_backup="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p0"
R="$HOME/si-devnet2-multisource-s3a-rehearsal"
R_P0="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p0-rehearsal"
si_stage3_image() { # the stage-3 sentio-node image recorded in §1.1
  printf 'ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-%s@%s\n' "$(sed -n 3p "$si_backup/pins")" "$(sed -n 4p "$si_backup/pins")"
}
si_previous_image() { # the sentio-node image both hosts ran before this runbook (§1.1)
  printf 'ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-%s@%s\n' "$(sed -n 3p "$si_backup/previous-pins")" "$(sed -n 4p "$si_backup/previous-pins")"
}
si_stage2_image() { echo "si_stage2_image reads the stage-2 pins; this runbook uses si_stage3_image and si_previous_image" >&2; return 1; }
si_host() { # $1 a|b, then a command: runs it in that indexer's sentio-node container
  case "$1" in a|b) ;; *) echo "usage: si_host a|b <command>" >&2; return 1 ;; esac
  si_kubectl exec "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1-0" -c sentio-node -- "${@:2}"
}
si_host_started() { # $1 a|b: the sentio-node container's start time and restart count
  si_kubectl get pod "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1-0" -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="sentio-node")].state.running.startedAt} {.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="sentio-node")].restartCount}{"\n"}'
}
si_epoch() { jq -rn --arg t "$1" '$t | fromdate'; } # $1 an RFC 3339 UTC time such as 2026-10-15T03:21:00Z: seconds since the epoch
si_host_series() { # $1 a|b, $2 extended regexp of series names: those series of that host's embedded HouseGate registry (:9091); fails only when the endpoint cannot be read
  local m
  m="$(si_host "$1" wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9091/metrics)" || { echo "cannot read indexer-$1's :9091 metrics" >&2; return 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$m" | grep -E "^($2)(\\{[^}]*\\})? " || true
}
si_audit() { # $1 a|b: the six owner-audit series (Plan S3-A contract §5); none before the stage-3 image
  si_host_series "$1" 'sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_(mode|unclean_tables|runs_total|dropped_twins_total|clickhouse_restarts_total|fsm_unavailable_total)'
}
si_peer_refusals() { # $1 a|b: HouseGate's peer reserved-name refusals, one series per reason, pre-initialised at 0; none before the stage-3 image
  si_host_series "$1" 'storage_integrity_peer_reserved_name_refusals_total'
}
si_series_value() { # $1 one series exactly as printed (name and labels): its value, read from stdin, as an integer; fails when the series is absent
  awk -v s="$1" '$1 == s {printf "%.0f\n", $2; found = 1} END {if (!found) exit 1}'
}
si_voter_series() { # $1 voter ordinal, $2 extended regexp of series names: those series of that voter's /metrics
  local m
  m="$(si_arbiter "$1" wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics)" || { echo "cannot read arbiter-$1's metrics" >&2; return 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$m" | grep -E "^($2)(\\{[^}]*\\})? " || true
}
si_state_size() { # $1 voter ordinal: the state-size and snapshot series (Plan S3-A contract §4); none on v0.12.0
  si_voter_series "$1" 'arbiter_(state_bytes|state_component_bytes|snapshot_doc_bytes|snapshot_bytes|snapshot_doc_read_cap_bytes|snapshot_serialize_seconds|snapshot_persist_seconds|snapshot_restore_seconds|snapshot_install_seconds|snapshot_failures_total|raft_log_store_bytes|raft_snapshot_store_bytes)'
}
si_hold_metrics() { # $1 voter ordinal: the consensus-hold series; none on v0.12.0
  si_voter_series "$1" 'arbiter_consensus_hold_active|arbiter_consensus_holds_total|arbiter_consensus_hold_held_promotions_total'
}
si_reserved_preflight() { # $1 a|b|v1|v2|v3: every tenant database, table, view and column on that SI ClickHouse whose name or definition mentions a reserved name, one TSV row each
  local r="['hg_safe', 'hg_unsafe', 'hg_promote', 'hg_member_unsafe', 'hg_replica', 'hg_rstage', 'hg_xfer', '_hg_row_id']"
  local own="('system', 'INFORMATION_SCHEMA', 'information_schema', 'hg_safe', 'hg_unsafe', 'hg_promote')"
  local q="SELECT 'database', name FROM system.databases WHERE name NOT IN $own AND multiSearchAnyCaseInsensitive(name, $r)
    UNION ALL SELECT 'table', concat(database, '.', name) FROM system.tables WHERE database NOT IN $own AND (multiSearchAnyCaseInsensitive(name, $r) OR multiSearchAnyCaseInsensitive(create_table_query, $r))
    UNION ALL SELECT 'column', concat(database, '.', table, '.', name) FROM system.columns WHERE database NOT IN $own AND multiSearchAnyCaseInsensitive(name, $r)
    FORMAT TSV"
  case "$1" in
    a|b) si_source_ch "$1" "$q" ;;
    v1|v2|v3) si_verifier_ch "${1#v}" "$q" ;;
    *) echo "usage: si_reserved_preflight a|b|v1|v2|v3" >&2; return 1 ;;
  esac
}
si_partstates_build() { # local only: builds $si_backup/tools/partstates for linux/amd64 from arbiter-core CORE_TAG (§1.1), with the source below
  local core tag src
  core="$(sed -n 2p "$si_backup/repos")"; tag="$(sed -n 5p "$si_backup/pins")"
  [ -n "$core" ] && [ -n "$tag" ] || { echo "run §1.1 first" >&2; return 1; }
  src="$(mktemp -d)"
  git -C "$core" fetch -q --tags origin || return 1
  git -C "$core" archive "$tag" | tar -x -C "$src" || return 1
  mkdir -p "$src/cmd/partstates" "$si_backup/tools" || return 1
  python3 -I - docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md "$src/cmd/partstates/main.go" <<'EOF' || return 1
import re, sys
blocks = re.findall(r"```go\n(.*?)```", open(sys.argv[1]).read(), re.S)
assert len(blocks) == 1, "the runbook must hold exactly one go block, the partstates source"
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write(blocks[0])
EOF
  (cd "$src" && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.3+auto CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false go build -trimpath -o "$si_backup/tools/partstates" ./cmd/partstates) || return 1
  cp "$src/cmd/partstates/main.go" "$si_backup/tools/partstates.go" && rm -rf "$src"
  shasum -a 256 "$si_backup/tools/partstates"
}
si_partstates_put() { # a write, only in a confirmed block: copies the tool to /tmp/partstates in every voter's arbiter container and checks each copy; a replaced or restarted voter loses its copy
  local sum i
  [ -x "$si_backup/tools/partstates" ] || { echo "build the tool first (§1.3)" >&2; return 1; }
  sum="$(shasum -a 256 "$si_backup/tools/partstates" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  for i in 0 1 2; do
    si_kubectl exec -i "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-$i" -c arbiter -- sh -c 'cat > /tmp/partstates.new && chmod 700 /tmp/partstates.new && mv /tmp/partstates.new /tmp/partstates' < "$si_backup/tools/partstates" || return 1
    [ "$(si_arbiter "$i" sha256sum /tmp/partstates | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$sum" ] || { echo "arbiter-$i: /tmp/partstates is not $sum" >&2; return 1; }
    echo "arbiter-$i: /tmp/partstates $sum"
  done
}
si_partstates_run() { # the tool's arguments: runs the copy in the current leader's arbiter container against every voter's data-plane listener; refuses when that copy is missing or stale (it never copies)
  local l sum peers i
  [ -x "$si_backup/tools/partstates" ] || { echo "build the tool first (§1.3)" >&2; return 1; }
  l="$(si_leader)" || { echo "no leader answers" >&2; return 1; }
  sum="$(shasum -a 256 "$si_backup/tools/partstates" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  [ "$(si_arbiter "$l" sh -c 'sha256sum /tmp/partstates 2>/dev/null | cut -d" " -f1')" = "$sum" ] || { echo "arbiter-$l holds no current copy of partstates (a replaced or restarted voter): run si_partstates_put again in a confirmed block of its own (§1.3)" >&2; return 1; }
  peers=""
  for i in 0 1 2; do peers="$peers,storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-$i=$(si_voter "$i")"; done
  si_arbiter "$l" /tmp/partstates -peers "${peers#,}" "$@"
}
si_partstates() { # $1 a|b: one JSON line per partition of a table that owner holds (indexer-a is SI indexer 0, indexer-b is 1), with the FSM's partition state (GetPartitionStates); a table without partition state and the summary on stderr
  case "$1" in
    a) si_partstates_run -indexer 0 ;;
    b) si_partstates_run -indexer 1 ;;
    *) echo "usage: si_partstates a|b" >&2; return 1 ;;
  esac
}
si_registry_names() { si_partstates_run -registry; } # one JSON line per table-registry incarnation: database_id, table, status, origin, owner
si_active_tables() { # $1 a|b: the Active tables that owner holds, one <database>.<table> per line, from the table registry
  local id
  case "$1" in a) id=0 ;; b) id=1 ;; *) echo "usage: si_active_tables a|b" >&2; return 1 ;; esac
  si_registry_names | jq -r --argjson id "$id" 'select(.status == "active" and .owner == $id) | "\(.database_id).\(.table)"' | sort -u
}
si_unpromoted() { # $1 a|b, $2 that owner's si_partstates output, $3 a promotion sequence: the owner's Active tables none of whose partitions has an acknowledged promotion above it
  local t tables
  tables="$(si_active_tables "$1")" || return 1
  for t in $tables; do
    jq -e --arg t "$t" --argjson seq "$3" 'select(.table_id == $t and .last_acked_promotion_seq > $seq)' "$2" >/dev/null || echo "$t"
  done
}
si_vm_query() { # $1 PromQL: one instant query against VictoriaMetrics (vmsingle-vm in monitoring), from inside arbiter-0; prints the JSON answer
  local q
  q="$(jq -rn --arg q "$1" '$q | @uri')"
  si_arbiter 0 wget -qO- "http://vmsingle-vm.monitoring.svc:8429/api/v1/query?query=$q"
}
si_vm_value() { si_vm_query "$1" | jq -r '.data.result[0].value[1] // "none"'; } # $1 PromQL: the first sample's value, or none
si_vmalert_groups() { # the rule groups vmalert (vmalert-vm in monitoring) loaded for this network: one JSON line per group with each rule's health
  local m
  m="$(si_arbiter 0 wget -qO- http://vmalert-vm.monitoring.svc:8080/api/v1/rules)" || { echo "vmalert does not answer from arbiter-0" >&2; return 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$m" | jq -c '.data.groups[] | select(.name | startswith("storage-integrity-")) | {group: .name, rules: [.rules[] | {name, type, health, lastError}]}'
}
si_head_is() { # the files HEAD changes, in any order: fails unless HEAD is one commit on origin/main that changes exactly them (both lists sorted bytewise, LC_ALL=C, whatever the session's locale)
  local got want
  git fetch -q origin main || return 1
  [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" ] || { echo "HEAD is not one commit on origin/main" >&2; return 1; }
  got="$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' ' ')"
  want="$(printf '%s\n' "$@" | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' ' ')"
  [ "$got" = "$want" ] || { echo "HEAD changes ${got% }, not ${want% }" >&2; return 1; }
}
si_revert_stage3() { # $1 commit file under $si_backup, $2 release, $3 optional rollout target: reverts that commit on origin/main, tests, pushes, syncs and waits; after a push it only syncs and waits again
  local f="$si_backup/$1" c
  [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no $1: nothing to revert"; return 0; }
  if [ -f "$f.reverted" ]; then
    echo "$1 is reverted on main already ($(cat "$f.reverted")): syncing only"
  else
    git fetch -q origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main || return 1
    c="$(cat "$f")"; git show --stat "$c" || return 1
    git revert --no-edit "$c" || { git revert --abort; echo "reverting $1 conflicts with a later commit on main: aborted, nothing changed (§12 names the order)" >&2; return 1; }
    python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py || return 1
    git push origin HEAD:main || return 1
    git rev-parse HEAD > "$f.reverted"
  fi
  helmfile -f k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml sync --selector "name=$2" || return 1
  [ -z "${3:-}" ] || si_kubectl rollout status "$3" --timeout=15m
}
```

`si_audit`, `si_peer_refusals`, `si_state_size` and `si_hold_metrics` print nothing for a component that does not export the series yet (the previous images export none of them) and fail only when the metrics endpoint cannot be read. `si_partstates`, `si_registry_names`, `si_active_tables` and `si_unpromoted` run the throwaway tool `partstates` (never committed) inside the leader's arbiter container. Copying it there writes into the voters' containers, so `si_partstates_put` runs only in a confirmed block of its own (§1.3, and §7 after the voters were replaced); `si_partstates_run` never copies and refuses when the leader's copy is missing or stale, for example after a voter restarted, until that block has run again. The arbiter's data-plane listener (`grpc_listen`, port 7080 on every voter, which the chart also uses for administration because it sets no `consensus_admin.listen`) is plaintext gRPC without authentication, like every data-plane client's connection; each `SafeState` read crosses one leader read barrier and a follower answers with the leader's id, which arbiter-core's `dataplane.Client` follows. The tool is that client, built from `CORE_TAG`'s arbiter-core (`dataplane.Client.GetPartitionStates`, `wire.TableRegistrySnapshotFromPB`), so it checks every answer exactly as the owner audit's own client does. It reads the table registry, takes every table whose newest incarnation with `hg_*` tables is owned by the given SI indexer, and prints one JSON line per partition the FSM holds state for (`table_id`, `partition_id`, `last_acked_promotion_seq`, `inventory_unrefreshed`, the table's `database_id`, `table`, `incarnation` and `status`, and the rest of the partition's state): a partition is listed only once an applied acknowledgement reached it (Plan S3-A contract §4), so a table never promoted prints no line, only a `no partition state` line on stderr. The checks that every Active table was promoted therefore take the Active tables from the registry (`si_active_tables`) and compare (`si_unpromoted`). It writes nothing. Its source, which `si_partstates_build` extracts from this file (the only go block here) into a `git archive` export of arbiter-core at `CORE_TAG` and builds for linux/amd64 (the voters' platform; the arbiter image is glibc-based, which the binary's purego dependency needs):

```go
// partstates is the throwaway reader of docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md
// (production), never committed. si_partstates_build compiles it from a
// git archive export of arbiter-core at CORE_TAG, as cmd/partstates/main.go,
// for linux/amd64, and si_partstates_run copies it into the leader's arbiter
// container and runs it there against the voters' data-plane listeners
// (grpc_listen :7080, plaintext gRPC like every data-plane client).
//
// It reads the leader's table registry (TableRegistry.GetTableRegistry) and,
// for every table one SI indexer owns, the FSM's partition states through
// arbiter-core's dataplane.Client.GetPartitionStates (housegate spec
// 2026-10-14 §14; plan S3-A contract §3), and prints one JSON line per
// partition on stdout (plan S3-B contract §9), one stderr line per owned
// table the FSM holds no partition state for, and a summary on stderr. With
// -registry it prints one JSON line per registry incarnation instead: the
// logical names the reserved-name preflight checks, and the owner and status
// the runbook's "every Active table" checks read. It writes nothing anywhere.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"
	"google.golang.org/grpc"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/emptypb"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// partitionLine is one partition the FSM holds state for (a partition is
// listed only once an applied acknowledgement reached it), of a table the
// indexer owns: the table's newest incarnation with hg_* tables in the
// registry, the read's promotion sequence and safe block, then the proto
// field names of PartitionStateEntry with the safe parts by name.
type partitionLine struct {
	IndexerID             uint64   `json:"indexer_id"`
	TableID               string   `json:"table_id"`
	DatabaseID            string   `json:"database_id"`
	Table                 string   `json:"table"`
	Incarnation           uint64   `json:"incarnation"`
	Status                string   `json:"status"`
	PromotionSeq          uint64   `json:"promotion_seq"`
	SafeBlockSeq          uint64   `json:"safe_block_seq"`
	PartitionID           string   `json:"partition_id"`
	BaseSafeSnapshotID    string   `json:"base_safe_snapshot_id"`
	BasePartitionRoot     string   `json:"base_partition_root"`
	PublishSeq            uint64   `json:"publish_seq"`
	SafeParts             []string `json:"safe_parts"`
	PromotedUnsafeParts   int      `json:"promoted_unsafe_parts"`
	UnackedPromotionSeq   uint64   `json:"unacked_promotion_seq"`
	LastAckedPromotionSeq uint64   `json:"last_acked_promotion_seq"`
	InventoryUnrefreshed  bool     `json:"inventory_unrefreshed"`
}

// registryLine is one incarnation of the table registry.
type registryLine struct {
	Incarnation uint64 `json:"incarnation"`
	DatabaseID  string `json:"database_id"`
	Table       string `json:"table"`
	Status      string `json:"status"`
	Origin      string `json:"origin"`
	Owner       uint64 `json:"owner"`
}

func main() {
	peers := flag.String("peers", "", "every voter as id=host:port, comma-separated")
	indexer := flag.Int("indexer", -1, "the SI indexer whose tables to read")
	registry := flag.Bool("registry", false, "print every registry incarnation instead")
	timeout := flag.Duration("timeout", 2*time.Minute, "deadline of the whole run")
	flag.Parse()
	if err := run(*peers, *indexer, *registry, *timeout); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "partstates:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func parsePeers(list string) ([]dataplane.Peer, error) {
	var out []dataplane.Peer
	for _, item := range strings.Split(list, ",") {
		id, addr, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(item), "=")
		if !ok || id == "" || addr == "" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("-peers entry %q is not id=host:port", item)
		}
		out = append(out, dataplane.Peer{ID: id, GRPCAddr: addr})
	}
	return out, nil
}

func run(peerList string, indexer int, registry bool, timeout time.Duration) error {
	if peerList == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("-peers is required")
	}
	if registry == (indexer >= 0) {
		return fmt.Errorf("pass exactly one of -indexer N and -registry")
	}
	peers, err := parsePeers(peerList)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	c, err := dataplane.New(dataplane.Config{Peers: peers})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer c.Close()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeout)
	defer cancel()

	var snap wire.TableRegistrySnapshot
	err = c.WithLeaderRetry(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, conn *grpc.ClientConn) error {
		m, err := pb.NewTableRegistryClient(conn).GetTableRegistry(ctx, &emptypb.Empty{})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		snap, err = wire.TableRegistrySnapshotFromPB(m)
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("GetTableRegistry: %w", err)
	}
	enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)

	if registry {
		for _, inc := range snap.Incarnations {
			if err := enc.Encode(registryLine{
				Incarnation: inc.Seq, DatabaseID: inc.DatabaseID, Table: inc.TableID,
				Status: string(inc.Status), Origin: string(inc.Origin), Owner: snap.Owner(inc),
			}); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "partstates: registry version %d: %d incarnations\n", snap.Version, len(snap.Incarnations))
		return nil
	}

	// The newest incarnation with hg_* tables per table id; the FSM keys
	// partition state by table id, so one read covers every incarnation.
	owned := map[string]wire.TableIncarnation{}
	for _, inc := range snap.Incarnations {
		if inc.HasPhysicalTables() && snap.Owner(inc) == uint64(indexer) {
			owned[inc.Key()] = inc
		}
	}
	keys := make([]string, 0, len(owned))
	for key := range owned {
		keys = append(keys, key)
	}
	sort.Strings(keys)

	partitions, unrefreshed, stateless := 0, 0, 0
	for _, key := range keys {
		inc := owned[key]
		st, err := c.GetPartitionStates(ctx, wire.PartitionStatesQuery{TableID: key})
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("GetPartitionStates %s: %w", key, err)
		}
		if len(st.Partitions) == 0 {
			stateless++
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "partstates: %s (%s, incarnation %d): no partition state\n", key, inc.Status, inc.Seq)
			continue
		}
		for _, p := range st.Partitions {
			names := make([]string, 0, len(p.SafeParts))
			for _, part := range p.SafeParts {
				names = append(names, part.PartName)
			}
			if err := enc.Encode(partitionLine{
				IndexerID: uint64(indexer), TableID: key, DatabaseID: inc.DatabaseID, Table: inc.TableID,
				Incarnation: inc.Seq, Status: string(inc.Status),
				PromotionSeq: st.PromotionSeq, SafeBlockSeq: st.SafeWatermark.SafeBlockSeq,
				PartitionID: p.PartitionID, BaseSafeSnapshotID: p.BaseSafeSnapshotID, BasePartitionRoot: p.BasePartitionRoot,
				PublishSeq: p.PublishSeq, SafeParts: names, PromotedUnsafeParts: len(p.PromotedUnsafePartRowLtHashes),
				UnackedPromotionSeq: p.UnackedPromotionSeq, LastAckedPromotionSeq: p.LastAckedPromotionSeq,
				InventoryUnrefreshed: p.InventoryUnrefreshed,
			}); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			partitions++
			if p.InventoryUnrefreshed {
				unrefreshed++
			}
		}
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "partstates: indexer %d: %d tables, %d partitions, %d with inventory_unrefreshed, %d tables without partition state\n",
		indexer, len(keys), partitions, unrefreshed, stateless)
	return nil
}
```

`si_vm_query` and `si_vmalert_groups` read VictoriaMetrics and vmalert through their in-cluster Services from arbiter-0 (the namespace has no NetworkPolicy); §8 checks first that both answer. `si_head_is` guards every pin commit, and `si_revert_stage3` is every revert of §12: it marks a pushed revert in `<commit file>.reverted`, so a block whose sync or rollout failed after the push only syncs and waits when it runs again.

## 1. Preparation

### 1.1 Pins

| Component | Pin | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arbiter voters and verifiers | `ghcr.io/sentioxyz/arbiter:<ARBITER_TAG>@<ARBITER_DIGEST>` (arbiter-core `<CORE_TAG>`, arbiter-proto `<PROTO_TAG>`, housegate `<HG_TAG>`) | arbiter release workflow (Plan S3-A Task 11); `docker buildx imagetools inspect`: OCI revision equals the tag's commit |
| sentio-node, indexer-a and indexer-b | `ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-<SN_COMMIT>@<SN_DIGEST>` (housegate `<HG_TAG>`, arbiter-core `<CORE_TAG>`, arbiter-proto `<PROTO_TAG>`) | main CI `docker-push` (Plan S3-B Task 12); OCI revision equals `<SN_COMMIT>`; index digest from `docker buildx imagetools inspect` |
| In-pod rewriter, both indexers | unchanged: `us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/sentio-352722/sentio/housegate-rewriter:0.17.0@sha256:b3b227fa4a28bd9dcd5d3d6aa172890ff66d7bf60e1c7039428efe4dabebb50a` | stage-1 runbook §1.1; `<HG_TAG>` changes no rewriter pin (Plan S3-A Tasks 1 and 2), and the embedded HouseGate refuses an incompatible rewriter at startup, so a Ready pod in §5 proves it |
| Agent sidecar, both indexers | unchanged: `ghcr.io/housegate/housegate:v0.15.0@sha256:1b51de76b7b7a15a8006d0ac06febb10012c74c92d4950d07e4e5a5b77b3570f` | stage-1 runbook §1.1 |

Before this upgrade the voters and verifiers run arbiter `v0.12.0` (`sha256:14ac64030e49de64afcd7387a2a6a99bf1588bc47e9ea5fbff56ece20f97fe70`) and both indexers run sentio-node `5d2f1695e33d911cb642bf60b49b71cdb74f62a0` (`sha256:be730c40d68e3de49d0d33c736a001a305b089ef11d1a81f0e883d804e15abaa`, HouseGate `v0.19.0`, arbiter-core `v0.14.1`), as `$HOME/si-devnet2-multisource-tracks/pins` records; those are the rollback targets of §12. Both stay valid ways back because nothing here changes consensus state: `v0.12.0` restores the v20 snapshots `<ARBITER_TAG>` writes (§3), and sentio-node `5d2f1695e33d911cb642bf60b49b71cdb74f62a0` ignores the `acked_safe_inventories` the stage-3 SNode adds to its `state.json` and the `owner_audit` key it does not know.

Set the three local clones (any clone with the release tags; the blocks only fetch from them and read), then:

```bash
ARBITER_TAG='<ARBITER_TAG>'; ARBITER_DIGEST='<ARBITER_DIGEST>'; SN_COMMIT='<SN_COMMIT>'; SN_DIGEST='<SN_DIGEST>'
CORE_TAG='<CORE_TAG>'; HG_TAG='<HG_TAG>'; PROTO_TAG='<PROTO_TAG>'
arbiter_repo=/path/to/arbiter; arbiter_core_repo=/path/to/arbiter-core; sentio_node_repo=/path/to/sentio-node
case "$ARBITER_TAG$ARBITER_DIGEST$SN_COMMIT$SN_DIGEST$CORE_TAG$HG_TAG$PROTO_TAG" in *'<'*) echo "pins are still placeholders; stop"; exit 1;; esac
for r in "$arbiter_repo" "$arbiter_core_repo" "$sentio_node_repo"; do
  git -C "$r" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "set arbiter_repo, arbiter_core_repo and sentio_node_repo to local clones first ($r is none)"; exit 1; }
done
if [ -e "$si_backup" ]; then
  # Created fresh for this run, here or just before by whoever runs it (mode 700): it may hold their own tools, never an earlier run's evidence.
  [ -d "$si_backup" ] && [ -n "$(find "$si_backup" -maxdepth 0 -perm 700)" ] || { echo "$si_backup is not a directory of mode 700: stop"; exit 1; }
  [ -f "$si_backup/pins" ] || [ -z "$(cd "$si_backup" && ls -d stage3-*-commit restart-* voter-order* replay-baseline preflight-reserved-* 2>/dev/null)" ] || { echo "$si_backup holds an earlier run's evidence without its pins: move it aside; si_backup is created fresh for each run"; exit 1; }
else
  mkdir -m 700 "$si_backup"
fi
git -C "$arbiter_repo" fetch -q --tags origin; git -C "$arbiter_core_repo" fetch -q --tags origin; git -C "$sentio_node_repo" fetch -q origin
deps() { awk '$1 == "github.com/housegate/housegate" || $1 == "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core" || $1 == "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto" {print $1, $2}' | sort | tr '\n' ' '; }
want="github.com/housegate/housegate $HG_TAG github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core $CORE_TAG github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto $PROTO_TAG "
[ "$(git -C "$arbiter_repo" show "$ARBITER_TAG:go.mod" | deps)" = "$want" ] || { echo "$ARBITER_TAG does not pin exactly $want"; exit 1; }
[ "$(git -C "$sentio_node_repo" show "$SN_COMMIT:go.mod" | deps)" = "$want" ] || { echo "sentio-node $SN_COMMIT does not pin exactly $want"; exit 1; }
git -C "$arbiter_core_repo" rev-parse -q --verify "$CORE_TAG^{commit}" >/dev/null || { echo "arbiter-core has no tag $CORE_TAG"; exit 1; }
[ "$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/arbiter:$ARBITER_TAG" | sed -n 's/^Digest: *//p')" = "$ARBITER_DIGEST" ] || { echo "the arbiter image digest is not $ARBITER_DIGEST"; exit 1; }
[ "$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-$SN_COMMIT" | sed -n 's/^Digest: *//p')" = "$SN_DIGEST" ] || { echo "the sentio-node image digest is not $SN_DIGEST"; exit 1; }
python3 -I -B - "$SN_COMMIT" "$SN_DIGEST" <<'EOF'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "charts/storage-integrity/tests")
import test_render as t
image = "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-%s@%s" % (sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
assert t.DEVNET2_STAGE3_SOURCE_IMAGE == image, t.DEVNET2_STAGE3_SOURCE_IMAGE
assert image in t.STAGE3_HOST_IMAGES and image in t.WRITER_AUTHORIZATION_IMAGES, "the stage-3 image is not reviewed"
print("test_render.py lists the stage-3 image in STAGE3_HOST_IMAGES and WRITER_AUTHORIZATION_IMAGES")
EOF
prev="$HOME/si-devnet2-multisource-tracks/pins"
[ "$(sed -n 1,4p "$prev" | tr '\n' ' ')" = "v0.12.0 sha256:14ac64030e49de64afcd7387a2a6a99bf1588bc47e9ea5fbff56ece20f97fe70 5d2f1695e33d911cb642bf60b49b71cdb74f62a0 sha256:be730c40d68e3de49d0d33c736a001a305b089ef11d1a81f0e883d804e15abaa " ] || { echo "$prev does not hold the stage-2 pins this runbook rolls back to; stop"; exit 1; }
printf '%s\n' "$ARBITER_TAG" "$ARBITER_DIGEST" "$SN_COMMIT" "$SN_DIGEST" "$CORE_TAG" "$HG_TAG" "$PROTO_TAG" > "$si_backup/pins.new"
if [ -f "$si_backup/pins" ] && ! cmp -s "$si_backup/pins.new" "$si_backup/pins"; then echo "$si_backup/pins records other pins: stop"; exit 1; fi
mv "$si_backup/pins.new" "$si_backup/pins"
sed -n 1,4p "$prev" > "$si_backup/previous-pins"
printf '%s\n' "$arbiter_repo" "$arbiter_core_repo" "$sentio_node_repo" > "$si_backup/repos"
echo "pins resolve"
```

Expected: `test_render.py lists the stage-3 image in STAGE3_HOST_IMAGES and WRITER_AUTHORIZATION_IMAGES` and `pins resolve`. `$si_backup/pins` holds, one per line, `ARBITER_TAG`, `ARBITER_DIGEST`, `SN_COMMIT`, `SN_DIGEST`, `CORE_TAG`, `HG_TAG`, `PROTO_TAG`; `$si_backup/previous-pins` the four stage-2 pins; `$si_backup/repos` the three clones.

## 2. Reserved-name preflight

HouseGate `<HG_TAG>`, embedded in sentio-node `<SN_COMMIT>`, refuses on every peer-trusted, non-forwarded session (the rewriter's `remote()` loopback legs between the two hosts) any mention of a reserved database (`hg_safe`, `hg_unsafe`, `hg_promote`, `hg_member_unsafe`, `hg_replica`, `hg_rstage`, `hg_xfer`) or of the row-id column `_hg_row_id`, string literals included, with code 392 (Plan S3-A contract §2). A tenant object whose name or definition carries one of them would become unreadable across indexers the moment §5 starts. Before any `<HG_TAG>` image reaches a host, every SI ClickHouse (indexer-a's source and the three verifiers of the network installation, indexer-b's source) and the table registry's logical names must be free of them; the protocol databases themselves and ClickHouse's own are excluded. Read-only:

```bash
{
  for h in a b v1 v2 v3; do
    si_reserved_preflight "$h" > "$si_backup/preflight-reserved-$h.tsv"
    echo "$h: $(wc -l < "$si_backup/preflight-reserved-$h.tsv" | tr -d ' ') rows"
    cat "$si_backup/preflight-reserved-$h.tsv"
  done
  si_registry_names > "$si_backup/registry-names.jsonl"
  jq -r '[.database_id, .table, .status] | @tsv' "$si_backup/registry-names.jsonl" | grep -i -E 'hg_(safe|unsafe|promote|member_unsafe|replica|rstage|xfer)|_hg_row_id' > "$si_backup/preflight-reserved-registry.tsv" || true
  echo "registry: $(wc -l < "$si_backup/registry-names.jsonl" | tr -d ' ') incarnations, $(wc -l < "$si_backup/preflight-reserved-registry.tsv" | tr -d ' ') rows"
  cat "$si_backup/preflight-reserved-registry.tsv"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/preflight-reserved.txt"
```

Expected: `0 rows` for `a`, `b`, `v1`, `v2` and `v3`, and `registry: <n> incarnations, 0 rows` with `partstates: registry version <v>: <n> incarnations` (the registry holds every SI and ordinary table of both indexers). Any row: stop. The object's owner renames or drops it first; this runbook has no workaround, and §5 must not start while a row remains.

## 3. Offline replay check

Plan S3-A Task 11's throwaway tools restore a copy of each voter's `raft` directory into one arbiter build: `statedigest` hashes the state after applying every logged command (one `key <member> <sha256>` line per member of the written snapshot document), `snapdump` writes the snapshot container the build then writes, and `v20check` restores one container and prints its version byte and the outcome. `old` is the voters' live release, `v0.12.0`; `new` is `<ARBITER_TAG>`. Neither tool is committed anywhere. Identical lines and an identical container prove on devnet2's own log that the new release changes no consensus byte (Plan S3-A contract §0), and each build's restore of the other's container proves the way back.

### 3.1 Rehearsal binaries

The binaries are Plan S3-A Task 11's, in `$R`, read only: `bin/old` built from the tag `$R/old_tag.txt` names, `bin/new` from `<ARBITER_TAG>`. They are reused only while `old` is still the voters' live release; otherwise the second block rebuilds both into `$R_P0` (`$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p0-rehearsal`) from the same tool sources, and `$R` stays untouched. Local only (one image inspect):

```bash
{
  ARBITER_TAG="$(sed -n 1p "$si_backup/pins")"; ARBITER_DIGEST="$(sed -n 2p "$si_backup/pins")"
  for b in old new; do for t in statedigest v20check snapdump; do [ -x "$R/bin/$b/$t" ] || { echo "missing $R/bin/$b/$t: Plan S3-A Task 11 Step 13 did not run; stop"; exit 1; }; done; done
  [ "$(sed -n 1p "$R/arbiter-release")" = "$ARBITER_TAG" ] && [ "$(sed -n 2p "$R/arbiter-release")" = "$ARBITER_DIGEST" ] || { echo "\$R/arbiter-release does not name $ARBITER_TAG $ARBITER_DIGEST; stop"; exit 1; }
  old_tag="$(cat "$R/old_tag.txt")"
  live="$(si_images | awk '$1 ~ /^storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-/ {sub(/.*@/, "", $3); print $3}' | sort -u)"
  old_digest="$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/arbiter:$old_tag" | sed -n 's/^Digest: *//p')"
  echo "old_tag $old_tag ($old_digest); voters run $live"
  if [ -n "$live" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$live" | wc -l)" -eq 1 ] && [ "$live" = "$old_digest" ]; then
    echo "$R/bin" > "$si_backup/replay-bin"
    echo "\$R's old build is the voters' live release: reuse \$R"
  else
    echo "\$R's old build is not the voters' live release: rebuild with the next block"
  fi
  shasum -a 256 "$R"/bin/old/* "$R"/bin/new/*
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/replay-tools.txt"
```

Expected: `old_tag v0.12.0 (sha256:14ac6403…); voters run sha256:14ac6403…`, `$R's old build is the voters' live release: reuse $R`, and six checksums. Only when the block says to rebuild, run this one, with `OLD_TAG` set to the voters' live release (local only; `arbiter_repo` from §1.1):

```bash
OLD_TAG='v0.12.0'
ARBITER_TAG="$(sed -n 1p "$si_backup/pins")"; arbiter_repo="$(sed -n 1p "$si_backup/repos")"
[ ! -e "$R_P0" ] || { echo "$R_P0 exists: move it aside; a rehearsal directory is never reused"; exit 1; }
mkdir -m 700 "$R_P0"
git -C "$arbiter_repo" fetch -q --tags origin
for build in "old $OLD_TAG" "new $ARBITER_TAG"; do
  b="${build%% *}"; tag="${build#* }"; src="$R_P0/src/$b"
  mkdir -p "$src" "$R_P0/bin/$b"
  git -C "$arbiter_repo" archive "$tag" | tar -x -C "$src"
  for tool in statedigest v20check snapdump; do mkdir -p "$src/cmd/$tool" && cp "$R/$tool/main.go" "$src/cmd/$tool/main.go"; done
  (cd "$src" && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.3+auto GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false go build -o "$R_P0/bin/$b/" ./cmd/statedigest ./cmd/v20check ./cmd/snapdump)
done
echo "$OLD_TAG" > "$R_P0/old_tag.txt"
echo "$R_P0/bin" > "$si_backup/replay-bin"
ls "$R_P0/bin/old" "$R_P0/bin/new"
```

Expected: both directories list `snapdump`, `statedigest` and `v20check`.

### 3.2 Baseline

Re-measure the voters' live build: a stale `old` binary compares the wrong build and proves nothing. Every voter must run one image, the published digest of the release the chosen `old_tag.txt` names; the check records the verified baseline in `$si_backup/replay-baseline`, which §3.3 requires:

```bash
{
  bin="$(cat "$si_backup/replay-bin")" || { echo "run §3.1 first"; exit 1; }
  old_tag="$(cat "$(dirname "$bin")/old_tag.txt")"
  live="$(si_images | awk '$1 ~ /^storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-/ {sub(/.*@/, "", $3); print $3}' | sort -u)"
  echo "old_tag $old_tag; voters run $live"
  [ -n "$live" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$live" | wc -l)" -eq 1 ] || { echo "the voters do not run exactly one image; stop"; exit 1; }
  old_digest="$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/arbiter:$old_tag" | sed -n 's/^Digest: *//p')"
  [ "$live" = "$old_digest" ] || { echo "the voters run $live, but $old_tag is $old_digest: rerun §3.1"; exit 1; }
  printf '%s %s %s\n' "$old_tag" "$live" "$bin" > "$si_backup/replay-baseline"
  echo "old matches the voters' live release $old_tag"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/replay-baseline.txt"
```

Expected: `old_tag v0.12.0; voters run sha256:14ac64030e49de64afcd7387a2a6a99bf1588bc47e9ea5fbff56ece20f97fe70` and `old matches the voters' live release v0.12.0`. Never continue to §3.3 without the success line.

### 3.3 Replay

The replay loads each voter's `arbiter.yaml` with arbiter's `config.Load`, which requires `anchor.evm.private_key_hex`; in the pods it comes from `ARBITER_ANCHOR_EVM_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX`, so the block exports a throwaway random key (the offline replay signs nothing). Fresh copies of all three voters, local CPU only:

```bash
{
  read -r base_tag base_digest bin < "$si_backup/replay-baseline" || { echo "run the baseline check of §3.2 first"; exit 1; }
  [ "$(cat "$(dirname "$bin")/old_tag.txt")" = "$base_tag" ] || { echo "the old build no longer names $base_tag: rerun §3.2"; exit 1; }
  [ "$(si_images | awk '$1 ~ /^storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-/ {sub(/.*@/, "", $3); print $3}' | sort -u)" = "$base_digest" ] || { echo "the voters no longer run $base_digest: rerun §3.2"; exit 1; }
  ARBITER_ANCHOR_EVM_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"; export ARBITER_ANCHOR_EVM_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX  # config.Load needs one; the offline replay signs nothing
  si_show | tee "$si_backup/show-replay.json" | jq -c '{epoch, params_digest, promotion_seq}'
  for i in 0 1 2; do
    si_kubectl exec "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-$i" -c arbiter -- tar -C /data -czf - raft > "$si_backup/arbiter-$i-raft.tgz"
    si_kubectl exec "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-$i" -c arbiter -- cat /config/arbiter.yaml > "$si_backup/arbiter-$i.yaml"
    work="$(mktemp -d)"
    tar -C "$work" -xzf "$si_backup/arbiter-$i-raft.tgz"
    for v in old new; do
      out="$si_backup/digest-$i-$v"
      "$bin/$v/statedigest" -data-dir "$work/raft" -config "$si_backup/arbiter-$i.yaml" > "$out.txt" 2> "$out.err" || { echo "statedigest $v failed for arbiter-$i (a raft.db that fails to open is a torn copy; re-copy):"; cat "$out.err"; exit 1; }
      grep -E '^(snapshot_index|last_index|applied_commands|rejected_commands|written_version|genesis_configured|live_check|apply_error|apply_rejected|key|spent_ids|snapshot_sha256)' "$out.txt" > "$out.cmp"
      if grep -q '^apply_error ' "$out.txt"; then echo "arbiter-$i $v: apply_error"; exit 1; fi
      grep -q '^key tracks ' "$out.txt" || { echo "arbiter-$i $v: no tracks state after the tracks activation"; exit 1; }
      "$bin/$v/snapdump" -data-dir "$work/raft" -config "$si_backup/arbiter-$i.yaml" -out "$si_backup/written-$i-$v.container" || { echo "snapdump $v failed for arbiter-$i"; exit 1; }
    done
    if cmp -s "$si_backup/digest-$i-old.cmp" "$si_backup/digest-$i-new.cmp"; then
      echo "arbiter-$i: old and new replay identically"
    else
      echo "arbiter-$i: DIFFERENT; stop"; diff "$si_backup/digest-$i-old.cmp" "$si_backup/digest-$i-new.cmp"; exit 1
    fi
    cmp -s "$si_backup/written-$i-old.container" "$si_backup/written-$i-new.container" || { echo "arbiter-$i: the containers differ; stop"; exit 1; }
    echo "arbiter-$i: both builds write the same v20 container"
    "$bin/old/v20check" "$si_backup/written-$i-new.container"
    "$bin/new/v20check" "$si_backup/written-$i-old.container"
    grep -E '^(applied_commands|written_version|live_check)' "$si_backup/digest-$i-new.txt"
    rm -rf "$work"
  done
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/replay.txt"
```

Expected, for each voter: `wrote …: <n> bytes, version 20` twice with the same `<n>` (11868827 for the stage-2 copy at promotion 54; more now), `old and new replay identically`, `both builds write the same v20 container`, `restore_ok version 20` twice (`v0.12.0` restores what `<ARBITER_TAG>` writes and back), `applied_commands` above zero, `written_version 20`, and `live_check network_id=devnet2 genesis_snapshot_id=0x63700cf1… epoch=5 params_digest=<show-replay.json> promotion_seq=<show-replay.json, or later if a promotion landed between the read and the copy>` plus `live_check next_l3_block_seq=<n> safe_block_seq=<m>`; no `apply_error`. Any difference, a `snapshot_sha256` difference included: stop before §4; the release changed a consensus byte.

## 5. SNodes in report mode

Both SI indexers move to sentio-node `<SN_COMMIT>`, indexer-a first, each with `storageIntegrity.snode.ownerAudit: report` in the same commit (`test_owner_audit_needs_a_reviewed_image` sets the key only on a host whose pinned image is in `STAGE3_HOST_IMAGES`). The image embeds HouseGate `<HG_TAG>` (the peer reserved-name guard of §2) and arbiter-core `<CORE_TAG>`: its SNode audits its `hg_safe` partitions at startup, before every promotion's shadow build and after every ClickHouse restart, against the newer of its own acknowledged inventory and the FSM's `SafeParts`. In report mode it logs an unclean partition at error level (`owner audit: hg_safe partition is unclean`) and counts it, but never drops a part and never holds a table (clarification K1). Until §6 replaces the leader, the arbiter answers `GetPartitionStates` with `Unimplemented`: each pass then audits against the SNode's own inventory and counts `fsm_unavailable` once, and so does each promotion (K3); that growth is expected and stops after §6. Its table state also answers an Active table that is not ready on its SNode as Pending carrying its schema (K11). The sidecars, the in-pod rewriters and the ClickHouse connection (no `clickhouse_username`) do not change. Each sync restarts that indexer's pod, and its tables answer `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` (retryable) until its SNode is active again.

### 5.1 indexer-a

One commit: sentio-node `sha-<SN_COMMIT>@<SN_DIGEST>` in `k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/sentio-node-indexer-a-storage-integrity-si-v2-source-image.yaml`, its mirrors `docs/examples/storage-integrity-fresh-source-image.yaml` and `FRESH_SOURCE_IMAGE` in `test_render.py`, with the header comments naming `<SN_COMMIT>` (housegate `<HG_TAG>`, arbiter-core `<CORE_TAG>`) and the rollback target `sha-5d2f1695e33d911cb642bf60b49b71cdb74f62a0@sha256:be730c40d68e3de49d0d33c736a001a305b089ef11d1a81f0e883d804e15abaa`; and `ownerAudit: report` under `storageIntegrity.snode` in `k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/sentio-node-indexer-a-storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml` with its mirror `DEVNET2_OWNER_AUDIT["sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a"] = "report"`.

## 6. Voters

Followers first, the leader last, one pod at a time, so two voters always form a quorum; the sealed tip must agree on all three before the next deletion. The voters are `OnDelete`, so the deletion moves a pod onto the digest §4 committed. `<ARBITER_TAG>` adds no feature string (Plan S3-A contract §0), so the capability lines stay as they are; the new gauges appear on each replaced voter (the state-size ones from its startup restore of its newest local snapshot). The stage-3 reads and the holds answer once the leader runs `<ARBITER_TAG>`, which is the case from the third deletion on, because leadership then moves to a replaced voter. Each deletion is confirmed on its own.

First the order, read-only: the two followers, then the current leader, one ordinal per line in `$si_backup/voter-order`. The order is fixed once written; should the leadership move before the last deletion, keep it. The block never overwrites the file; to choose a new order deliberately, only before the first deletion, remove it (`rm "$si_backup/voter-order"`) and run the block again.

```bash
if [ -s "$si_backup/voter-order" ]; then echo "$si_backup/voter-order exists already, so the order stays:"; cat "$si_backup/voter-order"; echo "stop"; exit 1; fi
leader="$(si_leader)"
{ printf '0\n1\n2\n' | grep -vx "$leader"; echo "$leader"; } > "$si_backup/voter-order.new"
[ "$(sort "$si_backup/voter-order.new" | tr '\n' ' ')" = "0 1 2 " ] || { echo "no order of the three voters around leader '$leader'; stop"; exit 1; }
mv "$si_backup/voter-order.new" "$si_backup/voter-order"
cat "$si_backup/voter-order"
```

Expected: three lines, the leader's ordinal last (or, on a later run, the existing order and `stop`).

Then the first follower. `si_replace_voter` (§0 of the stage-1 runbook) deletes the pod, waits until it is Ready and every voter reports the same sealed tip, and prints its capability:

Confirm before running.

```bash

```

Then the second follower, once the first one returned with matching tips:

Confirm before running.

```bash
si_replace_voter "$(sed -n 2p "$si_backup/voter-order")" 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/replace-voter-2.txt"
```

Then the leader, last. The block also records when the leader was replaced and both owners' audit series right after it, which §7 and §9 compare against:

Confirm before running.

```bash
si_replace_voter "$(sed -n 3p "$si_backup/voter-order")" 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/replace-voter-3.txt"
date -u +%s > "$si_backup/leader-replaced-at"
for x in a b; do si_audit "$x" > "$si_backup/audit-$x-after-leader.txt"; done
```

Then the read-only checks:

```bash

  si_images
  l="$(si_leader)"; echo "leader arbiter-$l"
  for i in 0 1 2; do si_capability "$i"; echo "arbiter-$i"; si_state_size "$i"; si_hold_metrics "$i"; done

  cat "$si_backup/state-samples.tsv"

Expected: all six arbiter pods on `<ARBITER_DIGEST>`; every capability line names its own `node_id` with `protocol_version` `1`, `updates_enabled` `true` and `features` `["client_lanes_v1","signed_claims_v1","track_manifests_v1"]`; on every voter `arbiter_snapshot_doc_read_cap_bytes 1.073741824e+09`, `arbiter_state_bytes`, `arbiter_snapshot_doc_bytes` and `arbiter_snapshot_bytes` around `1.2e+07` (the measured state, about 2 % of L/4), `arbiter_raft_log_store_bytes` and `arbiter_raft_snapshot_store_bytes` above zero, `arbiter_snapshot_restore_seconds{trigger="startup"}`, the four `arbiter_snapshot_failures_total{operation=…}` at `0`, `arbiter_consensus_hold_active{mode="drain"} 0`, `arbiter_consensus_hold_active{mode="issuance"} 0` and `arbiter_consensus_hold_held_promotions_total 0`; the first line of `state-samples.tsv` (time, state bytes, document bytes, promotion sequence; §13.4); both owners' audit series as §5 left them.

## 7. Reads and holds

The voters §6 replaced lost their copy of `partstates` (§1.3). First copy it again, the only write of this section:

Confirm before running.

```bash
si_partstates_put 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/partstates-put-after-voters.txt"
```

Expected: three lines `arbiter-<i>: /tmp/partstates <sha256>` with the checksum of `partstates-build.txt`.

Everything else here is read-only: the leader serves the stage-3 reads, holds no consensus hold, and the owner audits stopped counting `fsm_unavailable`. The hold id below is random and unknown, so `hold-status` must answer NotFound:

```bash
{
  l="$(si_leader)"; echo "leader arbiter-$l: $(si_kubectl get pod "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-$l" -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}')"
  if out="$(si_arbiter "$l" /usr/local/bin/arbiter-admin consensus hold-status --address "$(si_voter "$l")" --hold-id "$(openssl rand -hex 16)" 2>&1)"; then echo "hold-status answered a hold: $out; stop"; exit 1; fi
  echo "$out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'code = NotFound desc = unknown consensus hold' || { echo "hold-status did not answer NotFound unknown consensus hold; stop"; exit 1; }
  echo "hold-status of an unknown id: NotFound unknown consensus hold"
  for i in 0 1 2; do echo "arbiter-$i"; si_hold_metrics "$i"; done
  for x in a b; do
    si_partstates "$x" > "$si_backup/partstates-$x.jsonl" 2> "$si_backup/partstates-$x.txt"; cat "$si_backup/partstates-$x.txt"
    jq -sc 'group_by(.table_id)[] | {table_id: .[0].table_id, status: .[0].status, partitions: length, last_acked: (map(.last_acked_promotion_seq) | max), unrefreshed: (map(select(.inventory_unrefreshed)) | length)}' "$si_backup/partstates-$x.jsonl"
    before="$(si_series_value sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_fsm_unavailable_total < "$si_backup/audit-$x-after-leader.txt" || true)"
    now="$(si_audit "$x" | si_series_value sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_fsm_unavailable_total || true)"
    echo "indexer-$x fsm_unavailable_total: $before after the leader replacement, $now now"
    si_audit "$x"
  done
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/holds-readonly.txt"
```

Expected: the leader on `<ARBITER_DIGEST>`; `error: read consensus hold at <leader>:7080: rpc error: code = NotFound desc = unknown consensus hold` and `hold-status of an unknown id: NotFound unknown consensus hold` (a leader older than `<ARBITER_TAG>` answers `error: leader does not support consensus holds (arbiter older than this arbiter-admin); upgrade the leader or pass --hold none` instead: §6 is not done); on every voter `arbiter_consensus_hold_active{mode="drain"} 0` and `{mode="issuance"} 0` and no `arbiter_consensus_holds_total` above `0`; `partstates: indexer 0: <n> tables, …` and one summary line per table with partition state, `devnet101.swap_new2` among them (`last_acked` at or above the promotion of `accept-3002.txt`), `partstates: indexer 1: …` for indexer-b (no table line while it owns no SI table), `unrefreshed` `0` everywhere (§10 requires it); `fsm_unavailable_total` equal on both lines for each owner (flat since the leader replacement although indexer-a promoted 3002); `runs_total{trigger="promotion"}` one more on indexer-a than after §5.1; `unclean_tables 0` and `dropped_twins_total 0` on both. A `partstates` error naming `ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable` or `Unimplemented` means the leader is not on `<ARBITER_TAG>`.

## 8. Monitoring

The chart's monitoring (stage 0, off) renders a headless `storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-metrics` Service, the VMServiceScrapes `storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter` (the voters' `/metrics`) and `storage-integrity-si-v2-hosts` (both hosts' embedded HouseGate on `hg-metrics`, with a `release` label), each adding `network="devnet2-si-v2"` and `si_component`, and the VMRule `storage-integrity-si-v2` with the groups `storage-integrity-si-v2.arbiter-state-size`, `.arbiter-promotion`, `.arbiter-voters`, `.hosts` and `.clickhouse`, every alert with a `severity`, a `summary` and a `runbook_url` into this file. It is turned on only now, once every voter and both hosts export the series the rules read: an absent series never fires. vmalert on sea runs `notifier.blackhole` and no Alertmanager exists, so a loaded VMRule only writes `ALERTS` series and notifies nobody (clarification K13): "alerts live" means the chart's rules loaded with their series present, a Grafana-managed rule on those `ALERTS` routed to `#alerts`, and a probe alert whose firing and resolved messages are seen there.

First the read-only checks of the access and the series this section relies on:

```bash
{
  for r in services vmservicescrapes.operator.victoriametrics.com vmrules.operator.victoriametrics.com; do echo "create $r: $(si_kubectl auth can-i create "$r")"; done
  echo "delete vmrules: $(si_kubectl auth can-i delete vmrules.operator.victoriametrics.com)"
  si_vm_query 'vector(1)' | jq -c '{status, value: .data.result[0].value[1]}'
  echo "vmalert groups of this network: $(si_vmalert_groups | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  for q in 'count(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="sentio-network-devnet2"})' 'count(up{namespace="sentio-network-devnet2"})' 'count(up{network="devnet2-si-v2"})'; do echo "$q = $(si_vm_value "$q")"; done
  # The series the chart's voter and ClickHouse rules select as the existing scrapes deliver them, read before the rules exist.
  chis='clickhouse_altinity_com_chi=~"storage-integrity-si-v2|storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b"'
  for q in 'count(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="sentio-network-devnet2", pod=~"storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-[0-9]+", container="arbiter"})' \
    "count(ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_Uptime{namespace=\"sentio-network-devnet2\", $chis})" \
    "count(ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_DiskAvailable_default{namespace=\"sentio-network-devnet2\", $chis})" \
    "count(ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_DiskTotal_default{namespace=\"sentio-network-devnet2\", $chis})"; do echo "$q = $(si_vm_value "$q")"; done
  si_kubectl get vmservicescrape,vmrule 2>&1
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/monitoring-before.txt"
```

Expected: `yes` four times; `{"status":"success","value":"1"}`; `vmalert groups of this network: 0`; a count above zero for the kube-state-metrics restarts and for `up` in the namespace (the existing annotation scrape), `none` for `up{network="devnet2-si-v2"}`; at least `3` for the voters' restart counter and at least `5` for each of the three ClickHouse series (the network installation's source and three verifier ClickHouses and indexer-b's source, labelled by the pod-annotation scrape; a series scraped twice counts twice, which the rules' `max`/`min` by pod absorb); no VMServiceScrape or VMRule of this release. `none` or a lower count for a rule's series: stop before the commit, because that rule would never see those pods (fix the chart first). `no` for any permission, or no answer from VictoriaMetrics or vmalert: stop and resolve that first (the `editor` role grants the VictoriaMetrics CRDs; a refusal from the `monitoring` namespace means the user reads the same series in vmui instead).

The commit: `monitoring.enabled: true` in `k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml` with its mirror `DEVNET2_MONITORING_ENABLED = True` in `test_render.py`. Before pushing it, render the release at `origin/main` and at the commit, read-only: the commit must add exactly the four monitoring objects and change nothing else (the monitoring values sit outside every checksum, so no pod moves):

```bash
{
  si_head_is charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml
  base="$(mktemp -d)"
  git archive origin/main charts k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2 docs/examples | tar -x -C "$base"
  (cd "$base" && helmfile -f k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml template --selector name=storage-integrity-si-v2 --skip-deps) > "$si_backup/monitoring-render-base.yaml"
  helmfile -f k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml template --selector name=storage-integrity-si-v2 --skip-deps > "$si_backup/monitoring-render-head.yaml"
  rm -rf "$base"
  python3 -I - "$si_backup/monitoring-render-base.yaml" "$si_backup/monitoring-render-head.yaml" <<'EOF'
import sys, yaml
def objects(path):
    return {(d["kind"], d["metadata"]["name"]): d for d in yaml.safe_load_all(open(path)) if d}
base, head = objects(sys.argv[1]), objects(sys.argv[2])
added = sorted(set(head) - set(base))
removed = sorted(set(base) - set(head))
changed = sorted(k for k in set(base) & set(head) if base[k] != head[k])
print("added:", added)
print("removed:", removed)
print("changed:", changed)
expected = [("Service", "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-metrics"), ("VMRule", "storage-integrity-si-v2"),
            ("VMServiceScrape", "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter"), ("VMServiceScrape", "storage-integrity-si-v2-hosts")]
if added != expected or removed or changed:
    sys.exit("the monitoring commit must add exactly the four monitoring objects and change nothing else")
print("the monitoring commit adds the four monitoring objects and changes nothing else")
EOF
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/monitoring-render-diff.txt"
```

Expected: `the monitoring commit adds the four monitoring objects and changes nothing else`.

Confirm before running.

```bash
python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py
si_head_is charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml
si_kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.metadata.uid} {.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -E '^storage-integrity-si-v2-(arbiter|verifier)-[0-9] |^sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-[ab]-0 ' | sort > "$si_backup/monitoring-pods-before.txt"
git rev-parse HEAD > "$si_backup/stage3-monitoring-commit"
git push origin HEAD:main

date -u +%s > "$si_backup/monitoring-synced-at"
```

Then the read-only checks: the objects, the scrape targets, every series the rules read, vmalert's groups, and that no pod moved. The block waits up to five minutes for the five targets:

```bash
{
  si_kubectl get service storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-metrics
  si_kubectl get vmservicescrape storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter storage-integrity-si-v2-hosts
  si_kubectl get vmrule storage-integrity-si-v2
  for n in $(seq 1 30); do [ "$(si_vm_value 'count(up{network="devnet2-si-v2"} == 1)')" = 5 ] && break; sleep 10; done
  si_vm_query 'up{network="devnet2-si-v2"}' | jq -c '.data.result[] | {si_component: .metric.si_component, release: .metric.release, pod: .metric.pod, up: .value[1]}'
  si_kubectl get vmrule storage-integrity-si-v2 -o json > "$si_backup/vmrule-live.json"
  python3 -I - "$si_backup/vmrule-live.json" > "$si_backup/vmrule-selectors.txt" <<'EOF'
import json, re, sys
seen = []
for group in json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["spec"]["groups"]:
    for rule in group["rules"]:
        for name, matchers in re.findall(r"([A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_:]*)\{([^}]*)\}", rule["expr"]):
            selector = "%s{%s}" % (name, matchers)
            if selector not in seen:
                seen.append(selector)
print("\n".join(seen))
EOF
  while read -r sel; do printf '%s %s\n' "$(si_vm_value "count($sel)" < /dev/null)" "$sel"; done < "$si_backup/vmrule-selectors.txt" | tee "$si_backup/vmrule-series.txt"
  si_vmalert_groups | tee "$si_backup/vmalert-groups.txt"
  si_vm_query 'ALERTS{network="devnet2-si-v2"}' | jq -c '.data.result[] | .metric'
  si_kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.metadata.uid} {.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -E '^storage-integrity-si-v2-(arbiter|verifier)-[0-9] |^sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-[ab]-0 ' | sort > "$si_backup/monitoring-pods-after.txt"
  cmp "$si_backup/monitoring-pods-before.txt" "$si_backup/monitoring-pods-after.txt" && echo "no arbiter, verifier or host pod moved"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/monitoring-after.txt"
```

Expected: the four objects; five targets `up` `1` (three `si_component` `arbiter`, two `host` with `release` `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a` and `-b`); in `vmrule-series.txt` a count above zero for every selector, exactly as the rules write it, except `kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{…}` and `sentio_node_storage_integrity_table_pending_seconds{…}` (kube-state-metrics exports a waiting reason only while a container waits, and a host exports a pending time only for a table that is Pending, so `none` is the healthy answer for both), the recording rules' own outputs (`arbiter:…`) included after their first evaluation (repeat the block if one still says `none`); five groups `storage-integrity-si-v2.arbiter-state-size`, `.arbiter-promotion`, `.arbiter-voters`, `.hosts` and `.clickhouse`, every rule with `health` `ok` and an empty `lastError`; no `ALERTS` series, or only ones read and explained before going on; `no arbiter, verifier or host pod moved` (the sync re-ran only the chart's `bootstrap-source` hook Job, as every sync of this release does). Any other `none`: the rule reads a series nobody exports and would never fire; stop and fix the chart.

Then the Grafana rule, a user action in the user's own browser (the agent never logs into Grafana). In the sea Grafana, Alerting → Alert rules → New alert rule, on the sea VictoriaMetrics data source: the query `count by (alertname, network, severity) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing", network="devnet2-si-v2", alertname=~"Arbiter.*|SentioNode.*|StorageIntegrity.*"}) > 0`, evaluated every minute with a pending period of one minute, "Alert state if no data" set to Normal (no firing alert is the healthy answer, which must not raise a NoData alert), the labels the existing `#alerts` notification policy routes on, and the summary `{{ $labels.alertname }} on {{ $labels.network }} ({{ $labels.severity }})`. The user saves it and reads its UID from the rule's URL; then record it (local only):

```bash
grafana_rule_uid='<the rule UID from Grafana>'
case "$grafana_rule_uid" in ''|*'<'*) echo "set grafana_rule_uid to the UID of the Grafana rule the user created"; exit 1;; esac
printf '%s\n' "$grafana_rule_uid" > "$si_backup/grafana-rule-uid"
```

Then the delivery probe, a throwaway VMRule applied with `kubectl`, never through the chart (the chart's alert set stays the reviewed one). First the file and a server-side dry run, read-only:

```bash
cat > "$si_backup/delivery-probe.yaml" <<'EOF'
apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1beta1
kind: VMRule
metadata:
  name: storage-integrity-delivery-probe
  namespace: sentio-network-devnet2
spec:
  groups:
    - name: storage-integrity-delivery-probe
      interval: 30s
      rules:
        - alert: StorageIntegrityDeliveryProbe
          expr: vector(1)
          labels:
            network: devnet2-si-v2
            severity: warning
          annotations:
            summary: Delivery probe of docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md §8; it resolves when the probe VMRule is deleted
EOF
si_kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f "$si_backup/delivery-probe.yaml" 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/delivery-probe-dry-run.txt"
```

Expected: `vmrule.operator.victoriametrics.com/storage-integrity-delivery-probe created (server dry run)`.

date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >> "$si_backup/delivery-probe-apply.txt"

Then the read-only wait for the firing series (up to ten minutes):

```bash
{

Expected: `firing=1` within about two minutes, and the probe group with `health` `ok`. Within about three more minutes Grafana posts `StorageIntegrityDeliveryProbe on devnet2-si-v2 (warning)` as firing to `#alerts`. The user copies that message's permalink (Slack: More actions → Copy link) and records it (local only):

```bash
permalink='<the #alerts permalink of the firing message>'
case "$permalink" in https://*) ;; *) echo "set permalink to the Slack permalink of the firing message"; exit 1;; esac
! grep -q '^[^ ]* firing ' "$si_backup/delivery-probe.txt" 2>/dev/null || { echo "a firing permalink is recorded already:"; cat "$si_backup/delivery-probe.txt"; exit 1; }

Then the read-only wait until the series is gone (up to fifteen minutes):
````
