```python
def si_grants(role, physical_database="devnet2"):
    """SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS[role] on an installation whose tenant database is physical_database."""
    return [grant.replace(" ON devnet2.*", f" ON {physical_database}.*") for grant in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS[role]]


def si_clickhouse_users(kind, posture, hashes, physical_database="devnet2"):
    """The users block of an SI ClickHouse installation of one kind in one posture.

    A is today's (default passwordless, any address, access management), B adds
    the si_* users with their grants and leaves default unchanged, C also locks
    default (its own password, loopback only, no access management). hashes maps
    every rendered user to the SHA-256 of its password.
    """
    if posture == "C":
        users = {
            "default/password_sha256_hex": hashes["default"],
            "default/networks/ip": ["127.0.0.1", "::1"],
        }
    elif posture in ("A", "B"):
        users = {
            "default/password": "",
            "default/networks/ip": ["0.0.0.0/0"],
            "default/access_management": "1",
        }
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown posture {posture!r}")
    if posture != "A":
        for user in SI_CLICKHOUSE_USERS[kind][1:]:
            users[f"{user}/password_sha256_hex"] = hashes[user]
            users[f"{user}/networks/ip"] = ["::/0"]
            users[f"{user}/profile"] = "default"
            users[f"{user}/grants/query"] = si_grants(user, physical_database)
    return users


def si_clickhouse_files(files, posture):
    """The files of an installation in one posture, given its files without the lock."""
    files = dict(files)
    if posture == "C":
        files[SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_FILE] = SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_XML
    return files


def unlocked_files(files):
    """An installation's files without posture C's users.d file."""
    return {name: text for name, text in files.items() if name != SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_FILE}


def clickhouse_access(posture, hashes=TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256):
    """storage-integrity values of one posture; C also gives every client of the
    installation its login, A and B leave the bootstrap hook passwordless."""
    access = {
        "users": posture in ("B", "C"),
        "lockDefault": posture == "C",
        "passwordSha256": {
            user: hashes[user] if posture == "C" or (posture == "B" and user != "default") else ""
            for user in SI_CLICKHOUSE_USERS["network"]
        },
        "bootstrapPasswordSecret": {"name": "", "key": "password"},
    }
    values = {"clickhouse": {"access": access}}
    if posture == "C":
        access["bootstrapPasswordSecret"] = {"name": "render-test-clickhouse-bootstrap", "key": "password"}
        values["verifier"] = {"clickhouse": {
            "username": "si_verifier",
            "passwordSecret": {"name": "render-test-clickhouse-verifier", "key": "password"},
        }}
    return values


def bootstrap_container(docs, name="storage-integrity"):
    return docs[("Job", f"{name}-bootstrap-source")]["spec"]["template"]["spec"]["containers"][0]
```

```python
class ClickHouseAccessTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Phase L (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14): the users of the network's SI
    ClickHouse installation posture by posture, and the logins of the
    verifiers and of the bootstrap-source hook."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.docs = documents(render())
        cls.posture = {"A": cls.docs}
        for posture in ("B", "C"):
            cls.posture[posture] = documents(render(clickhouse_access(posture)))

    def assert_rejected(self, overrides, error):
        result = render(overrides)
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
        self.assertIn(error, result.stderr)

    @staticmethod
    def installation(docs):
        return docs[("ClickHouseInstallation", "storage-integrity")]["spec"]

    def test_si_clickhouse_users_follow_the_posture(self):
        base = self.installation(self.docs)
        for posture in ("A", "B", "C"):
            with self.subTest(posture=posture):
                chi = self.installation(self.posture[posture])
                configuration = chi["configuration"]
                self.assertEqual(
                    configuration["users"],
                    si_clickhouse_users("network", posture, TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256, physical_database="render_test"),
                )
                self.assertEqual(configuration["files"], si_clickhouse_files(base["configuration"]["files"], posture))
                # Users and users.d files reload in place; nothing that restarts a
                # pod (Keeper, settings, other files, templates) changes.
                for key in ("zookeeper", "clusters", "settings", "profiles"):
                    self.assertEqual(configuration[key], base["configuration"][key], key)
                self.assertEqual((chi["defaults"], chi["templates"]), (base["defaults"], base["templates"]))
        # Posture B only adds users: default and every other object stay as in A.
        users_b = self.installation(self.posture["B"])["configuration"]["users"]
        self.assertEqual({key: value for key, value in users_b.items() if key.startswith("default/")},
                         self.installation(self.docs)["configuration"]["users"])
        changed = {key for key in self.docs if self.posture["B"][key] != self.docs[key]}
        self.assertEqual(changed, {("ClickHouseInstallation", "storage-integrity")})
        # Posture C also switches the installation's clients to their logins.
        changed = {key for key in self.docs if self.posture["C"][key] != self.docs[key]}
        self.assertEqual(changed, {
            ("ClickHouseInstallation", "storage-integrity"),
            ("ConfigMap", "storage-integrity-verifier-config"),
            ("StatefulSet", "storage-integrity-verifier"),
            ("Job", "storage-integrity-bootstrap-source"),
        })

    def test_si_clickhouse_users_hold_exactly_the_protocol_grants(self):
        self.assertEqual(set(SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS), set(SI_CLICKHOUSE_USERS["network"][1:]))
        self.assertEqual(set(SI_CLICKHOUSE_USERS["indexer"]), set(SI_CLICKHOUSE_USERS["network"]) - {"si_verifier"})
        for posture in ("B", "C"):
            users = self.installation(self.posture[posture])["configuration"]["users"]
            for role in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS:
                with self.subTest(posture=posture, role=role):
                    self.assertEqual(users[f"{role}/grants/query"], si_grants(role, "render_test"))
                    self.assertEqual((users[f"{role}/networks/ip"], users[f"{role}/profile"]), (["::/0"], "default"))
        for role, grants in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS.items():
            self.assertEqual(len(grants), len(set(grants)), role)
            for grant in grants:
                with self.subTest(role=role, grant=grant):
                    self.assertRegex(grant, r"^GRANT [A-Z]")
                    self.assertNotIn(" TO ", grant)
                    for database in SI_MEMBER_DATABASES:
                        self.assertNotIn(database, grant)
                    # Never a write to a remote or an external source, never access management.
                    self.assertNotRegex(grant, r"\b(ALL|WRITE|REMOTE ON|URL|S3|FILE|ACCESS MANAGEMENT|NAMED COLLECTION|INTROSPECTION)\b")
        # si_gateway's login reaches every HouseGate session: it reads hg_safe and
        # hg_unsafe and nothing else of the protocol databases, and has no SYSTEM.
        for grant in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS["si_gateway"]:
            if " ON hg_" in grant:
                self.assertRegex(grant, r"^GRANT SELECT ON hg_(safe|unsafe)\.\*$")
            self.assertNotIn("SYSTEM", grant)
        self.assertFalse([grant for grant in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS["si_verifier"] if "SYSTEM MERGES" in grant])
        self.assertTrue(all(grant.startswith("GRANT SELECT") for grant in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS["si_reader"]))

    def test_si_clickhouse_default_is_locked_to_loopback_in_posture_c(self):
        configuration = self.installation(self.posture["C"])["configuration"]
        users = configuration["users"]
        self.assertEqual(users["default/password_sha256_hex"], TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256["default"])
        self.assertEqual(users["default/networks/ip"], ["127.0.0.1", "::1"])
        self.assertNotIn("default/password", users)
        self.assertNotIn("default/access_management", users)
        # Exactly one users.d file, contract §11's text verbatim as a block scalar
        # (one line and a trailing newline).
        self.assertEqual(unlocked_files(configuration["files"]), self.installation(self.docs)["configuration"]["files"])
        self.assertEqual(configuration["files"][SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_FILE], SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_XML)
        self.assertEqual(SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_XML, (
            '<clickhouse><users><default><networks replace="replace"><ip>::1</ip><ip>127.0.0.1</ip></networks>'
            "<access_management>0</access_management></default></users></clickhouse>\n"
        ))
        self.assertIn(
            f"        </clickhouse>\n      {SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_FILE}: |\n        {SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_XML}    users:\n",
            render(clickhouse_access("C")).stdout,
        )
        default = ElementTree.fromstring(SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_XML).find("users/default")
        self.assertEqual([child.tag for child in default], ["networks", "access_management"])
        networks = default.find("networks")
        self.assertEqual(networks.get("replace"), "replace")
        self.assertEqual([(ip.tag, ip.text) for ip in networks], [("ip", "::1"), ("ip", "127.0.0.1")])
        self.assertEqual(default.find("access_management").text, "0")
        # users.d/ files reload in place, and this one sorts after the operator's own users file.
        self.assertTrue(SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_FILE.startswith("users.d/zz-"))
        for posture in ("A", "B"):
            with self.subTest(posture=posture):
                configuration = self.installation(self.posture[posture])["configuration"]
                self.assertEqual(unlocked_files(configuration["files"]), configuration["files"])
                self.assertEqual(configuration["users"]["default/networks/ip"], ["0.0.0.0/0"])

    def test_bootstrap_hook_authenticates_when_it_has_a_login(self):
        plain = bootstrap_container(self.docs)
        self.assertIn('ch() { clickhouse-client --host "$host" --port 9000 "$@"; }', plain["args"][0])
        self.assertNotIn("env", plain)
        self.assertEqual(bootstrap_container(self.posture["B"]), plain)
        login = bootstrap_container(self.posture["C"])
        self.assertIn('ch() { clickhouse-client --host "$host" --port 9000 --user si_gateway "$@"; }', login["args"][0])
        self.assertEqual(login["env"], [{"name": "CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD", "valueFrom": {"secretKeyRef": {
            "name": "render-test-clickhouse-bootstrap", "key": "password",
        }}}])
        # Nothing else of the hook changes: the password never reaches its arguments.
        unchanged = {key: value for key, value in login.items() if key != "env"}
        unchanged["args"] = [login["args"][0].replace(" --user si_gateway", "")]
        self.assertEqual(unchanged, plain)

    def test_verifier_login_needs_a_username(self):
        self.assertNotIn("clickhouse_username", config_for(self.docs, "verifier"))
        plain = pod_template(self.docs, "verifier")
        self.assertNotIn("env", plain["spec"]["containers"][0])
        self.assertNotIn("storage-integrity.sentio.xyz/clickhouse-user", plain["metadata"]["annotations"])
        login = self.posture["C"]
        self.assertEqual(config_for(login, "verifier")["clickhouse_username"], "si_verifier")
        template = pod_template(login, "verifier")
        self.assertEqual(template["spec"]["containers"][0]["env"], [{
            "name": "ARBITER_VERIFIER_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD",
            "valueFrom": {"secretKeyRef": {"name": "render-test-clickhouse-verifier", "key": "password"}},
        }])
        self.assertEqual(template["metadata"]["annotations"]["storage-integrity.sentio.xyz/clickhouse-user"], "si_verifier")
        # The identity checksum and the arbiter's config do not move with a login.
        self.assertEqual(template["metadata"]["annotations"]["checksum/config"], plain["metadata"]["annotations"]["checksum/config"])
        self.assertEqual(arbiter_config(login), arbiter_config(self.docs))
        # A user without a Secret is rendered (a passwordless named user); a Secret without a user is refused.
        named = documents(render({"verifier": {"clickhouse": {"username": "si_verifier"}}}))
        self.assertEqual(config_for(named, "verifier")["clickhouse_username"], "si_verifier")
        self.assertNotIn("env", pod_template(named, "verifier")["spec"]["containers"][0])
        self.assert_rejected(
            {"verifier": {"clickhouse": {"passwordSecret": {"name": "render-test-clickhouse-verifier"}}}},
            "verifier.clickhouse.passwordSecret requires verifier.clickhouse.username",
        )
        for docs in (named, login):
            self.assertNotIn("clickhouse_password", config_for(docs, "verifier"))

    def test_clickhouse_access_guards_fail_closed(self):
        b = clickhouse_access("B")["clickhouse"]["access"]
        c = clickhouse_access("C")

        def with_hash(access, user, value):
            return {"clickhouse": {"access": {**access, "passwordSha256": {**access["passwordSha256"], user: value}}}}

        malformed = "clickhouse.access.passwordSha256.{} must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
        unlocked_client = (
            "clickhouse.access.lockDefault requires clickhouse.access.bootstrapPasswordSecret and verifier.clickhouse.username: "
            "every client of this installation must log in before default is locked"
        )
        for overrides, error in (
            ({"clickhouse": {"access": {"lockDefault": True, "passwordSha256": {"default": TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256["default"]}}}},
             "clickhouse.access.lockDefault requires clickhouse.access.users"),
            ({"clickhouse": {"access": {"bootstrapPasswordSecret": {"name": "render-test-clickhouse-bootstrap"}}}},
             "clickhouse.access.bootstrapPasswordSecret requires clickhouse.access.users"),
            ({"clickhouse": {"access": {"users": True}}}, malformed.format("si_snode")),
            (with_hash(b, "si_reader", TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256["si_reader"].upper()), malformed.format("si_reader")),
            (with_hash(b, "si_gateway", TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256["si_gateway"][:63]), malformed.format("si_gateway")),
            (with_hash(b, "default", "not-a-hash"), malformed.format("default")),
            ({**c, **with_hash(c["clickhouse"]["access"], "default", "")}, malformed.format("default")),
            # The lock without every client's login: the bootstrap hook, the verifiers, a verifier user without its password.
            ({"clickhouse": {"access": {**c["clickhouse"]["access"], "bootstrapPasswordSecret": {"name": ""}}}, "verifier": c["verifier"]},
             unlocked_client),
            ({"clickhouse": c["clickhouse"]}, unlocked_client),
            ({"clickhouse": c["clickhouse"], "verifier": {"clickhouse": {"username": "si_verifier"}}}, unlocked_client),
            ({"verifier": {"clickhouse": {"passwordSecret": {"name": "render-test-clickhouse-verifier"}}}},
             "verifier.clickhouse.passwordSecret requires verifier.clickhouse.username"),
            # Typed values and only the users this chart renders (values.schema.json).
            ({"clickhouse": {"access": {"users": "true"}}}, "users"),
            ({"clickhouse": {"access": {"lockDefault": 1}}}, "lockDefault"),
            ({"clickhouse": {"access": {"passwordSha256": {"si_member": TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256["si_reader"]}}}}, "si_member"),
            ({"clickhouse": {"access": {"passwordSha256": {"si_snode": 7}}}}, "si_snode"),
            ({"clickhouse": {"access": {"bootstrapPasswordSecret": {"key": ""}}}}, "bootstrapPasswordSecret"),
            ({"verifier": {"clickhouse": {"username": "si-verifier"}}}, "username"),
        ):
            with self.subTest(error=error, overrides=overrides):
                self.assert_rejected(overrides, error)

    def test_unset_clickhouse_access_renders_unchanged(self):
        configuration = self.installation(self.docs)["configuration"]
        self.assertEqual(configuration["users"], {

            "    clickhouse_addr: __CLICKHOUSE_ADDR__\n    scratch_database: default\n",
            "          args: [-config, /config/verifier.yaml, -ensure-tables=create]\n          volumeMounts:\n",
            '              ch() { clickhouse-client --host "$host" --port 9000 "$@"; }\n',
            '              echo "$got"\n          resources:\n',
        ):
            with self.subTest(lines=lines):

        # Every new value set to its default renders exactly what leaving it unset does.

        explicit = {
            "clickhouse": {"access": defaults["clickhouse"]["access"]},
```

```gotemplate
default passwordless, any address, access_management), B (users: the si_*
users added, default unchanged) or C (lockDefault: default with a password,
loopback only, no access_management key; the users.d file below completes the
lock). Hashes are literal; validate.yaml checks them. */ -}}
{{- define "storage-integrity.clickhouseUsers" -}}
{{- $access := .Values.clickhouse.access -}}
{{- if $access.lockDefault }}
default/password_sha256_hex: {{ index $access.passwordSha256 "default" | quote }}
default/networks/ip:
  - 127.0.0.1
  - "::1"
{{- else }}
default/password: ""
default/networks/ip:
  - 0.0.0.0/0
default/access_management: "1"
{{- end }}
{{- if $access.users }}
{{- range $user := list "si_snode" "si_gateway" "si_verifier" "si_reader" }}
{{ $user }}/password_sha256_hex: {{ index $access.passwordSha256 $user | quote }}
{{ $user }}/networks/ip:
  - "::/0"
{{ $user }}/profile: default
{{ $user }}/grants/query:
{{ include (printf "storage-integrity.grants.%s" $user) $ | indent 2 }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

{{- /* Posture C's one users.d file (Plan S3-B contract §11): it replaces the
networks the operator merges into default (the installation's pod addresses,
its host regexp, the image's ::/0) with loopback only, and takes access
management from default, which the image's own users.xml grants
(access_management 1), so leaving the key out of the installation would not.
default keeps every data right and named collection control. clickhouse.yaml
writes it as a block scalar, the same text as every CHI manifest's. A users.d
file reloads in place and never restarts a pod. */ -}}
{{- define "storage-integrity.defaultLoopbackXML" -}}
<clickhouse><users><default><networks replace="replace"><ip>::1</ip><ip>127.0.0.1</ip></networks><access_management>0</access_management></default></users></clickhouse>
{{- end }}
```

```gotemplate
{{- /*
The ClickHouse users of this installation and the logins of its clients
(housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14, phase L;
docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md). Posture B (users) adds the
si_* users; posture C (lockDefault) locks default, so every client of the
installation must already log in as its own user: the bootstrap-source hook
runs on every sync, and the verifiers read this installation's verifier
ClickHouses. A hash is checked whenever it is given, so a typo cannot wait for
the posture that renders it.
*/ -}}
{{- $access := .Values.clickhouse.access }}
{{- $verifierLogin := .Values.verifier.clickhouse }}
{{- $hashes := $access.passwordSha256 | default dict }}
{{- if eq .Values.arbiter.protocol "legacy" }}
{{- if or $access.users $access.lockDefault $access.bootstrapPasswordSecret.name $verifierLogin.username $verifierLogin.passwordSecret.name (ne (join "" (values $hashes)) "") }}
{{- fail "clickhouse.access and verifier.clickhouse require arbiter.protocol=pinned-genesis-v1" }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- if and $access.lockDefault (not $access.users) }}
{{- fail "clickhouse.access.lockDefault requires clickhouse.access.users" }}
{{- end }}
{{- if and $access.bootstrapPasswordSecret.name (not $access.users) }}
{{- fail "clickhouse.access.bootstrapPasswordSecret requires clickhouse.access.users" }}
{{- end }}
{{- range $user := list "default" "si_snode" "si_gateway" "si_verifier" "si_reader" }}
{{- $hash := toString (index $hashes $user | default "") }}
{{- $rendered := ternary $access.lockDefault $access.users (eq $user "default") }}
{{- if and (or $rendered (ne $hash "")) (not (regexMatch "^[0-9a-f]{64}$" $hash)) }}
{{- fail (printf "clickhouse.access.passwordSha256.%s must be 64 lowercase hex characters" $user) }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- if and $verifierLogin.passwordSecret.name (empty $verifierLogin.username) }}
{{- fail "verifier.clickhouse.passwordSecret requires verifier.clickhouse.username" }}
{{- end }}
{{- /* A verifier user without its passwordSecret cannot log in either. */ -}}
{{- if and $access.lockDefault (or (empty $access.bootstrapPasswordSecret.name) (empty $verifierLogin.username) (empty $verifierLogin.passwordSecret.name)) }}
{{- fail "clickhouse.access.lockDefault requires clickhouse.access.bootstrapPasswordSecret and verifier.clickhouse.username: every client of this installation must log in before default is locked" }}
{{- end }}
```

```python
def render_sentio_node(*overrides):
    """helm template of charts/sentio-node with its defaults and overrides."""
    command = ["helm", "template", "probe", str(SENTIO_NODE_CHART), "--namespace", RENDER_NAMESPACE]
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        for index, override in enumerate(overrides):
            path = Path(directory) / f"override-{index}.yaml"
            path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(override))
            command += ["-f", str(path)]
        return subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
```

```python
    def test_snode_clickhouse_login_needs_a_reviewed_image(self):
        # sentio-node decodes its config leniently: an image older than the

        # keeps logging in as default, which fails once default is locked.
        checked = []
        referenced = set()
        for helmfile in sentio_node_helmfiles():
            for release in yaml.safe_load(helmfile.read_text())["releases"]:
                if (helmfile.parent / release["chart"]).resolve() != SENTIO_NODE_CHART:
                    continue
                label = f"{helmfile.relative_to(ROOT)}:{release['name']}"
                values, files = release_chart_values(helmfile, release, label)
                referenced.update(files)
                checked.append(label)
                if values["storageIntegrity"].get("clickhouseUsername"):
                    image = values["node"]["image"]
                    self.assertIn(
                        f'{image["repository"]}:{image["tag"]}', STAGE3_HOST_IMAGES,
                        f"{label}: storageIntegrity.clickhouseUsername needs a reviewed image",
                    )
        self.assertIn(f"{FRESH_HELMFILE.relative_to(ROOT)}:sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a", checked)
        self.assertIn(f"{FRESH_HELMFILE.relative_to(ROOT)}:sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b", checked)
        tracked = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "ls-files", "k8s-*"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
        ).stdout.split()
        for name in tracked:
            path = ROOT / name
            if path.suffix in (".yaml", ".yml") and path not in referenced and path.is_file():
                self.assertNotIn("clickhouseUsername", path.read_text(errors="ignore"), f"{name} is not part of any sentio-node release")

    def test_si_clients_take_clickhouse_passwords_only_from_secrets(self):
        # The end state of the lockdown: posture C and every client on its own login.
        rendered = {FRESH_RELEASE: documents(self.render_with(self.control_release, self.network_logins()))}
        expected = {FRESH_RELEASE: {
            "ARBITER_VERIFIER_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD": {"name": f"{FRESH_RELEASE}-clickhouse-verifier", "key": "password"},
            "CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD": {"name": f"{FRESH_RELEASE}-clickhouse-bootstrap", "key": "password"},
        }}
        for name, release in self.host_releases().items():
            rendered[name] = documents(self.render_with(release, self.host_logout(), self.host_login(name)))
            expected[name] = {"STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD": {"name": f"{name}-clickhouse", "key": "snode-password"}}

        def walk(node):
            if isinstance(node, dict):
                yield node
                for value in node.values():
                    yield from walk(value)
            elif isinstance(node, list):
                for value in node:
                    yield from walk(value)

        for name, docs in rendered.items():
            with self.subTest(release=name):
                passwords = {}
                for resource in docs.values():
                    for node in walk(resource):
                        for item in node.get("env") or []:
                            if "PASSWORD" in item["name"]:
                                self.assertEqual(set(item), {"name", "valueFrom"}, item["name"])
                                passwords[item["name"]] = item["valueFrom"]["secretKeyRef"]
                self.assertEqual(passwords, expected[name])
                # No rendered config carries a ClickHouse password key, and the
                # charts render no Secret holding one.
                for key, resource in docs.items():
                    for text in (resource.get("data") or {}).values():
                        self.assertNotIn("clickhouse_password", text, key)
                self.assertEqual({key[1] for key in docs if key[0] == "Secret"} - {f"{name}-docker-config"}, set())
        # The hashes appear in the installation's users only.
        control = rendered[FRESH_RELEASE]
        for key, resource in control.items():
            if key != ("ClickHouseInstallation", FRESH_RELEASE):
                for value in TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256.values():
                    self.assertNotIn(value, json.dumps(resource), key)
```

```python
def clickhouse_users_by_role(users):
    """A CHI's users with each literal hash replaced by a marker and the network
    installation's si_verifier left out, so installations compare by role."""
    return {
        key: "<sha256>" if key.endswith("/password_sha256_hex") else value
        for key, value in users.items()
        if not key.startswith("si_verifier/")
    }


def lockdown_staging_chi(posture, hashes):
    """The lockdown runbook's staging installation in one posture: the checked-in
    file (posture A) with the network's user set of that posture, as §5 applies it."""
    chi = yaml.safe_load(LOCKDOWN_STAGING_CHI.read_text())
    configuration = chi["spec"]["configuration"]
    configuration["users"] = si_clickhouse_users(SI_CLICKHOUSE_INSTALLATION_KIND[chi["metadata"]["name"]], posture, hashes)
    configuration["files"] = si_clickhouse_files(configuration["files"], posture)
    return chi


def grant_probe_rows():
    """(role, expect, statement) rows of the grant probe corpus, in file order."""
    lines = [line for line in GRANT_PROBE.read_text().splitlines() if line and not line.startswith("#")]
    if lines[0] != "role\texpect\tstatement":
        raise AssertionError(f"grant probe header is {lines[0]!r}")
    rows = []
    for line in lines[1:]:
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 3:
            raise AssertionError(f"grant probe row needs three tab-separated fields: {line!r}")
        rows.append(tuple(fields))
    return rows


def grant_atoms(grant):
    """The (privilege, object, columns) atoms one users.xml GRANT gives."""
    match = re.fullmatch(r"GRANT (.+) ON (\S+)", grant)
    if not match:
        raise AssertionError(f"unparsed grant {grant!r}")
    privileges, target = match.groups()
    atoms = set()
    for privilege in re.split(r",\s*(?![^()]*\))", privileges):
        columns = re.fullmatch(r"(\w+)\((.+)\)", privilege)
        if columns:
            atoms.add((columns.group(1), target, frozenset(c.strip() for c in columns.group(2).split(","))))
        else:
            atoms.add((privilege, target, None))
    return atoms


def role_atoms(role):
    """Every atom a role holds, ClickHouse's implicit grants included (any CREATE
    TABLE gives a global CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE, CREATE and DROP TABLE give the
    VIEW forms on the same object)."""
    atoms = set().union(*(grant_atoms(grant) for grant in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS[role]))
    for privilege, target, columns in list(atoms):
        if privilege == "CREATE TABLE":
            atoms |= {("CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE", "*.*", None), ("CREATE VIEW", target, None)}
        if privilege == "DROP TABLE":
            atoms.add(("DROP VIEW", target, None))
    return atoms


def probe_object(database, table):
    return f"system.{table}" if database == "system" else f"{database}.*"


def probe_columns(select, where):
    """The columns a SELECT reads, or None for count() without a WHERE."""
    columns = set() if select.strip() == "count()" else {column.strip() for column in select.split(",")}
    if where:
        columns |= set(re.findall(r"(\w+) = '", where))
    return frozenset(columns) or None


def probe_atoms(statement):
    """The (privilege, object, columns) atoms the access check of one probe statement needs."""
    name = r"(\w+)\.(\w+)"
    forms = (
        (rf"CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS (\w+)", lambda m: {("CREATE DATABASE", f"{m[1]}.*", None)}),
        (rf"CREATE TABLE (?:IF NOT EXISTS )?{name} \(.+\) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple\(\)",
         lambda m: {("CREATE TABLE", probe_object(m[1], m[2]), None)}),
        (rf"CREATE VIEW {name} AS SELECT (.+) FROM {name}",
         lambda m: {("CREATE VIEW", probe_object(m[1], m[2]), None), ("SELECT", probe_object(m[4], m[5]), None)}),
        (r"CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE \w+ \(.+\)", lambda m: {("CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE", "*.*", None)}),
        (rf"DROP (TABLE|VIEW) (?:IF EXISTS )?{name}", lambda m: {(f"DROP {m[1]}", probe_object(m[2], m[3]), None)}),
        (r"INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote\(.+\) VALUES \(.+\)",
         lambda m: {("WRITE", "REMOTE", None), ("CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE", "*.*", None)}),
        (rf"INSERT INTO {name} VALUES \(.+\)", lambda m: {("INSERT", probe_object(m[1], m[2]), None)}),
        (r"SELECT (.+) FROM (remote|url)\(.+\)",
         lambda m: {("READ", m[2].upper(), None), ("CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE", "*.*", None)}),
        (rf"SELECT (.+) FROM {name}(?: WHERE (.+))?",
         lambda m: {("SELECT", probe_object(m[2], m[3]), probe_columns(m[1], m[4]))}),
        (rf"ALTER TABLE {name} (?:REPLACE|ATTACH) PARTITION tuple\(\) FROM {name}", lambda m: {
            ("SELECT", probe_object(m[3], m[4]), None),
            ("ALTER DELETE", probe_object(m[1], m[2]), None),
            ("INSERT", probe_object(m[1], m[2]), None),
        }),
        (rf"ALTER TABLE {name} DROP PARTITION tuple\(\)", lambda m: {("ALTER DELETE", probe_object(m[1], m[2]), None)}),
        (rf"ALTER TABLE {name} ADD COLUMN \w+ \w+", lambda m: {("ALTER ADD COLUMN", probe_object(m[1], m[2]), None)}),
        (rf"(TRUNCATE|OPTIMIZE) TABLE {name}", lambda m: {(m[1], probe_object(m[2], m[3]), None)}),
        (rf"SYSTEM START MERGES {name}", lambda m: {("SYSTEM MERGES", probe_object(m[1], m[2]), None)}),
        (r"SYSTEM DROP REPLICA '[\w-]+' FROM ZKPATH '[\w/-]+'", lambda m: {("SYSTEM DROP REPLICA", "*.*", None)}),
    )
    for pattern, atoms in forms:
        match = re.fullmatch(pattern, statement)
        if match:
            return atoms(match)
    raise AssertionError(f"the grant probe has no access rule for {statement!r}")


def atom_granted(atom, held):
    """Whether a role holding the atoms held passes the access check for atom."""
    privilege, target, columns = atom
    for held_privilege, held_target, held_columns in held:
        if held_privilege != privilege and not (held_privilege == "ALTER" and privilege.startswith("ALTER ")):
            continue
        if held_target not in (target, "*.*"):
            continue
        if held_columns is None or (columns is not None and columns <= held_columns):
            return True
    return False


def atom_exercises(atom, grant_atom):
    """Whether a statement needing atom exercises the grant atom grant_atom."""
    privilege, target, columns = atom
    granted_privilege, granted_target, granted_columns = grant_atom
    return (
        (privilege == granted_privilege or (granted_privilege == "ALTER" and privilege.startswith("ALTER ")))
        and target == granted_target
        and (granted_columns is None or columns == granted_columns)
    )
```

```python
    def test_si_clickhouse_users_carry_only_literal_hashes(self):
        installations = {f"chart posture {p}": self.installation(self.posture[p])["configuration"] for p in self.posture}
        for path in (INDEXER_B_CHI, LOCKDOWN_STAGING_CHI):
            installations[path.name] = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())["spec"]["configuration"]
        for posture in ("B", "C"):
            installations[f"staging posture {posture}"] = lockdown_staging_chi(posture, TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256)["spec"]["configuration"]
        auth = ("password", "password_sha256_hex", "password_double_sha1_hex", "password_scram_sha256_hex", "no_password")
        for name, configuration in installations.items():
            with self.subTest(installation=name):
                users = configuration["users"]
                methods = {}
                for key, value in users.items():
                    user, field = key.split("/", 1)
                    # valueFrom rolls every pod; k8s_secret_* falls back silently to a known password.
                    self.assertNotIsInstance(value, dict, key)
                    self.assertNotIn("k8s_secret", field, key)
                    if field in auth:
                        methods.setdefault(user, []).append(field)
                    if field == "password_sha256_hex":
                        self.assertIsInstance(value, str, key)
                        self.assertRegex(value, r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$", key)
                    if field == "password":
                        self.assertEqual((user, value), ("default", ""), "a plaintext password is never in an installation")
                # A users.xml user holds one authentication method.
                self.assertEqual({user: len(fields) for user, fields in methods.items()}, dict.fromkeys(methods, 1))
                hashes = [value for key, value in users.items() if key.endswith("/password_sha256_hex")]
                self.assertEqual(len(hashes), len(set(hashes)), "one password per user and installation")

    def test_grant_probe_covers_every_protocol_grant(self):
        rows = grant_probe_rows()
        roles = [role for role, _, _ in rows]
        self.assertEqual(set(roles), {"default", *SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS})
        self.assertTrue(all(expect in ("ok", "denied") for _, expect, _ in rows))
        # default (the admin) only sets the referenced tables up first and drops them last.
        protocol = [index for index, role in enumerate(roles) if role != "default"]
        setup = [row for row in rows[:protocol[0]]]
        cleanup = [row for row in rows[protocol[-1] + 1:]]
        self.assertEqual([row for row in rows if row[0] == "default"], setup + cleanup)
        self.assertTrue(setup and cleanup and all(expect == "ok" for _, expect, _ in setup + cleanup))
        for _, _, statement in setup + cleanup:
            probe_atoms(statement)
        created = {target for _, _, statement in setup for privilege, target, _ in probe_atoms(statement) if privilege == "CREATE TABLE"}
        self.assertEqual(created, {"hg_unsafe.*", "hg_safe.*", "hg_promote.*", "devnet2.*"})
        for role in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS:
            held = role_atoms(role)
            mine = [(expect, statement, probe_atoms(statement)) for who, expect, statement in rows if who == role]
            with self.subTest(role=role):
                # Every ok row needs only grants the role holds; every denied row needs one it lacks.
                for expect, statement, atoms in mine:
                    granted = all(atom_granted(atom, held) for atom in atoms)
                    self.assertEqual(granted, expect == "ok", f"{role} {expect}: {statement}")
                # Every grant is exercised by an ok row of its role.
                for grant in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS[role]:
                    for grant_atom in grant_atoms(grant):
                        self.assertTrue(any(
                            expect == "ok" and any(atom_exercises(atom, grant_atom) for atom in atoms)
                            for expect, _, atoms in mine
                        ), f"{role}: no ok row exercises {grant_atom} of {grant!r}")
                self.assertIn("denied", [expect for expect, _, _ in mine])
        denied = {role: [atoms for who, expect, statement in rows if who == role and expect == "denied"
                         for atoms in [probe_atoms(statement)]] for role in SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS}

        def refused(role, test):
            return any(any(test(atom) for atom in atoms) for atoms in denied[role])

        # The refusals the lockdown relies on (spec §8.6, §14).
        self.assertTrue(refused("si_gateway", lambda atom: atom[:2] == ("INSERT", "hg_safe.*")))
        self.assertTrue(refused("si_gateway", lambda atom: atom[:2] == ("WRITE", "REMOTE")))
        self.assertTrue(refused("si_gateway", lambda atom: atom[0].startswith("SYSTEM ")))
        self.assertTrue(refused("si_gateway", lambda atom: atom[:2] == ("SELECT", "hg_promote.*")))
        reader_columns = next(atom[2] for atom in grant_atoms(SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS["si_reader"][-1]))
        self.assertTrue(refused("si_reader", lambda atom: atom[:2] == ("SELECT", "system.parts")
                                and atom[2] is not None and not atom[2] <= reader_columns))
```

```python
    def test_devnet2_clickhouse_logins_follow_the_rollout(self):
        indexer_b_chi = yaml.safe_load(INDEXER_B_CHI.read_text())

        access = (overlay.get("clickhouse") or {}).get("access") or {}
        network_posture = DEVNET2_CLICKHOUSE_POSTURE[FRESH_RELEASE]

        ))

                "secretKeyRef": {"name": f"{FRESH_RELEASE}-clickhouse-verifier", "key": "password"},

            }}])

                 "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b": (self.indexer_b, indexer_b)}
        self.assertEqual((set(DEVNET2_SNODE_LOGIN), set(DEVNET2_GATEWAY_LOGIN)), (set(hosts), set(hosts)))
        clients = {FRESH_RELEASE: [("verifiers", DEVNET2_VERIFIER_LOGIN, "si_verifier"),

        for name, (docs, installation) in hosts.items():

                env = {item["name"]: item for item in node.get("env") or []}

                    self.assertEqual(volumes["ckh-manager"]["secret"]["secretName"], f"{name}-clickhouse")
                    self.assertEqual(volumes["ckh-manager"]["secret"]["items"], [{"key": "ckh-manager.yaml", "path": "ckh-manager.yaml"}])
            clients[installation] += [(f"{name} SNode", snode, "si_snode"), (f"{name} gateway", gateway, "si_gateway")]
        # The order of the lockdown (K19): a client logs in as its user only once
        # its installation has that user (posture B or C), and an installation
        # locks default (C) only once every client of it logs in as its own user.
        for installation, logins in clients.items():
            posture = DEVNET2_CLICKHOUSE_POSTURE[installation]
            for client, login, user in logins:
                with self.subTest(installation=installation, client=client):
                    if login is not None:
                        self.assertEqual(login, user)
                        self.assertIn(posture, ("B", "C"), f"{client} logs in as {login} before {installation} has the user")
                    if posture == "C":
                        self.assertIsNotNone(login, f"{installation} locks default while {client} logs in as default")

        staging = yaml.safe_load(LOCKDOWN_STAGING_CHI.read_text())

        )

        self.assertEqual(configuration["users"], si_clickhouse_users("network", "A", {}))
        self.assertEqual(unlocked_files(configuration["files"]), configuration["files"])

        def shape(chi):
            spec = copy.deepcopy(chi["spec"])
            del spec["configuration"]["zookeeper"]["root"], spec["configuration"]["users"]
            spec["configuration"]["files"] = unlocked_files(spec["configuration"]["files"])
            for template in spec["templates"]["volumeClaimTemplates"]:
                del template["spec"]["resources"]["requests"]["storage"]
            return spec

        # Everything else is indexer-b's installation, which the same operator reconciles.
        self.assertEqual(shape(staging), shape(indexer_b))
        for posture in ("B", "C"):
            with self.subTest(posture=posture):
                rendered = lockdown_staging_chi(posture, TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256)
                self.assertEqual(rendered["spec"]["configuration"]["users"], si_clickhouse_users("network", posture, TEST_PASSWORD_SHA256))
                self.assertEqual(rendered["spec"]["configuration"]["files"], si_clickhouse_files(configuration["files"], posture))
                self.assertEqual(shape(rendered), shape(staging))
                self.assertEqual(rendered["metadata"], staging["metadata"])
```

```yaml
# Throwaway staging installation of the stage-3 ClickHouse lockdown (phase L,
# housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14): docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md
# §5 applies it with kubectl and §11 deletes it with its PVCs. It is indexer-b's
# source installation, storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source.yaml in
# k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2, renamed, under its own Keeper root and with
# 1Gi volumes, so the devnet2-operator that reconciles every SI
# installation reconciles exactly their shape here: the runbook proves on it
# that posture B (the si_* users) and posture C (default locked) reload in
# place and restart nothing, and runs the grant probe
# (charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv) as every role.
#
# This file is posture A. The runbook renders posture B and C from it with
# charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py's lockdown_staging_chi(posture,
# hashes): the network installation's user set (si_verifier included, so the
# probe covers every role) with the hashes of the staging logins (Secret
# storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging-logins, made by
# scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh staging).
# test_render.py keeps it equal to indexer-b's installation. No client of
# devnet2-si-v2 ever connects to it.
apiVersion: clickhouse.altinity.com/v1
kind: ClickHouseInstallation
metadata:
  name: storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging
  namespace: sentio-network-devnet2
spec:
  defaults:
    templates:
      podTemplate: clickhouse
      dataVolumeClaimTemplate: data-volume-claim
      logVolumeClaimTemplate: log-volume-claim
      clusterServiceTemplate: cluster-service
      replicaServiceTemplate: replica-service
    storageManagement:
      reclaimPolicy: Retain
  configuration:
    zookeeper:
      nodes:
        - host: clickhouse-keeper-extra-0.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local
          port: 2181
        - host: clickhouse-keeper-extra-1.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local
          port: 2181
        - host: clickhouse-keeper-extra-2.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local
          port: 2181
      session_timeout_ms: 100000
      operation_timeout_ms: 10000
      # Its own root on the shared ensemble: nothing here may join a replica
      # of devnet2-si-v2, whose tables live under /storage-integrity/devnet2/devnet2-si-v2.
      root: /storage-integrity/devnet2/lockdown-staging
    clusters:
      - name: source
        layout: {shardsCount: 1, replicasCount: 1}
    settings:
      logger/level: warning
      logger/console: "true"
      prometheus/endpoint: /metrics
      prometheus/port: 9363
      prometheus/metrics: true
      prometheus/events: true
      prometheus/asynchronous_metrics: true
      prometheus/status_info: true
      max_concurrent_queries: 500
      max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio: "0.85"
    files:
      zz-pool-settings.xml: |
        <clickhouse>
          <background_pool_size>16</background_pool_size>
          <background_fetches_pool_size>8</background_fetches_pool_size>
        </clickhouse>
    # Posture A, as every SI installation today: the lockdown runbook replaces
    # this block (and adds posture C's users.d file under files above).
    users:
      default/password: ""
      default/networks/ip:
        - 0.0.0.0/0
      default/access_management: "1"
    profiles:
      default/query_cache_nondeterministic_function_handling: ignore
      default/enable_json_type: "1"
  templates:
    podTemplates:
      - name: clickhouse
        generateName: "{chi}-{cluster}-{host}"
        podDistribution:
          - type: ClusterAffinity
        metadata:
          annotations:
            prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
            prometheus.io/path: /metrics
            prometheus.io/port: "9363"
        spec:
          automountServiceAccountToken: false
          nodeSelector:
            sentio.xyz/general: "true"
          imagePullSecrets:
            - name: google-image-secret
          containers:
            - name: clickhouse
              image: us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/sentio-352722/sentio/clickhouse-server:26.3-lts-decimal512-release-2026-09-16
              ports:
                - name: metrics
                  containerPort: 9363
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data-volume-claim
                  mountPath: /var/lib/clickhouse
              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: "2"
                  memory: 4Gi
                limits:
                  cpu: "8"
                  memory: 16Gi
    volumeClaimTemplates:
      - name: data-volume-claim
        spec:
          accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
          storageClassName: local-path
          resources:
            requests:
              storage: 1Gi
      - name: log-volume-claim
        spec:
          accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
          storageClassName: local-path
          resources:
            requests:
              storage: 1Gi
    serviceTemplates:
      - name: cluster-service
        generateName: "{chi}-{cluster}"
        spec:
          ports:
            - {name: http, port: 8123}
            - {name: tcp, port: 9000}
          type: ClusterIP
      - name: replica-service
        generateName: "{chi}-{cluster}-replica-{replica}"
        spec:
          ports:
            - {name: http, port: 8123}
            - {name: tcp, port: 9000}
            - {name: interserver, port: 9009}
          type: ClusterIP
```

```text
# The grant probe of the stage-3 ClickHouse lockdown (phase L, housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14): the "M15 grant probe" of Plan S3-A Appendix B (G-core-17).
# docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md §5 (si_grant_probe) runs every row in file order on the staging installation, as its role: clickhouse-client --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9000 --user <role>, the password from the staging logins Secret on stdin (default is the admin).
# expect ok: the statement is not refused with code 497 (any other outcome, an error included, passes); denied: it is refused with code 497.
# The rows of default set up the tables the other rows name and drop them at the end; they must succeed outright, or a denied row meets an unknown table (60) instead of 497. default runs passwordless before posture C.
```

```python
class ClickHouseLoginsScriptTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh, run against a stand-in kubectl."""

    STUB_KUBECTL = '''#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Test stand-in for kubectl: logs each call and keeps the Secrets it is asked to create."""
import json, os, sys
from pathlib import Path
state = Path(os.environ["KUBECTL_STUB_STATE"])
args = sys.argv[1:]
with (state / "calls.jsonl").open("a") as log:
    log.write(json.dumps(args) + "\\n")
if args[:4] != ["--context", "sentio-sea", "--namespace", "sentio-network-devnet2"]:
    sys.exit(f"stub kubectl: unexpected context or namespace {args}")
verb = args[4:]
path = state / "secrets.json"
secrets = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}
if verb[:2] == ["get", "secret"] and verb[3:] == ["--ignore-not-found", "-o", "name"]:
    if verb[2] in os.environ.get("KUBECTL_STUB_EXISTING", "").split() or verb[2] in secrets:
        print(f"secret/{verb[2]}")
    sys.exit(0)
if verb[:3] == ["create", "secret", "generic"]:
    data = {}
    for flag in verb[4:]:
        key, source = flag.removeprefix("--from-file=").split("=", 1)
        data[key] = {"path": source, "value": Path(source).read_text()}
    secrets[verb[3]] = data
    path.write_text(json.dumps(secrets))
    print(f"secret/{verb[3]} created")
    sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(f"stub kubectl: unexpected call {args}")
'''
    # The Secrets of each installation (contract §11): key -> the user whose password it holds.
    PLANS = {
        "network": {
            "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a-clickhouse": {"snode-password": "si_snode", "ckh-manager.yaml": "si_gateway"},
            "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-verifier": {"password": "si_verifier"},
            "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-bootstrap": {"password": "si_gateway"},
            "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-reader-network": {"password": "si_reader"},
            "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-admin-network": {"password": "default"},
        },
        **{
            f"indexer-{x}": {
                f"sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-{x}-clickhouse": {"snode-password": "si_snode", "ckh-manager.yaml": "si_gateway"},
                f"storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-reader-indexer-{x}": {"password": "si_reader"},
                f"storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-admin-indexer-{x}": {"password": "default"},
            }
            for x in ("b", "c")
        },
        "staging": {"storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging-logins": {user: user for user in SI_CLICKHOUSE_USERS["network"]}},
    }

    def run_script(self, directory, *arguments, existing=()):
        bin_dir, state, home, scratch = (directory / name for name in ("bin", "state", "home", "tmp"))
        for path in (bin_dir, state, home, scratch):
            path.mkdir()
        stub = bin_dir / "kubectl"
        stub.write_text(self.STUB_KUBECTL)
        stub.chmod(0o755)
        env = {
            "PATH": f"{bin_dir}{os.pathsep}{os.environ['PATH']}",
            "HOME": str(home),
            "TMPDIR": str(scratch),
            "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1",
            "KUBECTL_STUB_STATE": str(state),
            "KUBECTL_STUB_EXISTING": " ".join(existing),
        }
        result = subprocess.run(["bash", str(MAKE_CLICKHOUSE_LOGINS), *arguments], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
        calls_file, secrets_file = state / "calls.jsonl", state / "secrets.json"
        calls = [json.loads(line) for line in calls_file.read_text().splitlines()] if calls_file.exists() else []
        secrets = json.loads(secrets_file.read_text()) if secrets_file.exists() else {}
        return result, calls, secrets

    def test_logins_script_writes_only_hashes_and_never_prints_a_password(self):
        for installation, plan in self.PLANS.items():
            with self.subTest(installation=installation), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as name:
                directory = Path(name)
                hashes_file = directory / "hashes.yaml"
                result, calls, secrets = self.run_script(directory, installation, str(hashes_file))
                self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
                self.assertEqual({secret: set(keys) for secret, keys in secrets.items()},
                                 {secret: set(keys) for secret, keys in plan.items()})
                passwords = {}
                for secret, keys in plan.items():
                    for key, user in keys.items():
                        value = secrets[secret][key]["value"]
                        if key == "ckh-manager.yaml":
                            # HouseGate and the schema declarer read credential.subgraph only.
                            manager = yaml.safe_load(value)
                            self.assertEqual(list(manager), ["credential"])
                            self.assertEqual(list(manager["credential"]), ["subgraph"])
                            self.assertEqual(manager["credential"]["subgraph"]["username"], user)
                            value = manager["credential"]["subgraph"]["password"]
                        self.assertRegex(value, r"^[0-9a-f]{48}$")
                        self.assertEqual(passwords.setdefault(user, value), value, "one password per user and installation")
                users = SI_CLICKHOUSE_USERS["indexer" if installation.startswith("indexer-") else "network"]
                self.assertEqual(set(passwords), set(users))
                self.assertEqual(len(set(passwords.values())), len(users))
                # The hashes file holds the SHA-256 of each password, in the shape
                # clickhouse.access.passwordSha256 takes, and nothing else.
                text = hashes_file.read_text()
                self.assertEqual(yaml.safe_load(text), {"passwordSha256": {
                    user: hashlib.sha256(passwords[user].encode()).hexdigest() for user in users
                }})
                self.assertEqual(hashes_file.stat().st_mode & 0o777, 0o600)
                # No password on the terminal, on a kubectl command line or in a file left behind.
                for password in passwords.values():
                    self.assertNotIn(password, result.stdout + result.stderr + text)
                    self.assertNotIn(password, json.dumps(calls))
                self.assertTrue(all(call[:4] == ["--context", "sentio-sea", "--namespace", "sentio-network-devnet2"] for call in calls))
                for keys in secrets.values():
                    for entry in keys.values():
                        self.assertFalse(Path(entry["path"]).exists(), entry["path"])
                # mktemp -d made the plaintext directory under TMPDIR; the script removed it.
                self.assertEqual(list((directory / "tmp").iterdir()), [])

    def test_logins_script_refuses_to_overwrite_or_guess(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as name:
            directory = Path(name)
            hashes_file = directory / "hashes.yaml"
            existing = "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-admin-indexer-b"
            result, calls, secrets = self.run_script(directory, "indexer-b", str(hashes_file), existing=[existing])
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
            self.assertIn(f"Secret {existing} exists", result.stderr)
            self.assertEqual(secrets, {})
            self.assertNotIn("create", [call[4] for call in calls])
            self.assertFalse(hashes_file.exists())
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as name:
            directory = Path(name)
            hashes_file = directory / "hashes.yaml"
            hashes_file.write_text("passwordSha256: {}\n")
            result, calls, _ = self.run_script(directory, "indexer-b", str(hashes_file))
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
            self.assertIn("refusing to overwrite it", result.stderr)
            self.assertEqual(calls, [])
            self.assertEqual(hashes_file.read_text(), "passwordSha256: {}\n")
        for arguments in (("indexer-d", "hashes.yaml"), ("network",), ()):
            with self.subTest(arguments=arguments), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as name:
                result, calls, _ = self.run_script(Path(name), *arguments)
                self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2, result.stderr)
                self.assertIn("usage: bash scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh", result.stderr)
                self.assertEqual(calls, [])
```

Create `scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh` (mode 755):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Creates the ClickHouse logins of one SI ClickHouse installation of
# devnet2-si-v2 (phase L of housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14;
# docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md §4). Run it in your own
# terminal (from fish too):
#
#   bash scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh <installation> <hashes-file>
#
# <installation> is network, indexer-b, indexer-c or staging. For every user of
# that installation it generates a password (openssl rand -hex 24: 24 random
# bytes in hex), stores it only in the Kubernetes Secrets its clients read
# (context sentio-sea, namespace sentio-network-devnet2) and writes the SHA-256
# of each password to <hashes-file>:
#
#   passwordSha256:
#     <user>: "<64 lowercase hex>"
#
# which is what the installation's users take (charts/storage-integrity's
# clickhouse.access.passwordSha256, or <user>/password_sha256_hex in a CHI file).
# It never prints a password and never passes one on a command line; the
# plaintext exists only in a mode-700 temporary directory that it removes on
# exit. It refuses to overwrite an existing Secret or hashes file: a password is
# never changed in place (rotation creates a successor user, runbook §13).
set -euo pipefail
umask 077

readonly context=sentio-sea
readonly namespace=sentio-network-devnet2

usage() {
  echo "usage: bash scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh network|indexer-b|indexer-c|staging <hashes-file>" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ "$#" -eq 2 ] || usage
installation=$1
hashes_file=$2

case "$installation" in
  network) users="default si_snode si_gateway si_verifier si_reader" ;;
  indexer-b|indexer-c) users="default si_snode si_gateway si_reader" ;;
  # The staging installation carries the network's user set (grant probe).
  staging) users="default si_snode si_gateway si_verifier si_reader" ;;
  *) usage ;;
esac

# One line per Secret key: <secret> <key> <user> <format>; format plain is the
# password itself, ckh-manager the HouseGate ckh-manager file of that user.
plan() {
  case "$installation" in
    network|indexer-b|indexer-c)
      if [ "$installation" = network ]; then host=sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a; else host="sentio-node-devnet2-$installation"; fi
      printf '%s %s %s %s\n' \
        "$host-clickhouse" snode-password si_snode plain \
        "$host-clickhouse" ckh-manager.yaml si_gateway ckh-manager
      if [ "$installation" = network ]; then
        printf '%s %s %s %s\n' \
          storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-verifier password si_verifier plain \
          storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-bootstrap password si_gateway plain
      fi
      printf '%s %s %s %s\n' \
        "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-reader-$installation" password si_reader plain \
        "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-admin-$installation" password default plain
      ;;
    staging)
      for user in $users; do
        printf '%s %s %s %s\n' storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging-logins "$user" "$user" plain
      done
      ;;
  esac
}

kube() {
  kubectl --context "$context" --namespace "$namespace" "$@"
}

for tool in kubectl openssl shasum; do
  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || { echo "make-clickhouse-logins: $tool is required" >&2; exit 1; }
done
if [ -e "$hashes_file" ]; then
  echo "make-clickhouse-logins: $hashes_file exists; refusing to overwrite it" >&2
  exit 1
fi
[ -d "$(dirname "$hashes_file")" ] || { echo "make-clickhouse-logins: the directory of $hashes_file does not exist" >&2; exit 1; }

secrets=$(plan | awk '{print $1}' | uniq)
for secret in $secrets; do
  found=$(kube get secret "$secret" --ignore-not-found -o name)
  if [ -n "$found" ]; then
    echo "make-clickhouse-logins: Secret $secret exists in $namespace; refusing to overwrite it (nothing was created)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
chmod 700 "$tmp"
created=""
cleanup() {
  status=$?
  rm -rf "$tmp"
  if [ "$status" -ne 0 ] && [ -n "$created" ]; then
    echo "make-clickhouse-logins: failed after creating these Secrets:$created" >&2
    echo "make-clickhouse-logins: their passwords are lost; delete them with kubectl --context $context --namespace $namespace delete secret$created and run the script again" >&2
  fi
  exit "$status"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM

for user in $users; do
  openssl rand -hex 24 | tr -d '\n' > "$tmp/$user.password"
  grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{48}$' "$tmp/$user.password" || { echo "make-clickhouse-logins: openssl did not produce 24 random bytes" >&2; exit 1; }
  shasum -a 256 < "$tmp/$user.password" | cut -d ' ' -f 1 | tr -d '\n' > "$tmp/$user.sha256"
  grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' "$tmp/$user.sha256" || { echo "make-clickhouse-logins: shasum did not produce a SHA-256" >&2; exit 1; }
done

for secret in $secrets; do
  files=()
  while read -r name key user format; do
    [ "$name" = "$secret" ] || continue
    source="$tmp/$user.password"
    if [ "$format" = ckh-manager ]; then
      source="$tmp/$user.ckh-manager.yaml"
      {
        printf 'credential:\n  subgraph:\n    username: %s\n    password: ' "$user"
        cat "$tmp/$user.password"
        printf '\n'
      } > "$source"
    fi
    files+=("--from-file=$key=$source")
  done < <(plan)
  kube create secret generic "$secret" "${files[@]}" >/dev/null
  created="$created $secret"
  echo "created Secret $secret ($namespace)"
done

{
  echo "passwordSha256:"
  for user in $users; do
    printf '  %s: "%s"\n' "$user" "$(cat "$tmp/$user.sha256")"
  done
} > "$tmp/hashes.yaml"
(set -C; cat "$tmp/hashes.yaml" > "$hashes_file")
echo "wrote the SHA-256 of each password to $hashes_file; the passwords exist only in the Secrets above"
```

Notes (drafting decisions, Appendix B):
- **`si_ch_admin` sends no password before the lock (D9).** Measured on `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3` (26.3.51.7) with an operator-shaped users file: today's `default` (`<password></password>`) is `plaintext_password` with an empty value, and a client that sends any other password gets 516. So `si_ch_admin` pipes the admin password only once the runbook has recorded that installation's lock in `$si_lockdown_dir/locked-<installation>` (`$si_lockdown_dir` = `$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-lockdown`, this runbook's `si_backup`, a fixed directory a later runbook's `si_backup` does not move), and there is no override: each posture C block writes the record right after its apply or sync and only then waits for `system.users` (through `si_ch_admin`, so with the password), and §12.2 removes it right after the revert's apply or sync and only then waits for the reopened `default` (without). The indexer-c runbook (Task 20) writes `locked-indexer-c` there when it creates that born-locked installation.
- **Posture C is one users.d file (D7, contract §11).** `users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml` is the contract's text verbatim, `access_management` 0 included, written as a block scalar with a trailing newline. Measured on 26.3.51.7 with an operator-shaped posture C users file plus that one file: `default` is `sha256_password`, `host_ip` `[]`, `host_names` `['localhost']`, `host_names_regexp` `[]`; an unauthenticated login from another container and a passwordless one over loopback both get 516; as `default`, `CREATE USER` and `SHOW GRANTS FOR si_gateway` get 497, while `CREATE DATABASE`, `system.query_log`, `system.users` and `system.grants` keep working and named collection control stays. In `system.grants`, `default` holds 8 of `CREATE USER`, `ALTER USER`, `DROP USER`, `CREATE ROLE`, `ALTER ROLE`, `DROP ROLE`, `ROLE ADMIN`, `SHOW ACCESS` in posture A and B and none in C; `si_default_access` counts them and `si_wait_users` and the exit probe check the count.
- **The census is attribution plus coverage.** `si_census_check` maps each `query_log` address to the pod that held it when the rows were written (a pod holds an address only from its start on, so a reused address is not credited to its new holder); an address no current pod held then (pods restarted in P0) is attributed by its `client_hostname` (clickhouse-go sends `os.Hostname()`, the pod name), else to the host's own client only if its rows end before that client's current pod started, and listed; anything else is an unknown client and fails. A DinD address or a container-id hostname is a K17 stop. The operator's own `clickhouse_operator` user (its profile sets `log_queries` 0, so it should log nothing) is listed as a K18 residual, not checked. Coverage counts parent privileges, the always-accessible system tables and ClickHouse's implicit rights. Measured on 26.3: the server logs its own async-insert flushes with an empty user from `::ffff:0.0.0.0` (`query_kind` `AsyncInsertFlush`, excluded); IPv4 clients appear as `::ffff:a.b.c.d`; a `count()` of a system table records no privilege and a refused `remote()` INSERT as `default` records only `CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE` (so the probe and the soak remain necessary). A DinD pod that started inside the 7-day window stops the census (its earlier address is unknown).
- **`system.grants` is compared row by row.** The expansion of `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS` (contract §11 verbatim) into `system.grants` rows (columns `user_name`, `access_type`, `access_object`, `database`, `table`, `column`, `is_partial_revoke`, `grant_option` on 26.3) was compared with the server's own table on 26.3.51.7: 77 rows for the network installation's four users, equal, `ALTER ON devnet2.*` one row, `READ`/`REMOTE` one row and no `WRITE`.
- **The staging proof applies generated variants.** Posture A, B and C are generated from the committed staging file with that posture's users, so the proof does not depend on the posture the file was committed in. The staging installation carries the network user set, `si_verifier` included, and its logins Secret has five keys (D8), so the grant probe runs every role; a row whose role has no staging login fails the probe. The corpus's `default` rows set up and drop the probe's tables and must succeed outright (Task 16), so `si_grant_probe` runs them through `si_ch_admin` and fails a `default` row on any non-zero exit.
- **Staging lifecycle (D8).** The staging installation is deleted at the end of Task 18 (the runbook's §11, after the exit probe; contract §11 and §12). ClickHouse refuses Keeper operations until a CHI's root exists, so §5 creates `/storage-integrity/devnet2/lockdown-staging` (refusing a non-empty one) and §11 removes exactly that subtree.
- **The posture comment (D11).** §9.1's comment is Task 18 Step 15's `edit-b-posture-new.txt` text with one change: the users.d file "also removes access management". The header bullet is Task 18 Step 15's `edit-b-header-new.txt` text.
- **Post-switch traffic.** Each host step drives one HouseGate read and one `CREATE TABLE` (a wrong gateway password fails per query, not at startup; the declarer runs per `CREATE TABLE`): `devuser1.lockdown_b` on indexer 1 and `<db_a>.lockdown_a` on indexer 0 through `devuser1`'s owner's agent; §1.2 records `<db_a>` (candidate `devuser3`, seen on indexer-a's gateway in the 2026-10-09 agent log) and, only if that owner has none on indexer 0, creates permanent `lockdown_a<n>` databases until one lands there.
- **Every live commit is guarded twice:** `si_head_files` (HEAD is exactly one commit on a freshly fetched `origin/main`, so `git push origin HEAD:main` pushes that commit only, and it changes exactly the named files) and `si_render_diff` (only the CHI for users and locks; never the DinD Deployment or the `clickhouse-config` ConfigMap for a host).
