````markdown
# Storage integrity devnet2: stage-3 ClickHouse lockdown

This runbook locks every storage-integrity ClickHouse of devnet2-si-v2: the `default` user gets a password, accepts loopback connections only and loses access management, and every protocol client logs in as its own user with exactly its grants. It covers the network installation `storage-integrity-si-v2` (indexer-a's source and the three verifier ClickHouses, release `storage-integrity-si-v2`), indexer-b's installation `storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b` and a throwaway staging installation. Design: housegate `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-stage3-database-groups-design.md` §14 (ClickHouse lockdown, credentials first) and §16 row L, as clarified by the stage-3 plans (housegate `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-s3a-p0-guards.md` and `2026-10-14-multi-source-si-s3b-p0-hosts-rollout.md`, clarifications K15 to K19 and K22). It continues [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md), whose end (§11 there) is a precondition, and it supersedes the source-ClickHouse rule of §11 of [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md). indexer-c's installation is born locked by [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c.md) and is out of scope here.

| Stage | Change | Way back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | PR: the users, logins and staging support in both charts, the logins script, the staging installation, the grant probe corpus, render tests, this runbook, the stage-1 rule pointing here; inert until a value is set or a file applied | Revert the PR |
| 1 | Census of 7 days of `system.query_log` on every SI ClickHouse (§2) | None needed |
| 2 | `devnet2-operator` pinned to its live chart version, never synced (§3) | Revert the commit |
| 3 | Logins: the user's terminal creates every password, Secret and hashes file (§4) | Delete the Secrets, only before §6 |
| 4 | Staging proof (posture A, B, C restart nothing) and grant probe (§5) | Staging cleanup (§11) |
| 5 | Users, posture B: indexer-b's installation, then the network installation; `default` unchanged (§6) | Revert (§12.1) |
| 6 | Clients, one commit each: verifiers, bootstrap hook, indexer-b host, indexer-a host (§7) | Revert (§12.1) |
| 7 | Soak of at least 24 hours (§8) | Revert (§12.1) |
| 8 | Lock, posture C: indexer-b's installation, then the network installation (§9) | Revert the lock first (§12.2) |
| 9 | Exit probe (§10); staging cleanup (§11) | None needed |

Postures: A is today (`default` passwordless, open to `0.0.0.0/0`, with access management); B adds the `si_*` users with literal SHA-256 hashes and leaves `default` unchanged; C locks `default` (its own hash, `networks/ip` `127.0.0.1` and `::1`, no `default/access_management` key, and the one file `users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml`, which removes the pod addresses and host regexp the operator merges in and sets `access_management` 0, because the image's own `users.xml` grants it). Users and `users.d/` files reload in place; nothing in this runbook restarts a ClickHouse pod, and §5 proves that on the staging installation before any live change. L changes no consensus state: every step has a way back (§12) until `default` is locked, and after it once `default` is reopened.

| Installation | Users | Clients and their users |
| --- | --- | --- |
| network (`storage-integrity-si-v2`) | `default`, `si_snode`, `si_gateway`, `si_verifier`, `si_reader` | indexer-a's SNode (`si_snode`); indexer-a's HouseGate upstream and schema declarer (`si_gateway`); the release's `bootstrap-source` hook (`si_gateway`); verifier-1 to verifier-3 (`si_verifier`); `si_reader` is unused until stage 3 P2 |
| indexer-b (`storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b`) | `default`, `si_snode`, `si_gateway`, `si_reader` | indexer-b's SNode (`si_snode`); indexer-b's HouseGate upstream and schema declarer (`si_gateway`) |
| staging (`storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging`) | the users of its hashes file | none: the grant probe of §5 |

Grants are the reviewed set `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS` of `charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py`; they are confirmed three ways before `default` is locked (K15): the census of §2 (every privilege each client used in 7 days is covered by its users' grants), the grant probe of §5 (every grant has a statement that passes and the forbidden forms are refused, on an installation reconciled by the same operator), and the soak of §8 (no 497 for any `si_*` user). The DinD driver hosts keep the `clickhouse-config` ConfigMap with `default` and an empty password, byte for byte (K17): any direct dial from a driver or processor task fails closed once `default` is locked, and §2 stops this plan if the census shows one.

Every command block is bash. Run them from the root of a production checkout at `origin/main`, in order, in one dedicated `bash` session started with `set -eo pipefail` (from fish, run `bash` first). Every value a later block needs is written under `$si_backup`, so a block also runs in a new session once §0 is defined. Never run two stages in one window, never change more than one installation or one client per window, and never combine a lock (§9) with a client switch. `yq` is not used; YAML is read with `python3 -I` and PyYAML.

Every block that pushes to production `main`, syncs a release, applies, deletes or restarts a resource, creates a pod, writes Keeper, runs DDL or writes data needs explicit user confirmation in chat before it runs; each such block is preceded by the line `Confirm before running.`. Never re-run a confirmed block only to see its output: its read-only checks are in separate blocks, or `tee` their output into `$si_backup`; read that file instead.

Passwords (K16): only the user's own terminal generates them (`scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh`, §4); git and the CHIs carry only SHA-256 hashes; each plaintext lives only in its Kubernetes Secret. This runbook never prints, echoes, logs or passes a password on argv, and never copies one into `$si_backup`: the only flow it runs is a Secret read piped straight into `kubectl exec -i` stdin (`si_ch_exec`, under `si_ch_admin`, `si_login` and `si_grant_probe`). Never paste a password into chat.

Writes in this runbook: indexer-a's acceptance INSERTs into `devnet101.swap_new2` through indexer-a's sidecar, values `4101` to `4104`, one per step (`si_accept_a_track`; disjoint from the stage-3 P0 runbook's `3001` to `3004` and the indexer-c runbook's `3101` and up); the `devuser1` owner's writes through its own local agent: `devuser1.lockdown_b` (one row, then dropped) and `<db_a>.lockdown_a` (created and dropped; §1.2 records `<db_a>`); the statements of the grant probe on the staging installation; and, only if §1.2 needs it, up to four permanent `lockdown_a<n>` databases. Retryable `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` windows are expected for indexer-b's tables in §7.3 and for indexer-a's in §7.4, while that host restarts, and, since both hosts run `owner_audit: repair` from stage-3 P0 on, Pending (733, retryable) answers for that host's tables until its startup audit has completed; the verifiers roll one at a time in §7.1.

## 0. Session helpers

Define the helpers of §0 of [storage-integrity-devnet2-dynamic-table-set.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-dynamic-table-set.md), of [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md), of [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md) and of [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md) (for `si_vm_query`), unchanged and in that order, then these. They replace `si_backup`, and they redefine `si_source_ch` and `si_verifier_ch` over `si_ch_admin` with their stage-1 signatures, so every earlier runbook's block keeps working once `default` has a password.

`si_ch_admin` logs in as `default` over loopback inside the ClickHouse pod. Before an installation is locked its `default` user has an empty plaintext password, and ClickHouse refuses any password other than the empty one with 516, so `si_ch_admin` sends no password until this runbook has recorded that installation's lock (`$si_lockdown_dir/locked-<installation>`, written by §5, §9.1 and §9.2 right after the lock is applied, removed by §12.2 right after it is reverted); afterwards it pipes the admin password from the installation's admin Secret. There is no override: `si_wait_users` waits through `si_ch_admin`, so a lock wait sends the password and a reopen wait does not. The lock records and the hashes files stay in `$si_lockdown_dir` (this runbook's evidence directory) whatever `si_backup` a later runbook sets after defining these helpers, so every later runbook keeps the right choice; the indexer-c runbook writes `locked-indexer-c` there when it creates that installation, which is born locked.

```bash
si_lockdown_dir="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-lockdown"
si_backup="$si_lockdown_dir"
si_ch_image=us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/sentio-352722/sentio/clickhouse-server:25.8-lts-decimal512-2026-03-27@sha256:89839a322a59489fa14ca12e9d00f53d860b08c5486808f652a9484d7c247797
si_helm() { helm --kube-context sentio-sea -n sentio-network-devnet2 "$@"; }
# keeper-client in query mode (-q) never asks for confirmation; rmr still enforces its node limit.
si_keeper() { kubectl --context sentio-sea -n clickhouse exec clickhouse-keeper-extra-0-0 -- clickhouse-keeper-client -h localhost -p 2181 -q "$1"; }
si_stamp() { date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; }
si_dind() { si_kubectl exec "deploy/sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1-dind" -c docker -- "${@:2}"; }
si_ch_pod() { # $1 host a|b|c|v1|v2|v3|staging: its ClickHouse pod
  case "$1" in
    a) echo storage-integrity-si-v2-source-0-0-0 ;;
    b) echo storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source-0-0-0 ;;
    c) echo storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source-0-0-0 ;;
    v1|v2|v3) echo "storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-${1#v}-0-0-0" ;;
    staging) echo storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging-source-0-0-0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown host $1 (a|b|c|v1|v2|v3|staging)" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}
si_installation() { # $1 host: its ClickHouse installation (users are installation-wide)
  case "$1" in
    a|v1|v2|v3) echo network ;;
    b) echo indexer-b ;;
    c) echo indexer-c ;;
    staging) echo staging ;;
    *) echo "unknown host $1 (a|b|c|v1|v2|v3|staging)" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}
si_login_secret() { # $1 installation, $2 credential: "<Secret> <key> <format>" of the Secret that holds that credential's password (raw: the password itself; ckh: a ckh-manager.yaml)
  case "$1/$2" in
    network/default) echo "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-admin-network password raw" ;;
    network/si_snode) echo "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a-clickhouse snode-password raw" ;;
    network/si_gateway) echo "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a-clickhouse ckh-manager.yaml ckh" ;;
    network/si_gateway-bootstrap) echo "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-bootstrap password raw" ;;
    network/si_verifier) echo "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-verifier password raw" ;;
    network/si_reader) echo "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-reader-network password raw" ;;
    indexer-b/default|indexer-c/default) echo "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-admin-$1 password raw" ;;
    indexer-b/si_snode|indexer-c/si_snode) echo "sentio-node-devnet2-$1-clickhouse snode-password raw" ;;
    indexer-b/si_gateway|indexer-c/si_gateway) echo "sentio-node-devnet2-$1-clickhouse ckh-manager.yaml ckh" ;;
    indexer-b/si_reader|indexer-c/si_reader) echo "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-reader-$1 password raw" ;;
    staging/default|staging/si_snode|staging/si_gateway|staging/si_verifier|staging/si_reader) echo "storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging-logins $2 raw" ;;
    *) echo "no Secret holds credential $2 on installation $1" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}
# Runs inside the ClickHouse pod: $1 password format (none|raw|ckh), $2 user, $3 query; the password arrives on stdin and leaves only through CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD.
si_inpod_client='
fmt=$1 user=$2 query=$3
case "$fmt" in
  none) unset CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD; exec clickhouse-client --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9000 --user "$user" --query "$query" ;;
  raw) IFS= read -r CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD || [ -n "$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD" ] || { echo "no password on stdin for $user" >&2; exit 2; } ;;
  ckh) CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD="$(sed -n -e "s/^ *password: *//p" | head -n 1 | sed -e "s/^\"\(.*\)\"$/\1/")" ;;
  *) echo "unknown password format $fmt" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
[ -n "$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD" ] || { echo "empty password for $user" >&2; exit 2; }
export CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
exec clickhouse-client --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9000 --user "$user" --query "$query"
'
si_ch_exec() { # $1 host, $2 credential (none, default, si_snode, si_gateway, si_gateway-bootstrap, si_verifier, si_reader), $3 query: one query over loopback in that host's ClickHouse pod; the password goes from its Secret straight into kubectl exec stdin
  local pod inst secret key fmt
  pod="$(si_ch_pod "$1")" || return 2
  if [ "$2" = none ]; then
    si_kubectl exec -i "$pod" -c clickhouse -- sh -c "$si_inpod_client" sh none default "$3" < /dev/null
    return
  fi
  inst="$(si_installation "$1")" || return 2
  read -r secret key fmt <<< "$(si_login_secret "$inst" "$2")"
  [ -n "$fmt" ] || return 2
  si_kubectl get secret "$secret" -o "jsonpath={.data.${key//./\\.}}" | base64 -d |
    si_kubectl exec -i "$pod" -c clickhouse -- sh -c "$si_inpod_client" sh "$fmt" "${2%-bootstrap}" "$3"
}
si_ch_admin() { # $1 a|b|c|v1|v2|v3|staging, $2 query: as default over loopback; the admin password from its Secret only once $si_lockdown_dir records that installation's lock, no password before
  local inst
  inst="$(si_installation "$1")" || return 2
  if [ -e "$si_lockdown_dir/locked-$inst" ]; then
    si_ch_exec "$1" default "$2"
  else
    si_ch_exec "$1" none "$2"
  fi
}
si_source_ch() { # stage-1 signature: $1 a|b (c for indexer-c), $2 query: that indexer's source ClickHouse, now through si_ch_admin
  case "$1" in
    b) si_ch_admin b "$2" ;;
    c) si_ch_admin c "$2" ;;
    *) si_ch_admin a "$2" ;;
  esac
}
si_verifier_ch() { si_ch_admin "v$1" "$2"; } # stage-1 signature: $1 1|2|3, $2 query
si_login() { # $1 host, $2 credential: logs in over loopback with that credential's Secret and prints "<credential> ok" when the server names the expected user
  local got
  got="$(si_ch_exec "$1" "$2" "SELECT currentUser()")" || { echo "host $1: $2 cannot log in"; return 1; }
  [ "$got" = "${2%-bootstrap}" ] || { echo "host $1: $2 logged in as $got"; return 1; }
  echo "host $1: $2 ok"
}
si_users() { # $1 host: system.users as default sees it, one JSON row per user
  si_ch_admin "$1" "SELECT name, auth_type, host_ip, host_names, host_names_regexp FROM system.users ORDER BY name FORMAT JSONEachRow"
}
si_default_access() { # $1 host: how many access-management grants default holds in system.grants (8 with access management, 0 without)
  si_ch_admin "$1" "SELECT count() FROM system.grants WHERE user_name = 'default' AND access_type IN ('CREATE USER', 'ALTER USER', 'DROP USER', 'CREATE ROLE', 'ALTER ROLE', 'DROP ROLE', 'ROLE ADMIN', 'SHOW ACCESS')"
}
si_wait_users() { # $1 host, $2 posture A|B|C: polls system.users and default's access management through si_ch_admin (so the lock record must already match the posture) for up to 5 minutes until both match that posture; never waits on the CHI status
  local inst n tmp acc=unknown
  inst="$(si_installation "$1")" || return 2
  tmp="$si_backup/users-$1-wait.jsonl"
  for n in $(seq 1 30); do
    if si_users "$1" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null && acc="$(si_default_access "$1" 2>/dev/null)" && si_lockdown_py users-check "$2" "$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-$inst.yaml" "$tmp" "$acc" > /dev/null; then
      echo "host $1: $(si_lockdown_py users-check "$2" "$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-$inst.yaml" "$tmp" "$acc")"
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 10
  done
  echo "host $1: system.users did not reach posture $2 within 5 minutes"
  si_lockdown_py users-check "$2" "$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-$inst.yaml" "$tmp" "${acc:-unknown}" || true
  return 1
}
si_head_files() { # the files HEAD changes, sorted, each followed by one space; fails unless HEAD is exactly one commit on a freshly fetched origin/main and no tracked file differs from HEAD
  git fetch -q origin main || return 1
  [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" ] || { echo "HEAD is not exactly one commit on origin/main" >&2; return 1; }
  [ -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ] || { echo "the checkout has uncommitted changes" >&2; return 1; }
  git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' ' '
}
si_chi_state() { # $1 CHI: its reconcile status and operator, every pod's uid, restart count and start time, every StatefulSet's generation and revisions
  si_kubectl get chi "$1" -o jsonpath='chi {.metadata.name} status={.status.status} chop={.status.chopVersion} chop_ip={.status.chopIP}{"\n"}'
  si_kubectl get pods -l "clickhouse.altinity.com/chi=$1" -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}pod {.metadata.name} uid={.metadata.uid} restarts={.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount} started={.status.startTime}{"\n"}{end}'
  si_kubectl get statefulsets -l "clickhouse.altinity.com/chi=$1" -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}sts {.metadata.name} generation={.metadata.generation} current={.status.currentRevision} update={.status.updateRevision}{"\n"}{end}'
}
si_wait_chi() { # $1 CHI: waits up to 15 minutes for status Completed
  local n
  for n in $(seq 1 90); do
    [ "$(si_kubectl get chi "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.status}')" = Completed ] && return 0
    sleep 10
  done
  echo "CHI $1 is not Completed after 15 minutes"
  return 1
}
si_uptime() { si_ch_admin "$1" "SELECT uptime()"; }
si_runtime_uids() { # the uid of every arbiter and verifier pod of the release
  si_kubectl get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=storage-integrity-si-v2 -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.metadata.uid}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -E '^storage-integrity-si-v2-(arbiter|verifier)-[0-9] ' | sort
}
si_secret_keys() { # $1 Secret: its key names, sorted, from kubectl describe (never its values)
  si_kubectl describe secret "$1" | sed -n 's/^\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\):[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9]* bytes$/\1/p' | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' ' '
}
si_pods() { # every pod of the namespace: address, name, phase, start time
  si_kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.status.podIP}{"\t"}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.status.phase}{"\t"}{.status.startTime}{"\n"}{end}'
}
si_census() { # $1 host, $2 optional start (UTC 'YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss'; default 7 days ago): every query the host logged since then, one JSON row per user, client address, client hostname, client name, interface and used privilege ("" for a query that used none), with its first and last time in UTC
  local since="event_time >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY"
  [ -z "${2:-}" ] || since="event_time >= toDateTime('$2', 'UTC')"
  si_ch_admin "$1" "SELECT user, IPv6NumToString(address) AS addr, client_hostname, client_name, interface, priv, count() AS n, countIf(exception_code = 497) AS denied, toString(min(event_time), 'UTC') AS first, toString(max(event_time), 'UTC') AS last FROM system.query_log ARRAY JOIN if(empty(used_privileges), [''], arrayMap(p -> toString(p), used_privileges)) AS priv WHERE $since AND type != 'QueryStart' AND query_kind != 'AsyncInsertFlush' GROUP BY user, addr, client_hostname, client_name, interface, priv ORDER BY user, addr, client_hostname, client_name, interface, priv FORMAT JSONEachRow"
}
si_denials() { # $1 host, $2 start (UTC): every 497 since then by user, client address and missing privileges, with one exception text (its "(Missing permissions: ...)" part names the real gap)
  si_ch_admin "$1" "SELECT user, IPv6NumToString(address) AS addr, missing_privileges, count() AS n, min(event_time) AS first, max(event_time) AS last, any(exception) AS example FROM system.query_log WHERE event_time >= toDateTime('$2', 'UTC') AND exception_code = 497 GROUP BY user, addr, missing_privileges ORDER BY user, addr FORMAT JSONEachRow"
}
si_census_check() { # $1 host, $2 census file (si_census), $3 pods file (si_pods), then the client classes (host-a, host-b, bootstrap, verifier-1, verifier-2, verifier-3) that have switched to their own users
  si_lockdown_py census "$@"
}
si_grant_probe() { # $1 installation (staging only): every row of the committed corpus, in file order, as its role over loopback (default through si_ch_admin, every other role with its password from the staging logins Secret); one TSV line per row; fails on any row whose outcome differs from its expect column, on a default row that does not succeed outright, and on a role without a staging login
  local corpus=charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv roles role expect stmt out got code n=0 bad=0
  [ "$1" = staging ] || { echo "the grant probe runs only on the staging installation (§5)" >&2; return 2; }
  [ -s "$corpus" ] || { echo "$corpus is missing" >&2; return 2; }
  roles="$(si_secret_keys storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging-logins)" || return 2
  printf 'row\trole\texpect\tgot\tcode\tstatement\n'
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r role expect stmt <&3 || [ -n "$role" ]; do
    case "$role" in ''|'#'*|role) continue ;; esac
    n=$((n + 1))
    case " $roles" in
      *" $role "*) ;;
      *) printf '%s\t%s\t%s\tno-login\t-\t%s\n' "$n" "$role" "$expect" "$stmt"; bad=$((bad + 1)); continue ;;
    esac
    if [ "$role" = default ]; then
      if out="$(si_ch_admin staging "$stmt" 2>&1)"; then code=0; else code=""; fi
    else
      if out="$(si_ch_exec staging "$role" "$stmt" 2>&1)"; then code=0; else code=""; fi
    fi
    if [ -z "$code" ]; then
      code="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*Code: \([0-9][0-9]*\)\..*/\1/p' | head -n 1)"
      code="${code:-unknown}"
    fi
    case "$code" in
      0) got=ok ;;
      497) got=denied ;;
      209|210|unknown) got=error ;;
      # 516 is an error when this row's own login failed; a remote() leg that cannot log in answers 516 after the access check passed.
      516) if [ "$role" != default ] && ! printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q " $role: Authentication failed"; then got=ok; else got=error; fi ;;
      *) if [ "$role" = default ]; then got=error; else got=ok; fi ;;
    esac
    [ "$got" = "$expect" ] || bad=$((bad + 1))
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$n" "$role" "$expect" "$got" "$code" "$stmt"
  done 3< "$corpus"
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || { echo "the corpus has no rows" >&2; return 2; }
  [ "$bad" = 0 ] || { echo "$bad of $n rows differ from their expect column" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "every row of $n is as expected" >&2
}
si_grants() { # $1 host: system.grants of every si_* user, one JSON row per grant row
  si_ch_admin "$1" "SELECT user_name, access_type, access_object, database, table, column, is_partial_revoke, grant_option FROM system.grants WHERE startsWith(user_name, 'si_') ORDER BY user_name, access_type, database, table, column FORMAT JSONEachRow"
}
si_grants_check() { # $1 host, $2 file of si_grants: equal to SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS for the users of that installation, READ ON REMOTE without WRITE
  si_lockdown_py grants "$1" "$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-$(si_installation "$1").yaml" "$2"
}
si_anon_login() { # Services...: an unauthenticated native login as default to each, from one throwaway pod run detached; prints "<Service>: <first line of the answer>" per Service
  local pod n phase="" logged=""
  pod="si-lockdown-anon-$(date +%s)"
  si_kubectl run "$pod" --restart=Never --image="$si_ch_image" \
    --overrides='{"apiVersion":"v1","spec":{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"google-image-secret"}]}}' \
    --command -- sh -c 'for s in "$@"; do r="$(clickhouse-client --host "$s" --port 9000 --user default --query "SELECT 1" 2>&1 | head -n 1)"; echo "$s: $r"; done' sh "$@" > /dev/null || return 1
  for n in $(seq 1 90); do
    phase="$(si_kubectl get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}')" || phase=""
    case "$phase" in Succeeded|Failed) break ;; esac
    sleep 2
  done
  if si_kubectl logs "pod/$pod"; then logged=1; fi
  si_kubectl delete pod "$pod" > /dev/null || echo "could not delete pod $pod: delete it by hand" >&2
  [ "$phase" = Succeeded ] && [ -n "$logged" ] || { echo "no result from pod $pod (phase ${phase:-unknown})" >&2; return 1; }
}
si_render_diff() { # $1 release of the SI helmfile: kind/name of every rendered object that differs between HEAD~1 and HEAD (local only)
  local base rc=0 hf=k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml
  base="$(mktemp -d)"
  git archive HEAD~1 charts k8s-sea docs/examples | tar -x -C "$base" || rc=1
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] && { (cd "$base" && helmfile -f "$hf" template --selector "name=$1" --skip-deps) > "$base/old.yaml" || rc=1; }
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] && { helmfile -f "$hf" template --selector "name=$1" --skip-deps > "$base/new.yaml" || rc=1; }
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] && { si_lockdown_py render-diff "$base/old.yaml" "$base/new.yaml" || rc=1; }
  rm -rf "$base"
  return "$rc"
}
si_users_yaml() { si_lockdown_py users "$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-$1.yaml" "$2"; } # $1 installation, $2 posture A|B|C: the CHI users block to paste under spec.configuration
si_access_values() { # $1 posture B|C: the network overlay's clickhouse block (with the bootstrap login once §7.2 switched it)
  local b=no-bootstrap
  [ -e "$si_lockdown_dir/switched-bootstrap" ] && b=bootstrap
  si_lockdown_py values "$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-network.yaml" "$1" "$b"
}
si_staging_variant() { # $1 posture A|B|C: $si_backup/staging-chi-<posture>.yaml from the committed staging installation, with that posture's users
  si_lockdown_py variant docs/examples/storage-integrity-lockdown-staging-chi.yaml "$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-staging.yaml" "$1" "$si_backup/staging-chi-$1.yaml"
}
si_lockdown_py() { # the census, grants, users and render checks; imports SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS from this checkout's test_render.py
  python3 -I -B - "$@" <<'PY'
import json
import os
import re
import sys

ROLE_ORDER = ["si_snode", "si_gateway", "si_verifier", "si_reader"]
LOOPBACK_KEY = "users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml"
LOOPBACK_XML = '<clickhouse><users><default><networks replace="replace"><ip>::1</ip><ip>127.0.0.1</ip></networks><access_management>0</access_management></default></users></clickhouse>\n'
POSTURE_A_DEFAULT = {"default/password": "", "default/networks/ip": ["0.0.0.0/0"], "default/access_management": "1"}
ALWAYS_ACCESSIBLE = {"one", "contributors", "licenses", "time_zones", "collations", "formats", "privileges", "data_type_families", "database_engines", "table_engines", "table_functions", "aggregate_function_combinators", "completions", "functions", "settings", "current_roles", "enabled_roles", "quota_usage", "databases", "tables", "columns"}
SOURCE_ENGINES = {"Distributed", "URL", "File", "S3", "S3Queue", "HDFS", "MySQL", "PostgreSQL", "MaterializedPostgreSQL", "ODBC", "JDBC", "MongoDB", "Redis", "SQLite", "Kafka", "NATS", "RabbitMQ", "AzureBlobStorage", "AzureQueue", "Hive", "Iceberg", "DeltaLake", "Hudi", "ExternalDistributed", "YTsaurus", "ArrowFlight"}
CLIENTS = [
    (re.compile(r"sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-([abc])-0"), "host-{}"),
    (re.compile(r"sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-([abc])-dind-.+"), "dind-{}"),
    (re.compile(r"storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-([0-2])"), "verifier-{}"),
    (re.compile(r"storage-integrity-si-v2-bootstrap-source-.+"), "bootstrap"),
    (re.compile(r"devnet2-operator-.+"), "operator"),
]
CLASS_ROLES = {"host-a": ("si_snode", "si_gateway"), "host-b": ("si_snode", "si_gateway"), "host-c": ("si_snode", "si_gateway"), "bootstrap": ("si_gateway",), "verifier-1": ("si_verifier",), "verifier-2": ("si_verifier",), "verifier-3": ("si_verifier",)}
CLASS_HOST = {"host-a": "a", "host-b": "b", "host-c": "c", "bootstrap": "a", "verifier-1": "v1", "verifier-2": "v2", "verifier-3": "v3"}
HOST_CLASS = {"a": "host-a", "b": "host-b", "c": "host-c", "v1": "verifier-1", "v2": "verifier-2", "v3": "verifier-3"}
CLASS_POD = {"host-a": "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a-0", "host-b": "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b-0", "host-c": "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-0", "verifier-1": "storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-0", "verifier-2": "storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-1", "verifier-3": "storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-2"}


def protocol_grants():
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("charts/storage-integrity/tests"))
    import test_render
    return {user: list(grants) for user, grants in test_render.SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS.items()}


def load_hashes(path):
    import yaml
    with open(path) as f:
        doc = yaml.safe_load(f)
    if not isinstance(doc, dict) or not isinstance(doc.get("passwordSha256"), dict):
        sys.exit(f"{path}: no passwordSha256 mapping")
    hashes = doc["passwordSha256"]
    for user, value in hashes.items():
        if user != "default" and user not in ROLE_ORDER:
            sys.exit(f"{path}: unknown user {user}")
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", value):
            sys.exit(f"{path}: the hash of {user} is not 64 lowercase hex characters")
    if "default" not in hashes:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: no hash for default")
    return hashes


def roles_of(hashes):
    return [user for user in ROLE_ORDER if user in hashes]


def users_map(hashes, posture, grants):
    users = {}
    if posture == "C":
        users["default/password_sha256_hex"] = hashes["default"]
        users["default/networks/ip"] = ["127.0.0.1", "::1"]
    else:
        users.update(POSTURE_A_DEFAULT)
    if posture in ("B", "C"):
        for user in roles_of(hashes):
            users[f"{user}/password_sha256_hex"] = hashes[user]
            users[f"{user}/networks/ip"] = ["::/0"]
            users[f"{user}/profile"] = "default"
            users[f"{user}/grants/query"] = list(grants[user])
    return users


def split_top(text):
    parts, depth, cur, quoted = [], 0, "", False
    for ch in text:
        if ch == "`":
            quoted = not quoted
        elif not quoted and ch == "(":
            depth += 1
        elif not quoted and ch == ")":
            depth -= 1
        if ch == "," and depth == 0 and not quoted:
            parts.append(cur.strip())
            cur = ""
        else:
            cur += ch
    if cur.strip():
        parts.append(cur.strip())
    return parts


def unquote(name):
    name = name.strip()
    if len(name) >= 2 and name[0] == "`" and name[-1] == "`":
        return name[1:-1].replace("``", "`")
    return name


def parse_object(text):
    text = text.strip()
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(`(?:[^`]|``)*`|[^.`\s]+)\.(`(?:[^`]|``)*`|[^.`\s]+)", text)
    if m:
        return ("table", unquote(m.group(1)), unquote(m.group(2)))
    return ("param", text, None)


def parse_element(text):
    text = text.strip()
    if text.upper().startswith("GRANT "):
        text = text[6:]
    flags_text, sep, obj = text.rpartition(" ON ")
    if not sep:
        return None
    flags = []
    for part in split_top(flags_text):
        m = re.fullmatch(r"([A-Za-z][A-Za-z ]*?)\s*(?:\((.*)\))?", part.strip())
        if not m:
            return None
        cols = None if m.group(2) is None else frozenset(unquote(c) for c in split_top(m.group(2)))
        flags.append((m.group(1).upper(), cols))
    return flags, parse_object(obj)


def object_covers(g, u):
    if g[0] == "param" or u[0] == "param":
        return g == u
    if g[1] != "*" and g[1] != u[1]:
        return False
    return g[2] == "*" or g[2] == u[2]


def flag_covers(gname, gcols, uname, ucols):
    if gname == "ALL":
        return True
    if gname == uname:
        return gcols is None or (ucols is not None and ucols <= gcols)
    return gname in ("ALTER", "SYSTEM", "CREATE", "DROP", "SHOW") and uname.startswith(gname + " ")


def granted_by(elements, name, cols, obj):
    return any(object_covers(gobj, obj) and any(flag_covers(g, gc, name, cols) for g, gc in gflags) for gflags, gobj in elements)


def covered(priv, elements):
    parsed = parse_element(priv)
    if parsed is None:
        return False
    flags, obj = parsed
    for name, cols in flags:
        if granted_by(elements, name, cols, obj):
            continue
        if name == "TABLE ENGINE" and obj[0] == "param" and obj[1] not in SOURCE_ENGINES:
            continue
        if name == "SELECT" and obj[0] == "table" and obj[1] == "system" and obj[2] in ALWAYS_ACCESSIBLE:
            continue
        if name.startswith("SHOW ") and obj[0] == "table" and any(gobj[0] == "table" and gobj[1] in ("*", obj[1]) for _, gobj in elements):
            continue
        if name == "CREATE VIEW" and granted_by(elements, "CREATE TABLE", None, obj):
            continue
        if name == "DROP VIEW" and granted_by(elements, "DROP TABLE", None, obj):
            continue
        if name in ("CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE", "CREATE ARBITRARY TEMPORARY TABLE") and any(g == "CREATE TABLE" for gflags, _ in elements for g, _ in gflags):
            continue
        if name == "ALTER MOVE PARTITION" and granted_by(elements, "SELECT", None, obj) and granted_by(elements, "ALTER DELETE", None, obj):
            continue
        return False
    return True


def elements_of(grant_list):
    out = []
    for grant in grant_list:
        parsed = parse_element(grant)
        if parsed is None:
            sys.exit(f"SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS: cannot parse {grant!r}")
        out.append(parsed)
    return out


def read_jsonl(path):
    with open(path) as f:
        return [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]


def classify(name):
    for pattern, fmt in CLIENTS:
        m = pattern.fullmatch(name or "")
        if m:
            if fmt == "verifier-{}":
                return fmt.format(int(m.group(1)) + 1)
            return fmt.format(*m.groups())
    return None


def cmd_users(hashes_path, posture):
    hashes = load_hashes(hashes_path)
    grants = protocol_grants()
    print("    users:")
    for key, value in users_map(hashes, posture, grants).items():
        if isinstance(value, list):
            print(f"      {key}:")
            for item in value:
                print(f"        - {json.dumps(item)}")
        else:
            print(f"      {key}: {json.dumps(value)}")


def cmd_values(hashes_path, posture, bootstrap):
    hashes = load_hashes(hashes_path)
    print("clickhouse:")
    print("  # Stage-3 ClickHouse lockdown (docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md):")
    print("  # literal SHA-256 hashes only; every password lives in a Kubernetes Secret.")
    print("  access:")
    print("    users: true")
    if posture == "C":
        print("    lockDefault: true")
    if bootstrap == "bootstrap":
        print("    bootstrapPasswordSecret:")
        print("      name: storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-bootstrap")
        print("      key: password")
    print("    passwordSha256:")
    if posture == "C":
        print(f"      default: {json.dumps(hashes['default'])}")
    for user in roles_of(hashes):
        print(f"      {user}: {json.dumps(hashes[user])}")


def cmd_variant(example, hashes_path, posture, out):
    import yaml
    hashes = load_hashes(hashes_path)
    grants = protocol_grants()
    with open(example) as f:
        doc = yaml.safe_load(f)
    if doc.get("kind") != "ClickHouseInstallation" or doc["metadata"]["name"] != "storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging":
        sys.exit(f"{example} is not the staging installation")
    conf = doc["spec"]["configuration"]
    conf["users"] = users_map(hashes, posture, grants)
    files = dict(conf.get("files") or {})
    files.pop(LOOPBACK_KEY, None)
    if posture == "C":
        files[LOOPBACK_KEY] = LOOPBACK_XML
    conf["files"] = files
    with open(out, "w") as f:
        yaml.safe_dump(doc, f, sort_keys=False, default_flow_style=False, width=1000)
    print(f"{out}: staging installation in posture {posture}, users {', '.join(['default'] + roles_of(hashes))}")


def cmd_users_check(posture, hashes_path, users_path, access):
    hashes = load_hashes(hashes_path)
    rows = {row["name"]: row for row in read_jsonl(users_path)}
    problems = []
    if not access.isdigit():
        problems.append(f"default's access-management grants could not be read ({access!r})")
    elif posture == "C" and int(access) != 0:
        problems.append(f"default keeps {access} access-management grants in posture C")
    elif posture != "C" and int(access) == 0:
        problems.append("default has no access management before posture C")
    for user in roles_of(hashes):
        row = rows.get(user)
        if posture == "A":
            if row is not None:
                problems.append(f"{user} exists in posture A")
            continue
        if row is None:
            problems.append(f"{user} is missing")
        elif row["auth_type"] != ["sha256_password"] or "::/0" not in row["host_ip"]:
            problems.append(f"{user}: auth_type {row['auth_type']}, host_ip {row['host_ip']}")
    default = rows.get("default")
    if default is None:
        problems.append("default is missing")
    elif posture == "C":
        local_only = set(default["host_ip"]) <= {"127.0.0.1", "::1"} and set(default["host_names"]) <= {"localhost"} and default["host_names_regexp"] == [] and (default["host_ip"] or default["host_names"])
        if default["auth_type"] != ["sha256_password"] or not local_only:
            problems.append(f"default is not locked: auth_type {default['auth_type']}, host_ip {default['host_ip']}, host_names {default['host_names']}, host_names_regexp {default['host_names_regexp']}")
    elif default["auth_type"] == ["sha256_password"]:
        problems.append("default has a password before posture C")
    for p in problems:
        print(f"  {p}")
    if problems:
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"system.users matches posture {posture} (default access-management grants: {access})")


def utc(stamp):
    # '2026-10-14T00:00:00Z' (a pod's startTime) or '2026-10-14 00:00:00' (si_census) -> '2026-10-14 00:00:00'
    return (stamp or "").replace("T", " ").rstrip("Z")


def cmd_census(host, census_path, pods_path, switched):
    grants = {user: elements_of(g) for user, g in protocol_grants().items()}
    pods = []
    with open(pods_path) as f:
        for line in f:
            fields = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            if len(fields) >= 4 and fields[0] and fields[1]:
                pods.append((fields[0], fields[1], utc(fields[3])))
    started = {name: start for _, name, start in pods}
    failures, notes, groups, counted = [], [], {}, {}

    def count(message, n):
        counted[message] = counted.get(message, 0) + n

    for row in read_jsonl(census_path):
        addr, hostname, user, priv = row["addr"], row.get("client_hostname") or "", row["user"], row.get("priv") or ""
        n, denied = int(row["n"]), int(row["denied"])
        first, last = utc(row.get("first")), utc(row.get("last"))
        if user == "clickhouse_operator":
            notes.append(f"{n} queries of the operator's own clickhouse_operator user from {addr} (a K18 residual, not an SI client)")
            continue
        if addr == "::1" or addr.startswith("::ffff:127.") or addr.startswith("127."):
            cls, note = "loopback", None
        else:
            ip = addr[7:] if addr.startswith("::ffff:") else addr
            # A pod holds its address only from its start on: rows older than the pod are an earlier holder's.
            holders = [(start, name) for pip, name, start in pods if pip == ip and start]
            current = sorted(h for h in holders if first and h[0] <= first)
            if current:
                pod = current[-1][1]
                cls, note = classify(pod) or f"other:{pod}", None
            elif re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{12}", hostname):
                cls, note = "possible-dind", f"former address {addr} with a container-id client_hostname {hostname}"
            else:
                cls = classify(hostname)
                if cls is not None:
                    note = f"former address {addr} (client_hostname {hostname!r}, user {user}): attributed to {cls} by its client hostname"
                else:
                    own = HOST_CLASS[host]
                    own_start = started.get(CLASS_POD[own], "")
                    # the host's own client: an earlier pod of it (rows that end before its current pod started), or its current pod at the same address again
                    if not ((own_start and last and last < own_start) or any(name == CLASS_POD[own] for _, name in holders)):
                        count(f"queries from {addr} (client_hostname {hostname!r}, client_name {row.get('client_name')!r}, user {user}, last {last} UTC) that no pod of the namespace held and no client hostname names, after {CLASS_POD[own]} started ({own_start or 'not found'}): an unknown client", n)
                        continue
                    cls = own
                    when = f"before {CLASS_POD[own]} started ({own_start})" if own_start and last and last < own_start else f"at the address {CLASS_POD[own]} holds again"
                    note = f"former address {addr} (client_hostname {hostname!r}, client_name {row.get('client_name')!r}, user {user}, last {last} UTC): {when}, attributed to {own}"
        if note:
            notes.append(note)
        if cls.startswith("dind-") or cls == "possible-dind":
            count(f"K17: queries from a DinD address ({cls}, {addr}, user {user}): stop and amend the plan (si_driver)", n)
            continue
        if cls.startswith("other:") or cls == "operator":
            count(f"queries from {cls[6:] if cls.startswith('other:') else 'the operator pod'} ({addr}, user {user}), which is no SI client", n)
            continue
        if cls != "loopback" and CLASS_HOST[cls] != host:
            count(f"queries from {cls} ({addr}) on host {host}, which it never uses", n)
            continue
        if user.startswith("si_") and denied:
            count(f"queries of {user} from {cls} ({addr}) were refused with 497 (si_denials shows the missing privileges)", denied)
        if cls in switched and user == "default":
            count(f"queries from {cls} ({addr}) still log in as default after its switch", n)
        groups.setdefault((cls, user), {}).setdefault(priv, 0)
        groups[(cls, user)][priv] += n
    failures.extend(f"{n} {message}" for message, n in sorted(counted.items()))
    for (cls, user), privs in sorted(groups.items()):
        total = sum(privs.values())
        if cls == "loopback" and user == "default":
            print(f"host {host}: loopback default (this runbook's admin sessions): {total} queries")
            continue
        if user == "default":
            roles = CLASS_ROLES[cls]
        elif cls == "loopback" and user in grants:
            roles = (user,)
        elif cls != "loopback" and user in CLASS_ROLES[cls]:
            roles = (user,)
        else:
            failures.append(f"{total} queries of {user} from {cls}, which is not one of its users")
            continue
        elements = [e for role in roles for e in grants[role]]
        used = sorted(p for p in privs if p)
        missing = [p for p in used if not covered(p, elements)]
        print(f"host {host}: {cls} as {user}: {total} queries, {len(used)} distinct privileges, checked against {'+'.join(roles)}")
        for p in missing:
            failures.append(f"{cls} as {user} used {p!r}, which {'+'.join(roles)} does not grant")
    for note in sorted(set(notes)):
        print(f"host {host}: note: {note}")
    for failure in failures:
        print(f"host {host}: FAIL: {failure}")
    if failures:
        print(f"host {host}: census NOT clean")
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"host {host}: census clean")


def expected_grant_rows(user, grant_list):
    rows = set()
    for flags, obj in elements_of(grant_list):
        for name, cols in flags:
            if obj[0] == "param":
                keys = [(name, obj[1], None, None, None)]
            else:
                database = None if obj[1] == "*" else obj[1]
                table = None if obj[2] == "*" else obj[2]
                keys = [(name, "", database, table, col) for col in (sorted(cols) if cols else [None])]
            for key in keys:
                rows.add((user,) + key + (0, 0))
    return rows


def cmd_grants(host, hashes_path, grants_path):
    hashes = load_hashes(hashes_path)
    grants = protocol_grants()
    expected = set()
    for user in roles_of(hashes):
        expected |= expected_grant_rows(user, grants[user])
    actual = set()
    for row in read_jsonl(grants_path):
        actual.add((row["user_name"], row["access_type"], row["access_object"], row["database"], row["table"], row["column"], int(row["is_partial_revoke"]), int(row["grant_option"])))
    for row in sorted(expected - actual, key=str):
        print(f"host {host}: missing grant row {row}")
    for row in sorted(actual - expected, key=str):
        print(f"host {host}: unexpected grant row {row}")
    write_remote = [r for r in actual if r[1] == "WRITE"]
    read_remote = [r for r in actual if r[0] == "si_gateway" and r[1] == "READ" and r[2] == "REMOTE"]
    print(f"host {host}: si_gateway READ ON REMOTE rows {len(read_remote)}, WRITE rows of any si_* user {len(write_remote)}")
    if expected != actual or write_remote or not read_remote:
        print(f"host {host}: system.grants does NOT equal SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS")
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"host {host}: system.grants equals SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS for {', '.join(roles_of(hashes))}")


def cmd_render_diff(old_path, new_path):
    import yaml

    def index(path):
        out = {}
        with open(path) as f:
            for doc in yaml.safe_load_all(f):
                if doc:
                    out[f"{doc.get('kind')}/{doc.get('metadata', {}).get('name')}"] = doc
        if not out:
            sys.exit(f"{path} rendered nothing")
        return out

    old, new = index(old_path), index(new_path)
    lines = [f"changed {k}" for k in sorted(old.keys() & new.keys()) if old[k] != new[k]]
    lines += [f"added {k}" for k in sorted(new.keys() - old.keys())]
    lines += [f"removed {k}" for k in sorted(old.keys() - new.keys())]
    print("\n".join(lines) if lines else "no rendered object differs")


def main(argv):
    cmd = argv[0] if argv else ""
    if cmd == "users" and len(argv) == 3 and argv[2] in ("A", "B", "C"):
        cmd_users(argv[1], argv[2])
    elif cmd == "values" and len(argv) == 4 and argv[2] in ("B", "C") and argv[3] in ("bootstrap", "no-bootstrap"):
        cmd_values(argv[1], argv[2], argv[3])
    elif cmd == "variant" and len(argv) == 5 and argv[3] in ("A", "B", "C"):
        cmd_variant(argv[1], argv[2], argv[3], argv[4])
    elif cmd == "users-check" and len(argv) == 5 and argv[1] in ("A", "B", "C"):
        cmd_users_check(argv[1], argv[2], argv[3], argv[4])
    elif cmd == "census" and len(argv) >= 4 and argv[1] in HOST_CLASS:
        cmd_census(argv[1], argv[2], argv[3], set(argv[4:]))
    elif cmd == "grants" and len(argv) == 4:
        cmd_grants(argv[1], argv[2], argv[3])
    elif cmd == "render-diff" and len(argv) == 3:
        cmd_render_diff(argv[1], argv[2])
    else:
        sys.exit("usage: users <hashes> A|B|C | values <hashes> B|C bootstrap|no-bootstrap | variant <example> <hashes> A|B|C <out> | users-check A|B|C <hashes> <users.jsonl> <default access-management grants> | census <host> <census.jsonl> <pods.tsv> [<switched class>...] | grants <host> <hashes> <grants.jsonl> | render-diff <old> <new>")


main(sys.argv[1:])
PY
}
```

`si_census_check` attributes every row to a client by its address: loopback is this runbook's admin and probe sessions; an address of a pod that held it since before the rows were written names that pod (`sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-<x>-0` is that host's SNode, HouseGate upstream and schema declarer, `storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-<n>` is verifier `n+1`, `storage-integrity-si-v2-bootstrap-source-*` is the hook); any other address is a restarted pod's earlier address and is attributed by the client hostname the query carries, else to that host's own client but only when its rows end before that client's current pod started or that pod holds the address again, and listed as a note; rows of the operator's own `clickhouse_operator` user are listed, not checked (a K18 residual; its profile logs no queries). It fails on an address no pod and no client hostname accounts for, on a DinD address or a container-id hostname (K17), on any other pod of the namespace (the operator pod included), on a client seen on a host it never uses, on a 497 of an `si_*` user, on a switched client that still logs in as `default`, and on any used privilege the client's users do not grant (its parent privileges, the always-accessible system tables, the implicit `SHOW`, view, temporary-table and `ALTER MOVE PARTITION` rights, and `TABLE ENGINE` of a non-source engine count as granted). `query_log` records only the checks that throw, so a query that reads no column (a `count()` of a system table) and a query refused before a later check leave no privilege behind; the grant probe and the soak cover those.

## 1. Preparation

### 1.1 Pins

| Component | Pin | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arbiter voters and verifiers | `ghcr.io/sentioxyz/arbiter:<ARBITER_TAG>@<ARBITER_DIGEST>`: the verifiers read `clickhouse_username` and `ARBITER_VERIFIER_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` | stage-3 P0 runbook §1.1 |
| sentio-node, indexer-a and indexer-b | `ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-<SN_COMMIT>@<SN_DIGEST>`: the SNode reads `storage_integrity.clickhouse_username` and `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD`; the embedded HouseGate and the schema declarer read `credential.subgraph` from `housegate.ckh_manager_config_path` | stage-3 P0 runbook §1.1 |
| ClickHouse, every SI installation | `us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/sentio-352722/sentio/clickhouse-server:26.3-lts-decimal512-release-2026-09-16`, unchanged | the CHIs |
| `devnet2-operator` | the live chart version, read in §2 and pinned in §3 | `helm list` |

An older host image ignores `clickhouse_username` and keeps logging in as `default`, which only the census reveals; an older verifier image cannot log in at all. So every client of this runbook must run these pins before §7.

```bash
[ ! -e "$si_backup" ] || { echo "$si_backup exists: this runbook starts a fresh evidence directory; move the old one aside"; exit 1; }
mkdir -m 700 "$si_backup"
ARBITER_TAG='<ARBITER_TAG>'; ARBITER_DIGEST='<ARBITER_DIGEST>'; SN_COMMIT='<SN_COMMIT>'; SN_DIGEST='<SN_DIGEST>'
case "$ARBITER_TAG$ARBITER_DIGEST$SN_COMMIT$SN_DIGEST" in *'<'*) echo "pins are still placeholders; stop"; exit 1;; esac
[ "$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/arbiter:$ARBITER_TAG" | sed -n 's/^Digest: *//p')" = "$ARBITER_DIGEST" ]
[ "$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-$SN_COMMIT" | sed -n 's/^Digest: *//p')" = "$SN_DIGEST" ]
printf '%s\n' "$ARBITER_TAG" "$ARBITER_DIGEST" "$SN_COMMIT" "$SN_DIGEST" > "$si_backup/pins"
si_images | tee "$si_backup/images-before.txt"
awk -F'\t' -v d="@$ARBITER_DIGEST" '$1 ~ /verifier/ && index($2, d) == 0 {bad = 1} END {exit bad}' "$si_backup/images-before.txt" || { echo "a verifier does not run $ARBITER_TAG; finish stage-3 P0 first"; exit 1; }
for x in a b; do
  [ "$(si_node_image "$x")" = "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-$SN_COMMIT@$SN_DIGEST" ] || { echo "indexer-$x does not run sentio-node $SN_COMMIT; finish stage-3 P0 first"; exit 1; }
done
echo "pins resolve"
```

Expected: `pins resolve`.

### 1.2 Identities and Secrets

| Host (`si_ch_admin`) | Installation | ClickHouse pod | Service (9000, 8123) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `a` | network | `storage-integrity-si-v2-source-0-0-0` | `storage-integrity-si-v2-source` |
| `v1`, `v2`, `v3` | network | `storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-<n>-0-0-0` | `storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-<n>` |

| Installation | Secret | Keys | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| network | `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a-clickhouse` | `snode-password`, `ckh-manager.yaml` | indexer-a's sentio-node container (env `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD`; file `/etc/sentio-ckh/ckh-manager.yaml`) |

Each `ckh-manager.yaml` is `credential:` / `  subgraph:` / `    username: si_gateway` / `    password: <hex>`; HouseGate and the schema declarer read nothing else from it. The hashes files `$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-<installation>.yaml` hold only `passwordSha256:` (user → SHA-256 hex); hashes are not secret.

The test tables of §7 need one database of `devuser1`'s owner on each SI host: `devuser1` on indexer 1 (as in the stage-1 and stage-2 runbooks) and `<db_a>` on indexer 0. Set `db_a` to a database of that owner that indexer 0 hosts and record it:

```bash
db_a=devuser3
r="$(si_rpc "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"sentio_getDatabaseInfoById\",\"params\":[\"$db_a\"]}" | jq -c '.result | {databaseId, indexerId, pendingDelete}')"
echo "$r"
[ "$(printf '%s' "$r" | jq -r '"\(.indexerId) \(.pendingDelete)"')" = "0 false" ] || { echo "$db_a is not a live database of indexer 0: set db_a to another database of devuser1's owner, or create one with the next block"; exit 1; }
printf '%s\n' "$db_a" > "$si_backup/db-a"
si_rpc '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"sentio_getDatabaseInfoById","params":["devuser1"]}' | jq -c '.result | {databaseId, indexerId, pendingDelete}'
```

Expected: `{"databaseId":"<db_a>","indexerId":0,"pendingDelete":false}` and `{"databaseId":"devuser1","indexerId":1,"pendingDelete":false}`. The RPC does not name a database's owner: if `<db_a>` is not `devuser1`'s owner's, §7.4's `CREATE TABLE` is refused and stops that step before anything changes. Only when the owner has no database on indexer 0: the next block creates `lockdown_a1` to `lockdown_a4` through the owner's agent until one lands on indexer 0 (the assignment is the contract's round-robin over the active indexers; every database is permanent on chain, a DROP only marks it pending delete).

Confirm before running.

```bash
key_file=/path/to/devuser1-owner.key
si_agent_start "$key_file"
for n in 1 2 3 4; do
  db="lockdown_a$n"
  si_agent_ch --query "CREATE DATABASE $db"
  sleep 20
  id="$(si_rpc "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"sentio_getDatabaseInfoById\",\"params\":[\"$db\"]}" | jq -r '.result.indexerId')"
  echo "$db -> indexer $id" | tee -a "$si_backup/db-a-attempts.txt"
  if [ "$id" = 0 ]; then printf '%s\n' "$db" > "$si_backup/db-a"; break; fi
done
si_agent_stop
test -s "$si_backup/db-a" || { echo "no new database landed on indexer 0; stop and decide"; exit 1; }
```

The installations and their pods (read-only):

```bash
si_kubectl get pods -o wide | grep -E '^(storage-integrity-si-v2-(source|verifier-[123]|indexer-b-source)-0-0-0|sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-[ab]-0|storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-[012]) ' | tee "$si_backup/pods-identities.txt"
si_kubectl get services storage-integrity-si-v2-source storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-1 storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-2 storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-3 storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source
for h in a v1 v2 v3 b; do printf '%s ' "$h"; si_ch_admin "$h" "SELECT version(), currentUser() FORMAT TSV"; done | tee "$si_backup/servers.txt"
for x in a b; do si_info "$x"; done | tee "$si_backup/info-before.json"
```

Expected: four CHI pods of the network installation and indexer-b's, both hosts and the three verifier pods Running; every server answers `26.3.…` and `default`; `si_info a` with `"si_indexer_id":0,"enrolled":true` and `si_info b` with `"si_indexer_id":1,"enrolled":true`.

## 2. Census

Read-only. The census decides whether the grants of `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS` cover every client (K15) and whether any driver or processor task dials a source ClickHouse directly (K17). Today every client logs in as `default`, which holds every privilege, so `query_log.used_privileges` lists exactly what each client exercises.

First the operator, its restart policy and the reconciler of each CHI:

```bash
si_helm list --filter '^devnet2-operator$' -o json | jq -c '.[] | {name, chart, app_version, revision, updated}' | tee "$si_backup/operator-release.json"
chart="$(jq -r .chart "$si_backup/operator-release.json")"
case "$chart" in
  altinity-clickhouse-operator-*) printf '%s\n' "${chart#altinity-clickhouse-operator-}" > "$si_backup/operator-chart-version" ;;
  *) echo "unexpected operator chart $chart; stop"; exit 1 ;;
esac
si_kubectl get deployments -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=devnet2-operator -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{range .spec.template.spec.containers[*]} {.name}={.image}{end}{"\n"}{end}' | tee "$si_backup/operator-deploy.txt"
si_kubectl get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=devnet2-operator -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.podIP} {.status.startTime}{"\n"}{end}' | tee "$si_backup/operator-pods.txt"
for chi in storage-integrity-si-v2 storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b; do si_chi_state "$chi"; done | tee "$si_backup/chi-census.txt"
op_ip="$(awk 'NR == 1 {print $2}' "$si_backup/operator-pods.txt")"
if grep '^chi ' "$si_backup/chi-census.txt" | grep -qv "chop_ip=$op_ip\$"; then echo "a CHI was last reconciled by another operator than devnet2-operator ($op_ip); stop"; exit 1; fi
cm="$(si_kubectl get configmaps -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=devnet2-operator -o name | grep -- '-etc-clickhouse-operator-files$' || true)"
[ -n "$cm" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$cm" | wc -l)" -eq 1 ] || { echo "expected one operator ConfigMap *-etc-clickhouse-operator-files (the one holding config.yaml), got: $cm"; exit 1; }
si_kubectl get "$cm" -o jsonpath='{.data.config\.yaml}' > "$si_backup/operator-config.yaml"
python3 -I -c 'import json, sys, yaml
cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))
print(json.dumps({"watch": cfg.get("watch"), "configurationRestartPolicy": cfg.get("clickhouse", {}).get("configurationRestartPolicy"), "reconcile": cfg.get("reconcile")}, indent=1))' "$si_backup/operator-config.yaml" | tee "$si_backup/operator-policy.json"
echo "OPERATOR_CHART_VERSION $(cat "$si_backup/operator-chart-version")"
```

Expected: one release, chart `altinity-clickhouse-operator-0.27.2` and app version `0.27.2` (read 2026-10-11 from the CHIs' status), its image `…/clickhouse-operator:0.27.2`, and both CHIs `status=Completed chop=0.27.2` with `chop_ip` equal to the operator pod's address; the restart policy has no `users` rule (users never restart a pod), restarts on `files/*.xml`, `settings/*` and `zookeeper/*`, and the operator ignores `users.d/` files when it compares. The printed version is `OPERATOR_CHART_VERSION` (kept in `$si_backup/operator-chart-version`; Plan S3-B Task 18 records it in that plan's Appendix C with `L_END`). A chart version that differs from the CHIs' `chopVersion`, or an operator other than `devnet2-operator`: stop.

Then each server: version, seven days of `query_log`, its privilege columns, the effective access-control settings, and its users:

```bash
for h in a b v1 v2 v3; do
  echo "== $h"
  si_ch_admin "$h" "SELECT version(), uptime(), (SELECT min(event_time) FROM system.query_log) AS log_start, (SELECT min(event_time) <= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY FROM system.query_log) AS seven_days FORMAT TSV"
  si_ch_admin "$h" "SELECT name, type FROM system.columns WHERE database = 'system' AND table = 'query_log' AND name LIKE '%privileges' FORMAT TSV"
  si_kubectl exec "$(si_ch_pod "$h")" -c clickhouse -- grep -E '<(select_from_system_db_requires_grant|table_engines_require_grant|on_cluster_queries_require_cluster_grant|enable_read_write_grants)>' /var/lib/clickhouse/preprocessed_configs/config.xml || echo "none of these access_control_improvements settings is set: the code defaults apply (select_from_system_db_requires_grant true, table_engines_require_grant false)"
  si_users "$h"
  printf 'default access-management grants: '; si_default_access "$h"
done 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/servers-census.txt"
```

Expected: `26.3.…` everywhere and `seven_days` `1`; `used_privileges` and `missing_privileges` of type `Array(LowCardinality(String))`; `select_from_system_db_requires_grant` `true` (the grants list `SELECT ON system.<table>` for that reason), `table_engines_require_grant` `false` (so a `TABLE ENGINE` of a non-source engine needs no grant), `on_cluster_queries_require_cluster_grant` `true`, and no `enable_read_write_grants` line; `system.users` lists `default` (`plaintext_password`) and the operator's `clickhouse_operator`, nothing else; `default access-management grants: 8`. A `seven_days` of `0` means the log is younger than the census window: wait, then repeat this section.

Then the DinD driver hosts: their pods must have run for the whole window (so their address is the one the census can see), and a driver must run on each (otherwise the census cannot clear that host):

```bash
si_kubectl get pods -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-[ab]-dind-")) | "\(.metadata.name) \(.status.podIP) \(.status.startTime) \(if ((.status.startTime | fromdateiso8601) < (now - 7 * 86400)) then "started-more-than-7-days-ago" else "STARTED-WITHIN-7-DAYS" end)"' | tee "$si_backup/dind-census.txt"
for x in a b; do
  for kind in driver processor; do
    printf 'indexer-%s %s containers: %s\n' "$x" "$kind" "$(si_dind "$x" docker ps --filter label=sentio.managed_by=sentio-core --filter "label=sentio.service.type=$kind" -q | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  done
done | tee -a "$si_backup/dind-census.txt"
if grep -q 'STARTED-WITHIN-7-DAYS' "$si_backup/dind-census.txt"; then echo "a DinD pod started within the census window, so its earlier address is unknown: repeat §2 once it has run 7 days"; exit 1; fi
if grep -q 'driver containers: 0$' "$si_backup/dind-census.txt"; then echo "no driver runs on one host: the census cannot clear it; decide with the user before going on"; exit 1; fi
```

Expected: both DinD pods `started-more-than-7-days-ago`; at least one driver container on each host.

The census itself, 7 days on every server, attributed by client address:

```bash
si_pods > "$si_backup/pods-census.tsv"
rc=0
for h in a b v1 v2 v3; do
  si_census "$h" > "$si_backup/census-$h.jsonl"
  si_census_check "$h" "$si_backup/census-$h.jsonl" "$si_backup/pods-census.tsv" > "$si_backup/census-check-$h.txt" || rc=1
  cat "$si_backup/census-check-$h.txt"
done
[ "$rc" = 0 ] || { echo "the census is not clean: stop (K15, K17)"; exit 1; }
```

Expected, per host: `census clean`; on `a` the classes `host-a as default` (checked against `si_snode+si_gateway`), `bootstrap as default` if the hook ran within 7 days (against `si_gateway`) and `loopback default`; on `b` `host-b as default`; on `vN` `verifier-N as default` (against `si_verifier`); notes for former addresses of pods that restarted during stage-3 P0, each attributed to the client its hostname names or, with another hostname, to the host's own client because its rows end before that client's current pod started. Read every note: each must be an address a restarted host, verifier or hook pod used before its restart. Any `FAIL` (an unknown client included): stop. A `K17` line (a DinD address or a container-id hostname) means a driver or processor task dials the source ClickHouse directly: stop and amend the plan (a tenant-only `si_driver` user on `devnet2.*` and a planned DinD window); never put an SI user into the `clickhouse-config` ConfigMap, which tenant code can read. An uncovered privilege means `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS` misses something a client needs: stop and amend the grants in a reviewed change, with a new census and probe.

## 3. Operator pin

`devnet2-operator` is declared in `k8s-sea/clickhouse/helmfile.yaml` without a version, so a sync of that file could upgrade the operator and re-reconcile every devnet2 CHI (K22). One commit pins it to the live version and is never synced: under `- name: devnet2-operator` (after its `chart:` line) add the line `    version: <OPERATOR_CHART_VERSION>` with the version §2 recorded, for example `    version: 0.27.2`. Commit subject: `chore(clickhouse): pin devnet2-operator to its live chart version`.

Confirm before running.

```bash
v="$(cat "$si_backup/operator-chart-version")"
[ "$(si_head_files)" = "k8s-sea/clickhouse/helmfile.yaml " ] || { echo "HEAD is not the operator pin commit"; exit 1; }
[ "$(git diff --numstat HEAD~1 HEAD | awk '{print $1, $2}')" = "1 0" ] || { echo "the pin commit must add exactly one line"; exit 1; }
git show HEAD:k8s-sea/clickhouse/helmfile.yaml | grep -A3 -- '- name: devnet2-operator' | grep -qx "    version: $v" || { echo "devnet2-operator is not pinned to $v"; exit 1; }
git rev-parse HEAD > "$si_backup/lockdown-operator-pin-commit"
git push origin HEAD:main
```

Never run `helmfile` against `k8s-sea/clickhouse/helmfile.yaml` during stage 3 (§13): the pin only makes a later sync convergent. CHI files go through `kubectl apply`.

## 4. Logins (user action)

The user, in their own terminal (fish), from the root of the same production checkout, generates every password and Secret. Each run creates that installation's Secrets in `sentio-network-devnet2` (§1.2), refuses to overwrite an existing Secret, prints no password, removes its temporary plaintext, and writes only the hashes file:

```fish
bash scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh staging $HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-lockdown/hashes-staging.yaml
bash scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh indexer-b $HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-lockdown/hashes-indexer-b.yaml
bash scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh network $HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-lockdown/hashes-network.yaml
```

This runbook never runs the script, never reads a password, and only checks the results: every Secret exists with exactly its keys (from `kubectl describe`, which shows key names and sizes, never values), and every hashes file names exactly its installation's users with distinct 64-character hashes.

```bash
for f in staging indexer-b network; do test -s "$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-$f.yaml" || { echo "missing $si_lockdown_dir/hashes-$f.yaml: the user runs §4's commands first"; exit 1; }; done
python3 -I - "$si_backup" <<'EOF'
import re, sys, yaml
base = sys.argv[1]
network = {"default", "si_snode", "si_gateway", "si_verifier", "si_reader"}
want = {"network": network, "indexer-b": {"default", "si_snode", "si_gateway", "si_reader"}, "staging": network}
seen = {}
for inst in ("network", "indexer-b", "staging"):
    hashes = yaml.safe_load(open(f"{base}/hashes-{inst}.yaml"))["passwordSha256"]
    users = set(hashes)
    if users != want[inst]:
        sys.exit(f"{inst}: users {sorted(users)}, expected {sorted(want[inst])}")
    for user, value in sorted(hashes.items()):
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", str(value)):
            sys.exit(f"{inst}/{user}: not 64 lowercase hex characters")
        if value in seen:
            sys.exit(f"{inst}/{user} has the same hash as {seen[value]}: two equal passwords")
        seen[value] = f"{inst}/{user}"
        print(f"{inst}\t{user}\t{value}")
EOF
check() { local got; got="$(si_secret_keys "$1")"; [ "$got" = "$2" ] || { echo "Secret $1 has keys '$got', expected '$2'"; return 1; }; echo "$1: $got"; }
{
  check sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a-clickhouse "ckh-manager.yaml snode-password "
  check storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-verifier "password "
  check storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-bootstrap "password "
  check storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-reader-network "password "
  check storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-admin-network "password "
  check sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b-clickhouse "ckh-manager.yaml snode-password "
  check storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-reader-indexer-b "password "
  check storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-admin-indexer-b "password "
  check storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging-logins "default si_gateway si_reader si_snode si_verifier "
} | tee "$si_backup/secrets.txt"
```

Expected: one line per user and installation with its hash (14 distinct hashes: five for the network, four for indexer-b, five for staging, which carries the network user set so the grant probe runs every role), then the nine Secrets with exactly their keys. The passwords themselves are proven against the hashes by the logins of §5 and §6. A Secret created by mistake can be deleted until §6 has run; after that, a Secret is changed only by rotation (§13).

## 5. Staging proof and grant probe

The staging installation `storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging` (`docs/examples/storage-integrity-lockdown-staging-chi.yaml`: indexer-b's CHI renamed, Keeper root `/storage-integrity/devnet2/lockdown-staging`, 1Gi volumes) is reconciled by the same `devnet2-operator`. It goes through posture A, B and C, each a `kubectl apply` of a variant generated from the committed file with that posture's users, and nothing may restart: the pod uid, its restart count, the StatefulSet generation and revisions stay the same and `uptime()` keeps growing. Then the grant probe runs the committed corpus as each role.

ClickHouse refuses Keeper operations until its root exists, so the staging root is created first:

Confirm before running.

```bash
si_keeper "touch '/storage-integrity/devnet2/lockdown-staging'"
test -z "$(si_keeper "ls '/storage-integrity/devnet2/lockdown-staging'" | tr -d '[:space:]')" || { echo "the staging Keeper root is not empty: an earlier staging run left it; run §11 first"; exit 1; }
echo "staging Keeper root ready"
```

The three variants (local only):

```bash
for p in A B C; do si_staging_variant "$p"; done
python3 -I - "$si_backup" <<'EOF'
import sys, yaml
base = sys.argv[1]
docs = {p: yaml.safe_load(open(f"{base}/staging-chi-{p}.yaml")) for p in "ABC"}
for p, d in docs.items():
    conf = d["spec"]["configuration"]
    assert d["metadata"]["name"] == "storage-integrity-si-v2-lockdown-staging", p
    assert conf["zookeeper"]["root"] == "/storage-integrity/devnet2/lockdown-staging", p
    print(p, "users:", sorted(conf["users"]), "files:", sorted(conf.get("files") or {}))
strip = lambda d: {k: v for k, v in d["spec"]["configuration"].items() if k not in ("users", "files")}
assert strip(docs["A"]) == strip(docs["B"]) == strip(docs["C"]), "the variants differ outside users and files"
assert docs["A"]["spec"]["templates"] == docs["B"]["spec"]["templates"] == docs["C"]["spec"]["templates"], "the variants differ in their templates"
print("the variants differ only in users and the users.d file")
EOF
```

Expected: A with the three `default/*` keys of today, B adding the four keys of each of the four roles (`si_gateway`, `si_reader`, `si_snode`, `si_verifier`), C with `default/password_sha256_hex` and `default/networks/ip` instead of today's three and the one file `users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml` (contract §11's text, `access_management` 0 included); `the variants differ only in users and the users.d file`.

Expected: the dry run lists `default/networks/ip`, `default/password_sha256_hex` and the roles' keys, and the files `users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml` and `zz-pool-settings.xml`; the lock record is written right after the apply, so `si_wait_users` polls with the admin password; `system.users matches posture C (default access-management grants: 0)` (`default` with `sha256_password`, `host_names` `['localhost']`, no `host_ip` and no regexp, and no access management), no `diff` output, uptime still growing, `host staging: default ok` over loopback, and `Code: 516` for the unauthenticated login from another pod. A posture C that never matches (the reload failed): stop and remove the staging installation with §11; nothing live has changed.

The grant probe (the "M15 grant probe" of the stage-3 plans): every row of `charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv`, in order, as its role; `ok` means no 497, `denied` means 497, a login or network error is a failed row, and a `default` row (the corpus's setup and teardown of the probe tables) must succeed outright, since a missing table answers 60 or 81 before the access check. It runs DDL and DML on the staging installation only.

Confirm before running.

```bash
si_grant_probe staging | tee "$si_backup/grant-probe-staging.tsv"
awk -F'\t' 'NR > 1 {print $2, $3, $4}' "$si_backup/grant-probe-staging.tsv" | sort | uniq -c
```

Expected: `every row of <n> is as expected`; the summary shows `ok ok` rows for `default` and for each of `si_snode`, `si_gateway`, `si_verifier` and `si_reader`, and `denied denied` rows for the four roles; no `no-login`, `error` or mismatched row. An `ok` row may still fail after its access check passed, and its `code` column then shows that error: the `remote('127.0.0.2:9000', …)` row of `si_gateway` answers 516 from its leg, which logs in to the server's own loopback as the now locked `default` (a 516 of the row's own login is an `error`), and a Keeper error would show in the Keeper-dependent rows (`SYSTEM DROP REPLICA … FROM ZKPATH`, `system.zookeeper`), which are conclusive because the staging root exists. Any other outcome: stop; the grants or the corpus are wrong.

Leave the staging installation in posture C until §11.

## 6. Users (posture B)

Posture B adds the `si_*` users with their literal hashes and leaves `default` as it is, so no client changes. indexer-b's installation goes first (only track 1 depends on it, and no verifier), then the network installation. Each step waits on `system.users`, never on the CHI reporting `Completed`, and proves that nothing restarted.

## 7. Clients

One client per commit and per window, each followed by the census of its servers since its switch: the client's rows must appear under its own user, none of it under `default`, and no 497. Order (K19): verifiers, the bootstrap hook, indexer-b's host, indexer-a's host. Each host's SNode login and gateway Secret change in one commit, so each host restarts once. A wrong password does not stop a host at startup: HouseGate reads its credential file at startup but dials per query, and the schema declarer runs per `CREATE TABLE`, so each host step drives one HouseGate read and one `CREATE TABLE` after its switch.

## 8. Soak

At least 24 hours after §7.4, with every client on its own user and `default` still open: no 497 for any `si_*` user on any server since the first switch, no client of any server still on `default`, `default` only from loopback, and both tracks and every data-plane node healthy. Read-only:

```bash
start="$(cat "$si_backup/soak-start")"
python3 -I -c 'import datetime, sys
s = datetime.datetime.strptime(sys.argv[1], "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S").replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
h = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - s).total_seconds() / 3600
print(f"soak {h:.1f} h since {sys.argv[1]} UTC")
sys.exit(0 if h >= 24 else 1)' "$start" || { echo "the soak has not lasted 24 hours yet"; exit 1; }
first="$(cat "$si_backup/switched-verifiers")"
si_pods > "$si_backup/pods-soak.tsv"
rc=0
for h in a b v1 v2 v3; do
  si_census "$h" "$start" > "$si_backup/census-$h-soak.jsonl"
  si_census_check "$h" "$si_backup/census-$h-soak.jsonl" "$si_backup/pods-soak.tsv" host-a host-b bootstrap verifier-1 verifier-2 verifier-3 > "$si_backup/census-check-$h-soak.txt" || rc=1
  cat "$si_backup/census-check-$h-soak.txt"
  si_denials "$h" "$first" > "$si_backup/denials-$h-soak.jsonl"
  if grep -q '"user":"si_' "$si_backup/denials-$h-soak.jsonl"; then cat "$si_backup/denials-$h-soak.jsonl"; rc=1; fi
done
si_tracks | jq -c '{global: .global_safe_block_seq, tracks: [.indexers[] | {id: .indexer_id, published: .published.safe_block_seq, quarantined}]}' | tee "$si_backup/tracks-soak.json"
for i in 0 1 2; do si_metrics "$i"; done | tee "$si_backup/voters-soak.txt"
for x in a b; do si_info "$x"; done | tee "$si_backup/info-soak.json"
si_vm_query 'ALERTS{alertstate="firing", network="devnet2-si-v2"}' | jq -c '[.data.result[].metric.alertname] | unique' | tee "$si_backup/alerts-soak.json"
[ "$(cat "$si_backup/alerts-soak.json")" = "[]" ] || { echo "a storage-integrity alert is firing: explain it before §9"; rc=1; }
[ "$rc" = 0 ] || { echo "the soak is not clean: stop; revert the client whose rows fail (§12.1)"; exit 1; }
{ echo "soak $start .. $(si_stamp) UTC: census clean on a b v1 v2 v3, no 497 for any si_* user since $first"; cat "$si_backup/tracks-soak.json"; } | tee "$si_backup/soak.txt"
```

Expected: at least 24 hours; `census clean` on all five servers, with every client under its own users and only `loopback default` left; no denial row of an `si_*` user since §7.1; both tracks' published frontiers above `$si_backup/tracks-before.json`, neither quarantined; every voter with two active SNodes and three active verifiers; both hosts enrolled; `[]`: no alert of this network firing (stage-3 P0's monitoring, read with `si_vm_query`). Then one more signed write as the soak's last proof:

Confirm before running.

```bash
si_accept_a_track 4103 | tee "$si_backup/accept-4103.txt"
```

Expected: track 0's published frontier moves and the safe read returns `1`.

## 9. Lock (posture C)

Posture C gives `default` its hash and, with the one file `users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml` (`<clickhouse><users><default><networks replace="replace"><ip>::1</ip><ip>127.0.0.1</ip></networks><access_management>0</access_management></default></users></clickhouse>`, contract §11), restricts it to loopback and drops its access management (the image's own `users.xml` grants it, so leaving `default/access_management` out alone would keep it). The `si_*` users and every client stay as they are. indexer-b's installation first, then the network installation, each in its own window and never together with a client switch.
````
