## 10. Exit probe

The exit of spec §16 row L: `default` is locked on every SI ClickHouse (§9: an unauthenticated native login from another pod answers 516), every user's `system.grants` equals `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS` for its role, and the soak showed no 497 (§8). `READ ON REMOTE` without `WRITE` is judged by `system.grants` and by behaviour, never by `SHOW GRANTS` (on 26.3 with `enable_read_write_grants` off, `SHOW GRANTS` prints both as the deprecated `REMOTE`). Read-only:

```bash
rc=0
for h in a v1 v2 v3 b; do
  si_grants "$h" > "$si_backup/grants-$h.jsonl"
  si_grants_check "$h" "$si_backup/grants-$h.jsonl" > "$si_backup/exit-grants-$h.txt" || rc=1
  cat "$si_backup/exit-grants-$h.txt"
  si_users "$h" > "$si_backup/users-$h-exit.jsonl"
  acc="$(si_default_access "$h")" || acc=unknown
  printf 'host %s: ' "$h"
  si_lockdown_py users-check C "$si_lockdown_dir/hashes-$(si_installation "$h").yaml" "$si_backup/users-$h-exit.jsonl" "$acc" || rc=1
done
if ! grep -q 'Code: 516' "$si_backup/anon-indexer-b.txt" || [ "$(grep -c 'Code: 516' "$si_backup/anon-network.txt")" != 4 ]; then echo "the 516 records of §9 are incomplete"; rc=1; fi
test -s "$si_backup/soak.txt" || { echo "no soak record (§8)"; rc=1; }
[ "$rc" = 0 ] || { echo "an exit criterion is not met; stop"; exit 1; }
echo "exit criteria met"
```

Expected: for each of `a`, `v1`, `v2`, `v3` (`si_snode, si_gateway, si_verifier, si_reader`) and `b` (`si_snode, si_gateway, si_reader`): `si_gateway READ ON REMOTE rows 1, WRITE rows of any si_* user 0` and `system.grants equals SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS`; `system.users matches posture C (default access-management grants: 0)`; `exit criteria met`. A difference that is only a different grouping of the same privileges (ClickHouse printing a parent privilege as its children or the reverse) is compared by hand with `system.privileges` and recorded; anything else: stop.

`READ ON REMOTE` without `WRITE` by behaviour, as `si_gateway` over loopback on both source servers: an `INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote(…)` is refused with 497 before any connection, and a read through `remote()` passes the access check and fails only on the closed port.

Confirm before running.

```bash
: > "$si_backup/exit-remote.txt"
for h in a b; do
  if out="$(si_ch_exec "$h" si_gateway "INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote('127.0.0.1:1', 'default', 'si_lockdown_probe') VALUES (1)" 2>&1)"; then echo "host $h: the remote() INSERT was accepted; stop"; exit 1; fi
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'Code: 497.*WRITE ON REMOTE' || { echo "host $h: the remote() INSERT failed without a WRITE ON REMOTE refusal: $(printf '%s' "$out" | head -n 2)"; exit 1; }
  out="$(si_ch_exec "$h" si_gateway "SELECT dummy FROM remote('127.0.0.1:1', system.one)" 2>&1)" || true
  if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'Code: 497'; then echo "host $h: the remote() read was refused with 497; stop"; exit 1; fi
  echo "host $h: si_gateway READ ON REMOTE yes, WRITE ON REMOTE no" | tee -a "$si_backup/exit-remote.txt"
done
```

Expected: `si_gateway READ ON REMOTE yes, WRITE ON REMOTE no` for `a` and `b` (the read fails with a connection error such as 519 or 279, never 497). This block's two refused INSERTs are this runbook's own 497s for `si_gateway` over loopback, after the soak: a later denial check over a window that includes them must leave them out.

## 12. Rollback

L changes no consensus state, so every step can be undone; the only order that matters is that `default` reopens before any client returns to it. Every revert is a single-service commit pushed to `main` with the render tests passing; CHI files are applied with `kubectl`. A step that has not run has no commit file and is skipped. Once `default` is locked, rolling a host back to a sentio-node image older than `<SN_COMMIT>`, or a verifier to an arbiter older than `<ARBITER_TAG>`, breaks that client's login until `default` is reopened (§12.2): never roll back a P0 image before this section has run.

### 12.1 Before §9

Revert the client commits in reverse order (clients return to `default`), then, if wanted, the users (posture B back to A).

Confirm before running.

```bash
git fetch origin main
git merge --ff-only origin/main
for x in indexer-a indexer-b bootstrap verifiers; do
  f="$si_backup/lockdown-$x-commit"
  [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "no $x commit: skipped"; continue; }
  c="$(cat "$f")"; git show --stat "$c"
  git revert --no-edit "$c"
  python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py
  git push origin HEAD:main
  case "$x" in
    indexer-a|indexer-b)
      helmfile -f k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml sync --selector "name=sentio-node-devnet2-$x"
      si_kubectl rollout status "statefulset/sentio-node-devnet2-$x" --timeout=15m ;;
    bootstrap)
      helmfile -f k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml sync --selector name=storage-integrity-si-v2
      rm -f "$si_lockdown_dir/switched-bootstrap" ;;
    verifiers)
      helmfile -f k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml sync --selector name=storage-integrity-si-v2
      si_kubectl rollout status statefulset/storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier --timeout=15m ;;
  esac
  mv "$f" "$f.reverted"
done
for x in a b; do si_info "$x"; done
for i in 0 1 2; do si_metrics "$i"; done
```

### 12.3 Staging and the operator pin

The staging installation is removed with §11 at any time; a staging proof that restarted anything stops this runbook before any live change. ## 13. Operating rules

- Passwords: only the user's terminal generates them, with `scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh`; git and the CHIs carry only `password_sha256_hex` literals; each plaintext lives only in its Kubernetes Secret. Never paste a password into chat, never pass one on argv (`--password`, `--from-literal`, a URL), never print or `kubectl get -o yaml` a Secret, never copy one into `$si_backup` or a log; read Secrets only with `kubectl describe` and pipe them only into `kubectl exec -i` stdin, as `si_ch_exec` does.
- Never create an SI user with SQL `CREATE USER` (a source grant of an SQL-stored user widens to READ and WRITE after a serialization round trip, ClickHouse issue #111402), and never use `valueFrom`, `k8s_secret_*` or `k8s_secret_env_*` for a user's hash: the first rolls every pod, the others fall back silently to a known password when the Secret read fails (K16). Literal hashes only.
- After L, every change to the users of an SI ClickHouse goes through this runbook; it supersedes the source-ClickHouse rule of §11 of [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md). Grants change only through `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS`, with a new census (§2) and grant probe (§5).
- Rotation by successor user: a users.xml user holds exactly one authentication method, and the server reloads a new hash within minutes while a client keeps its old password until it restarts (HouseGate reads its credential file only at startup). So never change a protocol user's hash in place: add a successor user (for example `si_snode_r2`) with the same grants and its own Secret in a reviewed change (chart users, `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS` and `SI_CLICKHOUSE_USERS`, the logins script), switch the client in its own commit (one restart), soak, then remove the old user and its Secret. `default` has no client: its hash and its admin Secret change together, in one window, with `si_ch_admin` checked right after.
- Admin access only through `si_ch_admin`: `default` over loopback inside the ClickHouse pod with the password from its admin Secret. Never give `default` to a client, never reach `default` through `kubectl port-forward` (it arrives as loopback and bypasses this runbook's record), never re-add `access_management` to `default`.
- Wait on `system.users` after every users change, never on the CHI reporting `Completed`; a malformed users file keeps the old users silently (§5 shows the shape). Never change `spec.configuration.zookeeper`, `settings` or a non-`users.d` file of a live SI CHI as part of a users change: those restart pods.
- No `helmfile` against `k8s-sea/clickhouse/helmfile.yaml` during stage 3 (K22): `devnet2-operator` is pinned (§3) and never synced; an operator upgrade is its own reviewed window with a staging proof. CHI files go through `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` first, then `kubectl apply`.
- A client Secret's content changes only by rotation; a changed Secret takes effect only after a manual restart of its pod, and a missing Secret or key leaves the pod in `ContainerCreating`. Never delete a client Secret while its client runs.
- Never wire a debug-level logger into HouseGate, or raise its level, while a password is in use: its credential injector logs the original and mapped passwords at Debug.
- Residuals of K18, recorded and not fixed here: loopback includes the pod's other containers and `kubectl port-forward`, so for anyone with `pods/portforward` or `pods/exec` the password is the only barrier; the operator's own `clickhouse_operator` user is a full admin reachable from the operator pod's address (possibly with the chart's well-known default password; rotating it is a separate, confirmed operator change); users are installation-wide, so `si_snode` and `si_verifier` are valid on all four servers of the network installation; `GRANT SYSTEM DROP REPLICA ON *.*` lets a leaked `si_snode` or `si_verifier` password remove any inactive replica's metadata in the shared Keeper; `SELECT` with `ALTER DELETE` implies `ALTER MOVE PARTITION`, and any `CREATE TABLE` implies `CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE` and `CREATE ARBITRARY TEMPORARY TABLE`. Also recorded: the DinD `clickhouse-config` file keeps `default` and `""` and fails closed, and tenant processor code can read it, so it never carries an SI credential; if peer signing fails, HouseGate's rewriter falls back to its static credential for a `remote()` leg to a peer, which now is `si_gateway`'s (a housegate follow-up: refuse that fallback whenever a signer is configured).
- Left open until stage 3 P4: interserver HTTP (9009) credentials (in two rolling steps), an ACL and ingress allowlist on the shared Keeper ensemble, NetworkPolicies (which must admit 9000/8123 from the host pod and, for members, 9000 from the peer source ClickHouses, and 9009 from the verifier ClickHouses and the peer source ClickHouses; a policy applied blind cuts the verifiers' interserver fetches), and anti-affinity of the SI ClickHouses. Stage 3 P2 adds `named_collection_control` to `default` (a users-only change) before it creates the member collections.
````

        for c in cols:
            yield {"user_name": user, "access_type": name, "access_object": "", "database": None if db == "*" else db, "table": None if tb == "*" else tb, "column": c, "is_partial_revoke": 0, "grant_option": 0}
for u in users:
    for g in test_render.SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS[u]:
        for r in rows(u, g):
            print(json.dumps(r))

## Task 18: devnet2 — ClickHouse lockdown: census, operator pin, logins, staging proof, users, clients, soak, lock, exit probe (S3-B, live)

Spec §14 (third bullet) and §16 row L, as clarified by K15–K19 and K22 and bound by contract §11–§12: every SI ClickHouse of devnet2-si-v2 ends locked. `default` gets a password, accepts loopback only and loses access management, and every protocol client connects as its own user with exactly its grants. The task executes `docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md` (Task 17, merged in `L_PR`), section by section and block by block, in K19's order: census → operator pin → logins (the user's action) → staging proof and grant probe → posture B (indexer-b's installation, then the network's) → clients one at a time (verifiers, bootstrap hook, indexer-b host, indexer-a host) → soak → posture C (indexer-b's installation, then the network's) → exit probe → staging cleanup. The runbook is the source of truth for every check, acceptance name and value (decision D19); this task adds the exact content of each single-service commit, the gates, the user's devuser1 blocks, and the ledger: it makes the nine commits of phase L and records `OPERATOR_CHART_VERSION`, `L_END` (and `L_PR`, which Task 17 left as a local edit) in Appendix C through phase L's one docs PR.

No step changes consensus state. Every commit can be reverted (contract §12, runbook §12): before posture C a client's revert returns it to `default`; after posture C the lock commits are reverted first. The users changes reload in place, and the staging proof shows that before either live installation is touched. Irreversible: only throwaway data (the staging installation's volumes and Keeper root, runbook §11; the test tables `devuser1.lockdown_b` and `<db_a>.lockdown_a`, dropped in §7.3 and §7.4) and, only if runbook §1.2 needs it, up to four permanent databases `lockdown_a<n>` of devuser1's owner on chain.

Notes:
- **The runbook decides.** Every check, stop condition and expected output below is the runbook's; where this task adds a read-only check it says so. The census of runbook §2 (`si_census`, `si_census_check`) is the binding gate of K15 and K17 (contract §11): it attributes every row of 7 days of `query_log` to a client by the pod that held its address, checks every used privilege against `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS` for that client's users, and fails on a DinD address or a container-id client hostname, an unknown client, another pod of the namespace, a client on a host it never uses, or an uncovered privilege. Every switch in §7 and the lock in §9 run the same census since that change.
- **Generated users and values blocks.** The `users:` blocks of indexer-b's CHI and the `clickhouse:` block of the network overlay are pasted from the runbook's own generators (`si_users_yaml`, `si_access_values`), which read `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS` from the checkout and the hashes from the user's hashes files. So the committed grants equal the contract's, the hashes are the user's, and no hash passes through this task's text.
- **Passwords (K16).** No step reads, prints or passes a password. Every query reaches `default` through `si_ch_admin`, which sends no password to an installation until its lock record `locked-<installation>` exists (D9) and afterwards pipes the admin Secret into `kubectl exec -i`; the client logins are proven by `si_login` and by use. Secrets are inspected only with `kubectl describe` (key names and sizes). The hashes are not secret and are printed by runbook §4.
- **Cross-task dependency.** `test_indexer_b_source_clickhouse_carries_the_network_source_profile` and `test_devnet2_clickhouse_logins_follow_the_rollout` (Task 16) run at every commit here, including the two that leave the installations at different postures: Step 8 (indexer-b at B, network at A) and Step 15 (indexer-b at C, network at B). If either fails, stop: the live task never edits a test.
- **Both schema declarers are exercised.** Runbook §7.3 creates `devuser1.lockdown_b` through indexer-b and §7.4 creates `<db_a>.lockdown_a` through indexer-a after their switches, so each host's declarer reads a new table as `si_gateway` (a wrong gateway password fails per query, not at startup).

**Conventions for this task.**
- The agent runs every bash block, the runbook's and this task's, from a block file, never inside a heredoc (decision D24): runbook §4 and §5 and this task's blocks carry their own `<<'EOF'` and `<<'PY'` heredocs, so no wrapping delimiter is safe. For each run the agent writes, with the Write tool, a new file `$HOME/.cache/s3b-task18/blocks/<nn>-<what>.sh` (`<nn>` counts up in the order the blocks run; a file is never edited or reused once it ran) whose first two lines are

  ```bash
  source "$HOME/.cache/s3b-task18/helpers.sh"
  cd "$P"
  ```

  followed by the block, and runs it with the Bash tool as `bash -eo pipefail "$HOME/.cache/s3b-task18/blocks/<nn>-<what>.sh" < /dev/null` (the Bash tool's own shell is zsh, so a block never runs in it directly, and no command of a block can read the tool's stdin). `helpers.sh` (Step 1) holds the lockdown runbook's §0 helpers, the earlier runbooks' §0 helpers they build on (extracted by their fences, `l-helpers.py`, the same code as Task 15's `p0-helpers.py`), `P` (the live checkout) and this task's `l_*` helpers. Until Step 1 has written `helpers.sh`, the block files have no `source` and `cd` lines, and until it has created `$HOME/.cache/s3b-task18/blocks` they go into a fresh directory of the agent's session scratchpad. A block that may wait longer than 10 minutes (every sync with a rollout, every `si_wait_chi`) runs with `run_in_background: true`; read its output before the next step.
- **Runbook blocks.** "Run runbook §X's block" means: copy that block from `$P/docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md` verbatim into its block file, never edited (except where the runbook itself says to set a value), and run it as above; a block preceded by `Confirm before running.` runs only after the step's gate has its yes. A confirmed block that stopped is never re-run as is: report its output. If it stopped before its first write (`si_render_diff`, the render tests or `si_head_files`), fix the cause (for a moved `main`: `git -C "$P" fetch origin && git -C "$P" rebase origin/main`, then the render tests), and ask again.
- **Explicit user confirmation.** Every remote or live mutation waits for an explicit yes in chat, given for that block only: each push to production `main`, each sync, each `kubectl apply`, `run` or `delete`, each Keeper write, each acceptance INSERT, the grant probe, the exit probe's REMOTE check, the housegate push, PR and merge. Before asking, the agent states the block's Gate sentence, saying exactly what will change. Read-only blocks need none.
- **The user's terminal.** The user runs the logins script (runbook §4) and devuser1's owner's blocks in their own terminal; the agent never runs either. For a devuser1 block the agent states its Gate and hands the user one fish command, `bash ~/.cache/s3b-task18/l-user-block.sh <block> <path to devuser1's owner key file>`, which runs exactly that runbook block in bash with the session helpers defined (the key only in `HOUSEGATE_AGENT_KEY`, never in chat or on argv); the agent then reads `$si_backup/user-<block>.out`. Passwords and keys never appear in chat. Commands handed to the user are fish.
- **One window per step.** Steps 5 and 7–18 each are one window: never one installation and one client in the same window, and never a posture C commit together with a client switch. Run no helmfile against `k8s-sea/clickhouse` (K22) and no other sync of `storage-integrity-si-v2` or of either host during this task.
- **Stop rules.** Stop on any unexpected output and report it; never improvise a fix on the cluster. Above all: any `FAIL` or `K17` line of a census, any denial row of an `si_*` user from `si_denials` (except §10's own two refused `remote()` INSERTs), a `diff` or uptime line of a users change (a restart), a client that does not become Ready, logs an authentication failure or still logs in as `default`, and an acceptance that does not reach safe. A client that fails right after its switch: ask for runbook §12.1 at once (the revert needs its own yes). A commit block that stops before its `git commit` leaves its edits in the live checkout: discard them with `git -C "$P" checkout -- .` (local) and report. A local commit whose push the user declined stays on the detached HEAD and makes `l_fresh_main` stop: report it, and only on the user's word drop it with `git -C "$P" switch -q --detach origin/main` (local; it was never pushed).

`l-helpers.py`, which assembles the session helpers exactly as each runbook's §0 says to define them:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the session helpers of the lockdown runbook, earlier runbooks first (Plan S3-B Task 18).

  l-helpers.py DOCS_DIR RUNBOOK.md

A runbook's "## 0. Session helpers" section names the earlier runbooks whose
§0 helpers it builds on (Markdown links before its first bash block) and then
holds its own helpers in its first bash block (decision D20). This prints,
depth first and each runbook once, the earlier runbooks' first §0 bash blocks
and then the runbook's own, each behind a comment naming its source, exactly
as the runbooks say to define them. Blocks are found by their fences, line by
line (decision D24): a fence opens on a line of three or more backquotes and
closes only on a line of at least as many backquotes and nothing else, so a
line inside a block that mentions backquotes (the stage-3 P0 runbook's
partstates builder) or ends a heredoc never ends the block. Tasks 15 and 21
assemble their helpers with the same code.
"""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

FENCE = re.compile(r"(`{3,})([^`\s]*)\s*$")


def section_zero(path):
    lines = path.read_text().split("\n")
    if "## 0. Session helpers" not in lines:
        sys.exit(f"l-helpers: {path} has no '## 0. Session helpers' section")
    intro, block, fence = [], None, None
    for line in lines[lines.index("## 0. Session helpers") + 1:]:
        if fence is None:
            opening = FENCE.match(line)
            if opening:
                fence = opening.group(1)
                if opening.group(2) == "bash":
                    block = []
            elif line.startswith("## "):
                break
            else:
                intro.append(line)
        elif re.fullmatch(re.escape(fence) + r"`*\s*", line):
            if block is not None:
                earlier = re.findall(r"\]\((storage-integrity-devnet2-[a-z0-9-]+\.md)\)", "\n".join(intro))
                return earlier, "\n".join(block) + "\n"
            fence = None
        elif block is not None:
            block.append(line)
    sys.exit(f"l-helpers: {path}: no complete bash block in section 0")


def collect(docs, name, seen, out):
    if name in seen:
        return
    seen.add(name)
    earlier, block = section_zero(docs / name)
    for other in earlier:
        collect(docs, other, seen, out)
    out.append((name, block))


def main(docs, runbook):
    out = []
    collect(Path(docs), runbook, set(), out)
    for name, block in out:
        print(f"# --- §0 of docs/{name}")
        print(block, end="" if block.endswith("\n") else "\n")
    print("# --- end of runbook helpers: " + " ".join(name for name, _ in out), file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    main(*sys.argv[1:])
```

`l-helpers.sh`, this task's shell helpers (sourced last by `helpers.sh`):

```bash
# Plan S3-B Task 18 helpers (not part of the runbook), sourced last by helpers.sh after the
# runbooks' §0 helpers. P is the live checkout, a detached HEAD at origin/main. They edit and
# commit that checkout only; none of them reads a password or touches the cluster.
l_fresh_main() { # before every commit: the live checkout fast-forwarded to a freshly fetched origin/main, detached and clean
  git -C "$P" fetch -q origin main || return 1
  [ -z "$(git -C "$P" status --porcelain)" ] || { echo "the live checkout has local changes: stop"; return 1; }
  git -C "$P" merge -q --ff-only origin/main || { echo "the live checkout cannot fast-forward to origin/main: stop"; return 1; }
  [ "$(git -C "$P" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git -C "$P" rev-parse origin/main)" ] || { echo "the live checkout is not at origin/main (an unpushed local commit?): stop"; return 1; }
  [ "$(git -C "$P" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" = HEAD ] || { echo "the live checkout is on a branch, not a detached HEAD: stop"; return 1; }
  echo "live checkout at origin/main $(git -C "$P" rev-parse --short=9 HEAD) (detached)"
}
l_replace() { # $1 file, $2 file holding the exact old text, $3 file holding the new text: replaces the one occurrence; refuses none or several
  python3 -I - "$@" <<'PY'
import sys
path, old_path, new_path = sys.argv[1:]
text, old, new = (open(name).read() for name in (path, old_path, new_path))
if text.count(old) != 1:
    sys.exit(f"{path}: the old text occurs {text.count(old)} times, expected exactly once")
with open(path, "w") as out:
    out.write(text.replace(old, new))
print(f"{path}: {old.count(chr(10))} line(s) replaced by {new.count(chr(10))}")
PY
}
l_block() { # $1 file, $2 key, $3 indent (number of spaces), $4 file holding the new block: replaces the one block "<indent><key>:" with every following line indented deeper; refuses none or several
  python3 -I - "$@" <<'PY'
import re
import sys
path, key, indent, new_path = sys.argv[1:]
text, new = open(path).read(), open(new_path).read()
pad = " " * int(indent)
pattern = re.compile(r"^%s%s:\n(?:%s .*\n)*" % (re.escape(pad), re.escape(key), re.escape(pad)), re.M)
found = pattern.findall(text)
if len(found) != 1:
    sys.exit(f"{path}: {len(found)} blocks '{pad}{key}:', expected exactly one")
if not new.startswith(f"{pad}{key}:\n") or not new.endswith("\n"):
    sys.exit(f"{new_path} does not hold one '{pad}{key}:' block")
with open(path, "w") as out:
    out.write(pattern.sub(lambda _: new, text, count=1))
print(f"{path}: block {key} ({found[0].count(chr(10))} lines) replaced by {new.count(chr(10))} lines")
PY
}
l_set_rollout() { # $1 constant, $2 key ("-" for a scalar constant), $3 value now, $4 new value (Python literals): edits one entry of a test_render.py rollout constant in place, keeping its layout
  python3 -I - charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py "$@" <<'PY'
import ast
import json
import re
import sys
path, name, key, old, new = sys.argv[1:]
old, new = ast.literal_eval(old), ast.literal_eval(new)
def lit(value):
    return "None" if value is None else json.dumps(value)
def pattern(value):
    if value is None:
        return "None"
    return "(?:%s|%s)" % (re.escape(json.dumps(value)), re.escape("'" + value + "'"))
def assignment(text):
    found = [node for node in ast.parse(text).body
             if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and len(node.targets) == 1
             and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name) and node.targets[0].id == name]
    if len(found) != 1:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: expected one module-level assignment of {name}, found {len(found)}")
    return found[0]
src = open(path).read()
node = assignment(src)
current = ast.literal_eval(node.value)
lines = src.splitlines(keepends=True)
start = sum(map(len, lines[:node.lineno - 1])) + node.col_offset
end = sum(map(len, lines[:node.end_lineno - 1])) + node.end_col_offset
segment = src[start:end]
if key == "-":
    if current != old:
        sys.exit(f"{name} is {current!r}, expected {old!r}")
    edited, count = re.subn(r"^(%s\s*=\s*)%s$" % (re.escape(name), pattern(old)), lambda m: m.group(1) + lit(new), segment)
    want = new
else:
    if not isinstance(current, dict) or key not in current or current[key] != old:
        sys.exit(f"{name}[{key!r}] is not {old!r} (now {current!r})")
    edited, count = re.subn(r"""(["']%s["']\s*:\s*)%s(?=\s*[,}#\n])""" % (re.escape(key), pattern(old)), lambda m: m.group(1) + lit(new), segment)
    want = dict(current, **{key: new})
if count != 1:
    sys.exit(f"{name}: expected to edit one entry, edited {count}")
result = src[:start] + edited + src[end:]
if ast.literal_eval(assignment(result).value) != want:
    sys.exit(f"{name}: the edit did not produce {want!r}")
with open(path, "w") as out:
    out.write(result)
print(f"{name}{'' if key == '-' else '[' + json.dumps(key) + ']'}: {lit(old)} -> {lit(new)}")
PY
}
l_commit() { # $1 message file, then the exact files of this commit: refuses any other change, runs the render tests, commits on the detached HEAD (local only)
  local msg=$1
  shift
  [ "$(git diff --name-only HEAD | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' ' ')" = "$(printf '%s\n' "$@" | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' ' ')" ] || { echo "the working tree does not change exactly: $*"; git status --short; return 1; }
  [ -z "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ] || { echo "untracked files in the checkout:"; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; return 1; }
  python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py > "$si_backup/tests-last.txt" 2>&1 || { tail -n 40 "$si_backup/tests-last.txt"; echo "render tests fail: nothing committed; discard the edits with git -C \"\$P\" checkout -- ."; return 1; }
  tail -n 3 "$si_backup/tests-last.txt"
  git add -- "$@"
  git commit -q -F "$msg"
  git show --stat --oneline HEAD | cat
}
```

`l-user-block.sh`, which runs one of devuser1's owner's runbook blocks in the user's own terminal:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run one devuser1 block of docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md in the user's own terminal (Plan S3-B Task 18).
#
#   bash ~/.cache/s3b-task18/l-user-block.sh <block> <key file of devuser1's owner>
#
# From fish this is an ordinary command. <block> names one confirmed block of the live checkout's
# runbook whose first line is key_file=/path/to/devuser1-owner.key: db-a (§1.2, only when §1.2 asks
# for it), lockdown-b-create and lockdown-b-row (§7.3), lockdown-a (§7.4), lock-b-read (§9.1). The
# block runs verbatim in a bash with set -eo pipefail, the session helpers (helpers.sh) defined and
# the live checkout as its directory; only its first line is replaced by the key file path given
# here. si_agent_start reads the key into HOUSEGATE_AGENT_KEY: it never reaches argv, this terminal
# or the chat. The block as run is kept as $si_backup/user-<block>.sh and its output as
# $si_backup/user-<block>.out; a block that ran once is refused (a write is never re-run).
# shellcheck disable=SC2154  # si_backup and P come from helpers.sh
set -eo pipefail
[ "$#" = 2 ] || { echo "usage: bash ~/.cache/s3b-task18/l-user-block.sh db-a|lockdown-b-create|lockdown-b-row|lockdown-a|lock-b-read <key file>"; exit 2; }
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source "$HOME/.cache/s3b-task18/helpers.sh"
case "$1" in db-a|lockdown-b-create|lockdown-b-row|lockdown-a|lock-b-read) ;; *) echo "$1 is not one of the runbook's devuser1 blocks"; exit 2;; esac
[ -d "$si_backup" ] || { echo "$si_backup does not exist: runbook §1.1 has not run"; exit 1; }
[ ! -e "$si_backup/user-$1.sh" ] || { echo "$si_backup/user-$1.sh exists: that block ran already; never re-run it (read $si_backup/user-$1.out instead)"; exit 1; }
[ -f "$2" ] && [ -r "$2" ] || { echo "$2 is not a readable key file"; exit 1; }
key="$(cd "$(dirname "$2")" && pwd)/$(basename "$2")"
block="$si_backup/user-$1.sh"
python3 -I - "$P/docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md" "$1" "$key" "$block" <<'PY'
import re
import shlex
import sys

runbook, name, key, out = sys.argv[1:]
where = {
    "db-a": ("### 1.2 Identities and Secrets", 'si_agent_ch --query "CREATE DATABASE $db"'),
    "lockdown-b-create": ("### 7.3 indexer-b host", "CREATE TABLE lockdown_b"),
    "lockdown-b-row": ("### 7.3 indexer-b host", "INSERT INTO lockdown_b"),
    "lockdown-a": ("### 7.4 indexer-a host", "CREATE TABLE lockdown_a"),
    "lock-b-read": ("### 9.1 indexer-b", "si_agent_start"),
}
heading, marker = where[name]
first = "key_file=/path/to/devuser1-owner.key"
# The bash blocks of that subsection, found by their fences line by line (decision D24), as l-helpers.py
# does; a heading counts only outside a block, and so does the line before a block.
found, current, previous, fence, body, confirmed = [], None, "", None, None, False
for line in open(runbook).read().split("\n"):
    if fence is None:
        opening = re.match(r"(`{3,})([^`\s]*)\s*$", line)
        if opening:
            fence = opening.group(1)
            body = [] if opening.group(2) == "bash" and current == heading else None
            confirmed = previous == "Confirm before running."
            continue
        if re.match(r"#{2,3} ", line):
            current = line
        if line.strip():
            previous = line.strip()
    elif re.fullmatch(re.escape(fence) + r"`*\s*", line):
        if body and body[0] == first and any(marker in text for text in body):
            found.append((confirmed, body))
        fence, body, previous = None, None, line.strip()
    elif body is not None:
        body.append(line)
if len(found) != 1:
    sys.exit(f"l-user-block: expected one devuser1 block of {heading} with {marker!r}, found {len(found)}")
if not found[0][0]:
    sys.exit(f"l-user-block: the {name} block is not a confirmed block of the runbook")
with open(out, "w") as f:
    f.write("key_file=%s\n%s\n" % (shlex.quote(key), "\n".join(found[0][1][1:])))
PY
chmod 600 "$block"
cd "$P"
echo "running the runbook block $1 (kept as $block, output in $si_backup/user-$1.out)"
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
{ source "$block"; } 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/user-$1.out"
```

echo "sizes ok"
```

**What rollback means here** (runbook §12, contract §12; each revert is a single-service commit and push followed by the step's sync or apply, made by the runbook's §12 blocks, each with its own yes; run `l_fresh_main` first, so every revert starts from a clean, detached, freshly fetched `origin/main`, D4):
- **Before Step 15.** Runbook §12.1's first block reverts every client commit that has a `lockdown-<client>-commit` record, in the order indexer-a, indexer-b, bootstrap hook, verifiers, so every client returns to `default`, which is still open; it renames each record to `.reverted`. Its second block (posture B back to A) runs only to abandon L, after every client is back. A client that fails right after its switch is reverted at once.
- **From Step 15 on.** Runbook §12.2 first: it reverts the lock commits, the network's before indexer-b's, removes each `locked-<installation>` record right after that revert's sync or apply and waits until `default` is passwordless and open again (the users reload in place); only then §12.1, if the clients must go back too.
- **Pre-`SN_COMMIT` images.** While `default` is locked, never roll a host back to a sentio-node image older than `SN_COMMIT` or a verifier to an arbiter older than `ARBITER_TAG`: that client cannot log in until `default` reopens.
- **What stays.** The operator pin stays: it names the version that runs (runbook §12.3). The staging installation is only ever deleted (Step 18). No step touches consensus state.

Decisions fixed by this task:

- **D19-1. Born locked, with the member disk, from the first apply.** The Altinity operator restarts a ClickHouse for every `files` or `zookeeper` change (`files/*.xml: yes`; a `users.d/` file never restarts), so indexer-c's installation carries its posture-C users, `users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml` (contract §11 verbatim: loopback only and `<access_management>0</access_management>`, decision D7) and `zz-si-storage.xml` from its creation, when a restart costs nothing. Its users and files equal the network chart's at posture C by role (the same grants, its own hashes, one password per user and installation; decision D10) and its posture comment is indexer-b's text in indexer-c's name, copied mechanically from indexer-b's file on the branch base with each `indexer-b` replaced by `indexer-c` (that text names its own installation's SNode and HouseGate, so it is verbatim but for that name; contract §11, decision D11). The member disk is a second `local-path` volume (`member-volume-claim` at `/var/lib/clickhouse-member/`, disk `member`, policy `member`), on the same node SSD as the data volume: the recorded deviation from spec §8.1 of K21, bounded by one `keep_free_space_bytes` on both disks; no table uses policy `member` before stage 3 P2.
- **D19-2. Placement.** indexer-c's ClickHouse runs on none of `DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES` (the nodes where the network installation's source and verifier ClickHouses and indexer-b's source run or keep their volumes, plus `sea-dg-7` and `sea-dg-8`) and on neither `sea-g-3` nor `sea-g-4` (indexer-a's and indexer-b's hosts), so one node down never stops two tracks; its host runs on neither `sea-g-3` nor `sea-g-4` and, where possible, on no node of `DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES` and not on `INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE` (on that node it needs 32 GiB of unrequested memory: each role's 16 GiB). Both must carry `sentio.xyz/general=true`, be schedulable without a `NoSchedule`/`NoExecute` taint, Ready without pressure, have a `local-path` directory and at least 16 GiB of unrequested memory; the host also needs ephemeral storage for its DinD of at least max(50 GiB, 4 × indexer-b's DinD `/var/lib/docker`). Among the eligible nodes the one with the most unrequested memory wins. The CHI's pod selects `kubernetes.io/hostname` alone (contract §13), so the preflight checks the general label.
- **D19-3. Sizing.** `INDEXER_C_KEEP_FREE_SPACE_BYTES` = max(10 GiB, 10 % of the smallest `default` disk of the five existing SI ClickHouses, rounded up to a whole GiB): a node SSD of the same class, since no read-only path reads the chosen node's SSD before a pod runs there. `INDEXER_C_MEMBER_VOLUME_SIZE` = max(10Gi, 4 × the active `hg_safe` and `hg_unsafe` bytes of indexer-a and indexer-b, rounded up to a whole Gi): the copies stage 3 P2 will hold, with headroom; `local-path` enforces neither number, so the request is bookkeeping and `keep_free_space_bytes` is the bound.
- **D19-4. Logins.** Git carries only the four SHA-256 hashes the user's script wrote (K16); the plaintexts live only in the three Secrets. `clickhouse.username: default` / `password: ""` stays in indexer-c's ordinary values, as on indexer-a and indexer-b since L: it renders only the `clickhouse-config` ConfigMap the DinD driver tasks read, and fails closed against the locked `default` (K17). HouseGate and the schema declarer read `si_gateway` from the `ckh-manager.yaml` Secret file; the SNode connects as `si_snode`.
- **D19-5. Operator inputs are `__TOKEN__`s filled from the recorded values.** The files are written with `__INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE__`, `__INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE__`, `__DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES__`, `__INDEXER_C_KEEP_FREE_SPACE_BYTES__`, `__INDEXER_C_MEMBER_VOLUME_SIZE__`, `__SHA256_DEFAULT__`, `__SHA256_SI_SNODE__`, `__SHA256_SI_GATEWAY__`, `__SHA256_SI_READER__`, `__SN_COMMIT__`, `__SN_DIGEST__`, `__HG_TAG__` and `__CORE_TAG__`, and `fill-indexer-c.py` replaces them from `placement.env`, the user's hashes file `$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-lockdown/hashes-indexer-c.yaml` and the ledger; the existing `test_operator_inputs_are_filled_with_distinct_addresses` refuses any `__X__` left in `FRESH_FILES`.
- **D19-6. indexer-c is rendered only once declared.** `setUpClass` reads `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c` with `releases.get`, so the source-ClickHouse and gateway tests can fail and pass before the release exists (one TDD round per file), while every test that needs the release asserts it (`require_indexer_c`, `require_every_si_host`) and fails, never skips, when it is missing.
- **D19-7. Inert on merge.** No file here is synced or applied on merge: the CHI is applied with `kubectl`, the release is synced only with `--selector name=sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c` by the enrolment runbook right before the enrolment (its first start registers it on chain for good), and the Gateway is patched by hand; Step 10 proves that every other release renders byte-identically to the branch base.
- **D19-8. The three-indexer generalisations keep every merged assertion.** Tasks 13 and 16 add four of the ten tests contract §13 names. `test_owner_audit_needs_a_reviewed_image` (Task 13) already follows `DEVNET2_OWNER_AUDIT` and is not edited; `test_snode_clickhouse_login_needs_a_reviewed_image` and `test_devnet2_clickhouse_logins_follow_the_rollout` (Task 16) are extended in place by the hunks of Step 6, so their image, dead-configuration, overlay-hash, verifier, bootstrap-hook and K19-order checks stay; `host_releases` gains indexer-c once it is declared, so Task 16's gateway-file, DinD and Secret-only tests cover it too. `test_devnet2_owner_audit_follows_the_rollout` and the five indexer-b tests of the base are replaced whole by bodies that check at least what they did, for every SI host.

import re
import sys

for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    text = open(path).read()
    if "\n## 0. Session helpers" not in text:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: no section 0 (Session helpers)")
    section = text.split("\n## 0. Session helpers", 1)[1].split("\n## ", 1)[0]
    # Fences only at the start of a line (decision D24): the stage-3 P0 helpers
    # mention three backquotes inside a line, where an unanchored match would stop.
    blocks = re.findall(r"^```bash\n(.*?)^```$", section, re.S | re.M)
    if not blocks:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: no bash block in section 0")
    print(blocks[0])

type si_kubectl si_ch_admin >/dev/null && echo "helpers ok"
date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ > "$si_preflight/read-at.txt"

for x in a v1 v2 v3 b; do
  si_ch_admin "$x" "SELECT name, path, free_space, total_space, unreserved_space, keep_free_space FROM system.disks ORDER BY name FORMAT TSV" > "$si_preflight/disks-$x.tsv"
done
for x in a b; do
  si_ch_admin "$x" "SELECT database, sum(bytes_on_disk) FROM system.parts WHERE active AND database IN ('hg_safe', 'hg_unsafe', 'hg_promote', 'devnet2') GROUP BY database ORDER BY database FORMAT TSV" > "$si_preflight/bytes-$x.tsv"
done

A `Forbidden` on a cluster-wide read (`pv`, `nodes`, `pods -A`): stop and ask the user.

Then decide, locally, in the same session:

```bash
si_preflight="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c-preflight"
python3 -I - "$si_preflight" k8s-sea/local-path-storage/local-path-storage.yaml <<'PY'
import json
import math
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

out, local_path_file = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
GIB = 1024 ** 3
EXCLUDED = {"sea-dg-7", "sea-dg-8"}
OTHER_HOSTS = {"sea-g-3", "sea-g-4"}
SOURCES = {"storage-integrity-si-v2-source-0-0-0", "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source-0-0-0"} | {
    f"storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-{n}-0-0-0" for n in (1, 2, 3)
}
UNITS = {"": 1, "Ki": 1024, "Mi": 1024 ** 2, "Gi": 1024 ** 3, "Ti": 1024 ** 4,
         "k": 10 ** 3, "M": 10 ** 6, "G": 10 ** 9, "T": 10 ** 12, "m": 0.001}


def quantity(text):
    match = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)([A-Za-z]*)", str(text))
    if not match or match.group(2) not in UNITS:
        sys.exit(f"cannot read the quantity {text!r}")
    return float(match.group(1)) * UNITS[match.group(2)]


def memory_request(container):
    return quantity(((container.get("resources") or {}).get("requests") or {}).get("memory", "0"))


# The nodes of the network installation's source and verifier ClickHouses and
# of indexer-b's source: where each pod runs and where its volumes live.
pods = json.loads((out / "pods.json").read_text())["items"]
placed = {pod["metadata"]["name"]: pod["spec"].get("nodeName") or "" for pod in pods if pod["metadata"]["name"] in SOURCES}
if set(placed) != SOURCES or not all(placed.values()):
    sys.exit(f"expected the five source and verifier ClickHouse pods scheduled, found {placed}")
volume_nodes = set()
for pv in json.loads((out / "pvs.json").read_text())["items"]:
    claim = pv["spec"].get("claimRef") or {}
    if claim.get("namespace") != "sentio-network-devnet2" or not any(claim.get("name", "").endswith("-" + pod) for pod in SOURCES):
        continue
    terms = (((pv["spec"].get("nodeAffinity") or {}).get("required") or {}).get("nodeSelectorTerms")) or []
    found = [value for term in terms for expression in term.get("matchExpressions", [])
             if expression.get("key") == "kubernetes.io/hostname" for value in expression.get("values", [])]
    found += [value for key, value in (pv["metadata"].get("annotations") or {}).items() if key == "local.path.provisioner/selected-node"]
    if not found:
        sys.exit(f"cannot read the node of {pv['metadata']['name']} ({claim['name']})")
    volume_nodes.update(found)
source_nodes = set(placed.values()) | volume_nodes | EXCLUDED

config_map = next(doc for doc in yaml.safe_load_all(local_path_file.read_text())
                  if doc and doc.get("kind") == "ConfigMap" and doc["metadata"]["name"] == "local-path-config")
directories = {entry["node"]: entry["paths"] for entry in
               json.loads(config_map["data"]["config.json"])["storageClassConfigs"]["local-path"]["nodePathMap"]}

requested = {}
for pod in json.loads((out / "pods-all.json").read_text())["items"]:
    node = pod["spec"].get("nodeName")
    if node:
        main = sum(memory_request(container) for container in pod["spec"].get("containers", []))
        init = max([memory_request(container) for container in pod["spec"].get("initContainers", [])] or [0])
        requested[node] = requested.get(node, 0) + max(main, init)

dind_need = max(50 * GIB, 4 * 1024 * int((out / "dind-b-du.txt").read_text().split()[0]))
rows = []
for node in json.loads((out / "general-nodes.json").read_text())["items"]:
    name, spec, status = node["metadata"]["name"], node["spec"], node["status"]
    conditions = {condition["type"]: condition["status"] for condition in status.get("conditions", [])}
    free = quantity(status["allocatable"]["memory"]) - requested.get(name, 0)
    ephemeral = quantity(status["allocatable"].get("ephemeral-storage", "0"))
    reasons = []
    if spec.get("unschedulable"):
        reasons.append("unschedulable")
    reasons += [f'taint {taint["key"]}:{taint["effect"]}' for taint in spec.get("taints", []) if taint.get("effect") in ("NoSchedule", "NoExecute")]
    if conditions.get("Ready") != "True":
        reasons.append("not Ready")
    reasons += [kind for kind in ("MemoryPressure", "DiskPressure", "PIDPressure") if conditions.get(kind) == "True"]
    if not directories.get(name):
        reasons.append("no local-path directory")
    if free < 16 * GIB:
        reasons.append("less than 16 GiB unrequested memory")
    rows.append((name, free, ephemeral, reasons))

# indexer-c's ClickHouse shares no node with another owner's source or host
# or with a verifier ClickHouse; its host shares none with another owner's
# host and, where possible, none with a source or verifier ClickHouse, so
# one node down never stops two tracks. Where possible the host also runs
# apart from indexer-c's own ClickHouse; on that node it needs the memory of
# both (32 GiB unrequested), since each role is checked for 16 GiB alone.
chi = sorted((row for row in rows if not row[3] and row[0] not in source_nodes | OTHER_HOSTS),
             key=lambda row: (-row[1], row[0]))
if not chi:
    sys.exit("no general node can take indexer-c's ClickHouse: stop and ask")
chi_node = chi[0][0]
host = sorted((row for row in rows if not row[3] and row[0] not in OTHER_HOSTS and row[2] >= dind_need
               and (row[0] != chi_node or row[1] >= 32 * GIB)),
              key=lambda row: (row[0] in source_nodes, row[0] == chi_node, -row[1], row[0]))
if not host:
    sys.exit("no general node can take indexer-c's host and DinD: stop and ask")
host_node = host[0][0]

totals = []
for x in ("a", "v1", "v2", "v3", "b"):
    for line in (out / f"disks-{x}.tsv").read_text().splitlines():
        name, _path, _free, total, _unreserved, _keep = line.split("\t")
        if name == "default":
            totals.append(int(total))
if len(totals) != 5:
    sys.exit(f"expected five default disks, read {len(totals)}")
keep_free = max(10 * GIB, math.ceil(min(totals) / 10 / GIB) * GIB)
used = 0
for x in ("a", "b"):
    for line in (out / f"bytes-{x}.tsv").read_text().splitlines():
        database, size = line.split("\t")
        if database in ("hg_safe", "hg_unsafe"):
            used += int(size)
member_gi = max(10, math.ceil(4 * used / GIB))

print("node\tunrequested_GiB\tephemeral_GiB\tsource\tineligible")
for name, free, ephemeral, reasons in sorted(rows):
    print(f"{name}\t{free / GIB:.1f}\t{ephemeral / GIB:.1f}\t{'yes' if name in source_nodes else 'no'}\t{', '.join(reasons)}")
placement = {
    "INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE": chi_node,
    "INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE": host_node,
    "DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES": " ".join(sorted(source_nodes)),
    "INDEXER_C_KEEP_FREE_SPACE_BYTES": str(keep_free),
    "INDEXER_C_MEMBER_VOLUME_SIZE": f"{member_gi}Gi",
}
(out / "placement.env").write_text("".join(f'{key}="{value}"\n' for key, value in placement.items()))
print(f"source and verifier pods: {placed}; their volumes: {sorted(volume_nodes)}")
print(f"smallest default disk {min(totals)} B; hg_safe + hg_unsafe on a and b {used} B; DinD needs {dind_need} B of ephemeral storage")
print((out / "placement.env").read_text(), end="")
PY
```

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

# BaseLoader keeps every scalar a string: a hash of digits only stays a hash.
data = yaml.load(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(), Loader=yaml.BaseLoader)
if not isinstance(data, dict) or sorted(data) != ["passwordSha256"]:
    sys.exit("the hashes file must hold passwordSha256 and nothing else")

    sys.exit("passwordSha256 must name exactly default, si_gateway, si_reader and si_snode")
if any(not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", str(value)) for value in hashes.values()) or len(set(hashes.values())) != 4:
    sys.exit("each hash must be 64 lowercase hex characters and the four must differ")
taken = "\n".join(path.read_text() for path in sorted(Path("k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2").rglob("*.yaml")))
reused = sorted(user for user, value in hashes.items() if value in taken)
if reused:
    sys.exit(f"the hash of {reused} appears in a devnet2 file already: one password per user and installation")
print("hashes ok: default, si_gateway, si_reader, si_snode")
PY
for secret in sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-clickhouse storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-reader-indexer-c storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-admin-indexer-c; do

usage: python3 -I fill-indexer-c.py <placement.env> <hashes.yaml> <file>...

placement.env is Step 1's decision; hashes.yaml is the passwordSha256 map that
scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh indexer-c wrote (Step 2).
SN_COMMIT, SN_DIGEST, HG_TAG and CORE_TAG come from the environment (Appendix
C). Every file must exist; a token this script does not know is refused.
"""
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

if len(sys.argv) < 4:
    sys.exit("usage: fill-indexer-c.py <placement.env> <hashes.yaml> <file>...")
placement_path, hashes_path, *files = sys.argv[1:]

placement = {}
for line in Path(placement_path).read_text().splitlines():
    if line.strip() and not line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
        key, value = line.split("=", 1)
        placement[key] = value.strip().strip('"')
for key, pattern in (
    ("INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE", r"sea-[a-z]+-[0-9]+"),
    ("INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE", r"sea-[a-z]+-[0-9]+"),
    ("DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES", r"sea-[a-z]+-[0-9]+( sea-[a-z]+-[0-9]+)*"),
    ("INDEXER_C_KEEP_FREE_SPACE_BYTES", r"[1-9][0-9]*"),
    ("INDEXER_C_MEMBER_VOLUME_SIZE", r"[1-9][0-9]*Gi"),
):
    if not re.fullmatch(pattern, placement.get(key, "")):
        sys.exit(f"{placement_path}: {key} must match {pattern}, got {placement.get(key)!r}")

# BaseLoader keeps every scalar a string: a hash of digits only stays a hash.
hashes = (yaml.load(Path(hashes_path).read_text(), Loader=yaml.BaseLoader) or {}).get("passwordSha256")
if not isinstance(hashes, dict) or sorted(hashes) != ["default", "si_gateway", "si_reader", "si_snode"]:
    sys.exit(f"{hashes_path}: passwordSha256 must name exactly default, si_gateway, si_reader and si_snode")
for user, digest in hashes.items():
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", str(digest)):
        sys.exit(f"{hashes_path}: passwordSha256.{user} must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
if len(set(hashes.values())) != len(hashes):
    sys.exit(f"{hashes_path}: two users share a password hash")

ledger = {}
for key, pattern in (
    ("SN_COMMIT", r"[0-9a-f]{40}"),
    ("SN_DIGEST", r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}"),
    ("HG_TAG", r"v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"),
    ("CORE_TAG", r"v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"),
):
    value = os.environ.get(key, "")
    if not re.fullmatch(pattern, value):
        sys.exit(f"environment: {key} must match {pattern} (Appendix C), got {value!r}")
    ledger[key] = value

tokens = {
    "__INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE__": placement["INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE"],
    "__INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE__": placement["INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE"],
    "__DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES__": ", ".join(f'"{node}"' for node in sorted(placement["DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES"].split())),
    "__INDEXER_C_KEEP_FREE_SPACE_BYTES__": placement["INDEXER_C_KEEP_FREE_SPACE_BYTES"],
    "__INDEXER_C_MEMBER_VOLUME_SIZE__": placement["INDEXER_C_MEMBER_VOLUME_SIZE"],
    "__SHA256_DEFAULT__": hashes["default"],
    "__SHA256_SI_SNODE__": hashes["si_snode"],
    "__SHA256_SI_GATEWAY__": hashes["si_gateway"],
    "__SHA256_SI_READER__": hashes["si_reader"],
    "__SN_COMMIT__": ledger["SN_COMMIT"],
    "__SN_DIGEST__": ledger["SN_DIGEST"],
    "__HG_TAG__": ledger["HG_TAG"],
    "__CORE_TAG__": ledger["CORE_TAG"],
}
for name in files:
    path = Path(name)
    text = path.read_text()
    for token, value in tokens.items():
        text = text.replace(token, value)
    left = sorted(set(re.findall(r"__(?:INDEXER_C|DEVNET2_SOURCE|SHA256|SN|HG|CORE)_[A-Z0-9_]*__", text)))
    if left:
        sys.exit(f"{name}: unknown tokens {left}")
    path.write_text(text)
    print(f"filled {name}")
PY
chmod 600 "$P/fill-indexer-c.py"
python3 -I "$P/fill-indexer-c.py" || true
printf '%s\n' __INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE__ __INDEXER_C_MEMBER_VOLUME_SIZE__ __SHA256_SI_SNODE__ > "$P/fill-smoke.txt"
python3 -I "$P/fill-indexer-c.py" "$P/placement.env" "$HASHES" "$P/fill-smoke.txt" && cat "$P/fill-smoke.txt" && rm "$P/fill-smoke.txt"
```

```python
def source_clickhouse(path):
    """A source installation's cluster Service {chi}-{cluster}, port 9000."""
    chi = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
    (cluster,) = chi["spec"]["configuration"]["clusters"]
    return f'{chi["metadata"]["name"]}-{cluster["name"]}:9000'


def indexer_b_source_clickhouse():
    """indexer-b's own source ClickHouse: the cluster Service {chi}-{cluster}."""
    return source_clickhouse(INDEXER_B_CHI)


def source_profile(chi):
    """What every SI source installation shares with the network installation:
    Keeper, settings, files, users by role, profiles, defaults and templates,
    with indexer-c's member disk (zz-si-storage.xml, its volume claim and its
    mount) left out."""
    spec = copy.deepcopy(chi["spec"])
    configuration = spec["configuration"]
    templates = spec["templates"]
    for pod in templates["podTemplates"]:
        for container in pod["spec"]["containers"]:
            container["volumeMounts"] = [
                mount for mount in container.get("volumeMounts", []) if mount["name"] != MEMBER_VOLUME_CLAIM
            ]
    templates["volumeClaimTemplates"] = [
        claim for claim in templates["volumeClaimTemplates"] if claim["name"] != MEMBER_VOLUME_CLAIM
    ]
    return {
        "zookeeper": configuration["zookeeper"],
        "settings": configuration["settings"],
        "files": {name: text for name, text in configuration["files"].items() if name != MEMBER_STORAGE_FILE},
        "users": clickhouse_users_by_role(configuration["users"]),
        "profiles": configuration["profiles"],
        "defaults": spec["defaults"],
        "templates": templates,
    }


def posture_comment(path):
    """The comment block right above a source installation's users: key."""
    lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
    end = lines.index("    users:")
    start = end
    while start > 0 and lines[start - 1].startswith("    #"):
        start -= 1
    return lines[start:end]
```

    def test_indexer_b_source_clickhouse_carries_the_network_source_profile(self):
        for path in (INDEXER_B_CHI, INDEXER_C_CHI):
            with self.subTest(installation=path.name):
                chi = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
                self.assertEqual((chi["kind"], chi["metadata"]["namespace"]), ("ClickHouseInstallation", LEGACY_NAMESPACE))
                self.assertNotIn(chi["metadata"]["name"], {FRESH_RELEASE, "storage-integrity", "clickhouse-devnet2"})
                # Not part of the network's Helm release, so no selector of it matches these pods.
                self.assertNotIn("app.kubernetes.io/instance", chi["metadata"].get("labels") or {})
                configuration = chi["spec"]["configuration"]
                # Keeper: the network's ensemble, timeouts and root (spec §8).
                self.assertEqual(configuration["zookeeper"]["root"], "/storage-integrity/devnet2/devnet2-si-v2")
                self.assertEqual(configuration["clusters"], [{"name": "source", "layout": {"shardsCount": 1, "replicasCount": 1}}])
                # The network installation's Keeper, server build, settings,
                # files, users, profiles, defaults and templates: the verifier
                # replicas fetch from it. Users and posture C's users.d file move
                # one installation at a time (lockdown runbook §6, §9), so the
                # network chart is rendered at this installation's own posture,
                # file for file, and users compare by role (hashes aside, and
                # si_verifier, which only the network installation has).
                # indexer-c's member disk and node pin are checked by
                # test_indexer_c_source_clickhouse_carries_the_network_source_profile_and_a_member_disk.
                network = source_profile(self.network_at_posture(DEVNET2_CLICKHOUSE_POSTURE[chi["metadata"]["name"]]))
                profile = source_profile(chi)
                if path == INDEXER_C_CHI:
                    (pod,) = profile["templates"]["podTemplates"]
                    pod["spec"]["nodeSelector"] = network["templates"]["podTemplates"][0]["spec"]["nodeSelector"]
                else:
                    # The existing installations keep their disks (Plan S3-B K21).
                    self.assertNotIn(MEMBER_STORAGE_FILE, configuration["files"])
                    self.assertNotIn(MEMBER_VOLUME_CLAIM, [claim["name"] for claim in chi["spec"]["templates"]["volumeClaimTemplates"]])
                for key in network:
                    self.assertEqual(profile[key], network[key], key)
                replica = next(
                    template for template in chi["spec"]["templates"]["serviceTemplates"]
                    if template["name"] == chi["spec"]["defaults"]["templates"]["replicaServiceTemplate"]
                )
                self.assertIn({"name": "interserver", "port": 9009}, replica["spec"]["ports"])

    def test_indexer_c_source_clickhouse_carries_the_network_source_profile_and_a_member_disk(self):
        chi = yaml.safe_load(INDEXER_C_CHI.read_text())
        self.assertEqual(
            (chi["kind"], chi["metadata"]["namespace"], chi["metadata"]["name"]),
            ("ClickHouseInstallation", LEGACY_NAMESPACE, "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c"),
        )
        # Not part of the network's Helm release, so no selector of it matches these pods.
        self.assertNotIn("app.kubernetes.io/instance", chi["metadata"].get("labels") or {})
        configuration = chi["spec"]["configuration"]
        self.assertEqual(configuration["clusters"], [{"name": "source", "layout": {"shardsCount": 1, "replicasCount": 1}}])
        self.assertEqual(source_clickhouse(INDEXER_C_CHI), "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source:9000")
        # Born in posture C (Plan S3-B K20): the indexer user set with its grants,
        # default locked by contract §11's one users.d file, this installation's
        # own hashes, and indexer-b's posture comment in indexer-c's name while
        # indexer-b is in the same posture (contract §11): that comment names its
        # own installation's clients (indexer-b's SNode, indexer-b's HouseGate),
        # so each "indexer-b" of it reads "indexer-c" here and nothing else differs.
        self.assertEqual(DEVNET2_CLICKHOUSE_POSTURE["storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c"], "C")
        self.assertEqual(configuration["files"][SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_FILE], SI_DEFAULT_LOOPBACK_XML)
        self.assertNotEqual(posture_comment(INDEXER_C_CHI), [])
        self.assertNotIn("indexer-b", "\n".join(posture_comment(INDEXER_C_CHI)))
        if DEVNET2_CLICKHOUSE_POSTURE["storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b"] == "C":
            self.assertEqual(
                posture_comment(INDEXER_C_CHI),
                [line.replace("indexer-b", "indexer-c") for line in posture_comment(INDEXER_B_CHI)],
            )
        hashes = {key: value for key, value in configuration["users"].items() if key.endswith("/password_sha256_hex")}
        self.assertEqual(sorted(hashes), [f"{user}/password_sha256_hex" for user in ("default", "si_gateway", "si_reader", "si_snode")])
        for key, value in hashes.items():
            self.assertRegex(value, r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$", key)
        self.assertEqual(len(set(hashes.values())), len(hashes), "one password per user")
        # One password per user and installation: no other devnet2 file carries
        # any of these hashes.
        others = "\n".join(path.read_text() for path in sorted(DEVNET2.rglob("*.yaml")) if path != INDEXER_C_CHI)
        for key, value in hashes.items():
            self.assertNotIn(value, others, key)
        # The member disk: one more volume claim, mounted by ClickHouse at the
        # member disk's path ...
        (pod,) = chi["spec"]["templates"]["podTemplates"]
        (container,) = pod["spec"]["containers"]
        self.assertIn({"name": MEMBER_VOLUME_CLAIM, "mountPath": MEMBER_DISK_PATH}, container["volumeMounts"])
        (claim,) = [claim for claim in chi["spec"]["templates"]["volumeClaimTemplates"] if claim["name"] == MEMBER_VOLUME_CLAIM]
        self.assertEqual((claim["spec"]["accessModes"], claim["spec"]["storageClassName"]), (["ReadWriteOnce"], "local-path"))
        self.assertRegex(claim["spec"]["resources"]["requests"]["storage"], r"^[1-9][0-9]*Gi$")
        # ... and zz-si-storage.xml: disk member at that path, policy member on
        # it alone, and one keep_free_space_bytes of at least 10 GiB on both the
        # default and the member disk (spec §8.1; Plan S3-B K21).
        storage = ElementTree.fromstring(configuration["files"][MEMBER_STORAGE_FILE]).find("storage_configuration")
        disks = {disk.tag: disk for disk in storage.find("disks")}
        self.assertEqual(sorted(disks), ["default", "member"])
        self.assertEqual([child.tag for child in disks["default"]], ["keep_free_space_bytes"])
        self.assertEqual((disks["member"].findtext("type"), disks["member"].findtext("path")), ("local", MEMBER_DISK_PATH))
        keep = {name: disk.findtext("keep_free_space_bytes") for name, disk in disks.items()}
        self.assertRegex(keep["default"], r"^[1-9][0-9]*$")
        self.assertEqual(keep["member"], keep["default"])
        self.assertGreaterEqual(int(keep["default"]), 10 * 1024**3)
        policies = storage.find("policies")
        self.assertEqual([policy.tag for policy in policies], ["member"])
        self.assertEqual([disk.text for disk in policies.find("member").iter("disk")], ["member"])
        # Everything else is the network installation's source profile at
        # posture C; the pod is pinned to its node instead of the network's
        # general-node selector.
        network = source_profile(self.network_at_posture("C"))
        profile = source_profile(chi)
        (profile_pod,) = profile["templates"]["podTemplates"]
        self.assertEqual(profile_pod["spec"]["nodeSelector"], {"kubernetes.io/hostname": INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE})
        profile_pod["spec"]["nodeSelector"] = network["templates"]["podTemplates"][0]["spec"]["nodeSelector"]
        for key in network:
            self.assertEqual(profile[key], network[key], key)

- [ ] **Step 5: indexer-c's source ClickHouse**

Create `k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source.yaml` (indexer-b's posture-C manifest, renamed, pinned to its node and given the member disk):

```yaml
# Source ClickHouse of devnet2 indexer-c, the third SI indexer of the
# devnet2-si-v2 storage-integrity network (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16 E;
# docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c.md §4). Not Helm-managed:
# apply it with kubectl, never with helmfile. Like indexer-b's
# (storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source.yaml), this installation is
# indexer-c's own, so no two SNodes ever write one ClickHouse.
#
# The source profile of the network installation, mirrored from indexer-b's
# installation (test_render.py compares both with charts/storage-integrity's
# installation by role):
# - Keeper: the network's clickhouse-keeper-extra ensemble under the network
#   root /storage-integrity/devnet2/devnet2-si-v2, which already exists.
#   indexer-c's SNode replicates its hg_unsafe tables at
#   /sentio/0/unsafe/<db>__<table> below it, with replica name snode-3.
# - Interserver: the operator advertises the replica Service
#   storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source-replica-0 as interserver_http_host
#   and the Service exposes 9009, so the verifier ClickHouses in this namespace
#   fetch indexer-c's parts from it.
# - hg_safe / hg_unsafe / hg_promote: indexer-c's SNode creates them with the
#   DDL-pinned settings; nothing here pre-creates them.
# - Born locked: posture C of docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md
#   from creation, with this installation's own passwords. Git carries only
#   their SHA-256 hashes; each plaintext lives only in a Secret made by
#   scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh indexer-c.
#
# Unlike the other two source installations, this one is born with the member
# disk of housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.1, which stage 3 P2 fills with member
# copies: the volume member-volume-claim mounted at /var/lib/clickhouse-member/,
# disk member and storage policy member in zz-si-storage.xml, and
# keep_free_space_bytes on both the default and the member disk, so ClickHouse
# refuses inserts, merges and fetches before the node SSD fills. Both volumes
# are local-path directories on the same node SSD (devnet2 has no
# capacity-enforcing storage class): a recorded deviation from §8.1, bounded by
# keep_free_space_bytes (Plan S3-B K21). A files or zookeeper change restarts
# this ClickHouse, so both are part of the installation from its creation.
#
# The pod is pinned to __INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE__, which runs neither the network
# installation's source or verifiers, nor indexer-b's source, nor indexer-a's or
# indexer-b's host (test_render.py DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES; Plan S3-B Task 19
# Step 1 records the placement).
apiVersion: clickhouse.altinity.com/v1
kind: ClickHouseInstallation
metadata:
  name: storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c
  namespace: sentio-network-devnet2
spec:
  defaults:
    templates:
      podTemplate: clickhouse
      dataVolumeClaimTemplate: data-volume-claim
      logVolumeClaimTemplate: log-volume-claim
      clusterServiceTemplate: cluster-service
      replicaServiceTemplate: replica-service
    storageManagement:
      reclaimPolicy: Retain
  configuration:
    zookeeper:
      nodes:
        - host: clickhouse-keeper-extra-0.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local
          port: 2181
        - host: clickhouse-keeper-extra-1.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local
          port: 2181
        - host: clickhouse-keeper-extra-2.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local
          port: 2181
      session_timeout_ms: 100000
      operation_timeout_ms: 10000
      root: /storage-integrity/devnet2/devnet2-si-v2
    clusters:
      - name: source
        layout: {shardsCount: 1, replicasCount: 1}
    settings:
      logger/level: warning
      logger/console: "true"
      prometheus/endpoint: /metrics
      prometheus/port: 9363
      prometheus/metrics: true
      prometheus/events: true
      prometheus/asynchronous_metrics: true
      prometheus/status_info: true
      max_concurrent_queries: 500
      max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio: "0.85"
    files:
      zz-pool-settings.xml: |
        <clickhouse>
          <background_pool_size>16</background_pool_size>
          <background_fetches_pool_size>8</background_fetches_pool_size>
        </clickhouse>
      users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml: |
        <clickhouse><users><default><networks replace="replace"><ip>::1</ip><ip>127.0.0.1</ip></networks><access_management>0</access_management></default></users></clickhouse>
      # The member disk (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.1). keep_free_space_bytes
      # (__INDEXER_C_KEEP_FREE_SPACE_BYTES__ bytes, Plan S3-B Task 19 Step 1) is
      # the same on both disks because both are directories of one node SSD;
      # every table stays on the default policy unless it names policy member.
      zz-si-storage.xml: |
        <clickhouse>
          <storage_configuration>
            <disks>
              <default>
                <keep_free_space_bytes>__INDEXER_C_KEEP_FREE_SPACE_BYTES__</keep_free_space_bytes>
              </default>
              <member>
                <type>local</type>
                <path>/var/lib/clickhouse-member/</path>
                <keep_free_space_bytes>__INDEXER_C_KEEP_FREE_SPACE_BYTES__</keep_free_space_bytes>
              </member>
            </disks>
            <policies>
              <member>
                <volumes>
                  <main>
                    <disk>member</disk>
                  </main>
                </volumes>
              </member>
            </policies>
          </storage_configuration>
        </clickhouse>
    # Devnet posture since the stage-3 ClickHouse lockdown
    # (docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md): default has a
    # password and accepts loopback connections only (networks/ip, plus
    # users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml, which replaces the pod addresses and
    # the host regexp the operator merges in and also removes access
    # management, which the image's users.xml grants); it is the
    # administrators' user, reached through kubectl exec. Each protocol
    # client has its own user with exactly its grants (test_render.py
    # SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS): si_snode, indexer-c's SNode (hg_unsafe, hg_safe
    # and hg_promote, SYSTEM MERGES on hg_unsafe and hg_safe, SYSTEM DROP
    # REPLICA, and the system tables it reads); si_gateway, indexer-c's
    # HouseGate upstream and schema declarer (the tenant database devnet2,
    # SELECT only on hg_safe and hg_unsafe, READ ON REMOTE without WRITE,
    # nothing on hg_promote, hg_member_unsafe, hg_replica, hg_rstage or
    # hg_xfer, no SYSTEM and no access management); si_reader, member pulls
    # from stage 3 P2 on (SELECT on hg_safe and hg_unsafe and seven columns of
    # system.parts). Still open until stage 3 P4: interserver HTTP (9009) has
    # no credentials, the shared Keeper ensemble has no ACL, and the namespace
    # has no NetworkPolicy; that policy must admit 9000/8123 from the host pod
    # and, for members, 9000 from the peer source ClickHouses, and 9009 from
    # the verifier ClickHouses and the peer source ClickHouses (housegate spec
    # 2026-10-14 §14). Users are installation-wide; test_render.py keeps them
    # equal to the network installation's by role.
    users:
      default/password_sha256_hex: "__SHA256_DEFAULT__"
      default/networks/ip:
        - 127.0.0.1
        - "::1"
      si_snode/password_sha256_hex: "__SHA256_SI_SNODE__"
      si_snode/networks/ip:
        - "::/0"
      si_snode/profile: default
      si_snode/grants/query:
        - "GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON hg_unsafe.*"
        - "GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON hg_safe.*"
        - "GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON hg_promote.*"
        - "GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER DELETE, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE ON hg_unsafe.*"
        - "GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER DELETE, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE ON hg_safe.*"
        - "GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER DELETE, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE ON hg_promote.*"
        - "GRANT SYSTEM MERGES ON hg_unsafe.*"
        - "GRANT SYSTEM MERGES ON hg_safe.*"
        - "GRANT SYSTEM DROP REPLICA ON *.*"
        - "GRANT SELECT ON system.parts"
        - "GRANT SELECT ON system.detached_tables"
        - "GRANT SELECT ON system.replicas"
        - "GRANT SELECT ON system.zookeeper"
        - "GRANT SELECT ON system.merges"
      si_gateway/password_sha256_hex: "__SHA256_SI_GATEWAY__"
      si_gateway/networks/ip:
        - "::/0"
      si_gateway/profile: default
      si_gateway/grants/query:
        - "GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER, CREATE TABLE, CREATE VIEW, DROP TABLE, DROP VIEW, TRUNCATE, OPTIMIZE ON devnet2.*"
        - "GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON devnet2.*"
        - "GRANT SELECT ON hg_safe.*"
        - "GRANT SELECT ON hg_unsafe.*"
        - "GRANT READ ON REMOTE"
        - "GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.*"
        - "GRANT SELECT ON system.processes"
      si_reader/password_sha256_hex: "__SHA256_SI_READER__"
      si_reader/networks/ip:
        - "::/0"
      si_reader/profile: default
      si_reader/grants/query:
        - "GRANT SELECT ON hg_safe.*"
        - "GRANT SELECT ON hg_unsafe.*"
        - "GRANT SELECT(database, table, name, active, rows, partition_id, hash_of_all_files) ON system.parts"
    profiles:
      default/query_cache_nondeterministic_function_handling: ignore
      default/enable_json_type: "1"
  templates:
    podTemplates:
      - name: clickhouse
        generateName: "{chi}-{cluster}-{host}"
        podDistribution:
          - type: ClusterAffinity
        metadata:
          annotations:
            prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
            prometheus.io/path: /metrics
            prometheus.io/port: "9363"
        spec:
          automountServiceAccountToken: false
          nodeSelector:
            kubernetes.io/hostname: __INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE__
          imagePullSecrets:
            - name: google-image-secret
          containers:
            - name: clickhouse
              image: us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/sentio-352722/sentio/clickhouse-server:26.3-lts-decimal512-release-2026-09-16
              ports:
                - name: metrics
                  containerPort: 9363
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data-volume-claim
                  mountPath: /var/lib/clickhouse
                # The operator adds every volume claim template a container
                # mounts to the StatefulSet.
                - name: member-volume-claim
                  mountPath: /var/lib/clickhouse-member/
              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: "2"
                  memory: 4Gi
                limits:
                  cpu: "8"
                  memory: 16Gi
    volumeClaimTemplates:
      - name: data-volume-claim
        spec:
          accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
          storageClassName: local-path
          resources:
            requests:
              storage: 10Gi
      - name: log-volume-claim
        spec:
          accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
          storageClassName: local-path
          resources:
            requests:
              storage: 1Gi
      # local-path enforces no size: the request is bookkeeping, the bound is
      # keep_free_space_bytes in zz-si-storage.xml.
      - name: member-volume-claim
        spec:
          accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
          storageClassName: local-path
          resources:
            requests:
              storage: __INDEXER_C_MEMBER_VOLUME_SIZE__
    serviceTemplates:
      - name: cluster-service
        generateName: "{chi}-{cluster}"
        spec:
          ports:
            - {name: http, port: 8123}
            - {name: tcp, port: 9000}
          type: ClusterIP
      - name: replica-service
        generateName: "{chi}-{cluster}-replica-{replica}"
        spec:
          ports:
            - {name: http, port: 8123}
            - {name: tcp, port: 9000}
            - {name: interserver, port: 9009}
          type: ClusterIP

The posture comment above `users:` is the text of Task 18 Step 15 (decision D11) in indexer-c's name: indexer-b's text on the branch base with each `indexer-b` replaced by `indexer-c`, because that text names its own installation's clients (`si_snode, indexer-b's SNode`, `si_gateway, indexer-b's HouseGate upstream`), and nothing else changed (contract §11; the test compares the two with the name substituted, and refuses `indexer-b` in indexer-c's comment). The block below writes indexer-b's lines, renamed, over it, so a wording that changed after this plan was drafted is taken as it is on `main`; then it fills the recorded inputs and runs the tests:

```bash
cd "$W" && python3 -I - k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source.yaml k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source.yaml <<'PY'
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def comment(lines):
    end = lines.index("    users:")
    start = end
    while start > 0 and lines[start - 1].startswith("    #"):
        start -= 1
    return start, end


indexer_b, indexer_c = (Path(path) for path in sys.argv[1:3])
b_lines, c_lines = indexer_b.read_text().splitlines(), indexer_c.read_text().splitlines()
(b_start, b_end), (c_start, c_end) = comment(b_lines), comment(c_lines)
if b_end - b_start < 10 or not any("loopback" in line for line in b_lines[b_start:b_end]):
    sys.exit(f"{indexer_b.name} has no posture C comment above users: (Task 18 Step 15): stop")
if any("indexer-c" in line for line in b_lines[b_start:b_end]):
    sys.exit(f"{indexer_b.name}'s posture comment names indexer-c: renaming it for indexer-c would be ambiguous; stop")
# indexer-b's comment names its own installation's clients (indexer-b's SNode,
# indexer-b's HouseGate): indexer-c's copy names indexer-c there (contract §11).
own = [line.replace("indexer-b", "indexer-c") for line in b_lines[b_start:b_end]]
if own == c_lines[c_start:c_end]:
    print(f"posture comment: {indexer_b.name}'s in indexer-c's name, as drafted ({b_end - b_start} lines)")
else:
    c_lines[c_start:c_end] = own
    indexer_c.write_text("\n".join(c_lines) + "\n")
    print(f"posture comment: copied from {indexer_b.name} in indexer-c's name ({b_end - b_start} lines)")
PY

```python
def yaml_strings(value):
    """Every key and string value of a parsed YAML document."""
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for key, item in value.items():
            yield str(key)
            yield from yaml_strings(item)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for item in value:
            yield from yaml_strings(item)
    elif isinstance(value, str):
        yield value


def local_path_directories():
    """The local-path StorageClass's directories by node (ConfigMap local-path-config)."""
    config_map = next(
        doc for doc in yaml.safe_load_all(LOCAL_PATH_STORAGE.read_text())
        if doc and doc.get("kind") == "ConfigMap" and doc["metadata"]["name"] == "local-path-config"
    )
    config = json.loads(config_map["data"]["config.json"])
    return {entry["node"]: entry["paths"] for entry in config["storageClassConfigs"]["local-path"]["nodePathMap"]}
```
